jobs.description:
Create your own happiness!

Are you a passionate early childhood educator (m/f/d)? Do you put your heart and soul into your work, but haven’t been satisfied with your working conditions so far?

Come check us out—maybe you’ll like what you find here?

What you can look forward to…

The basics: pay, vacation time, and working hours.

We are actually offering a fixed-term full-time position, but a reduction in hours is possible. The full-time workweek is 38 hours. Initially, the contract would be fixed-term due to parental leave, but an extension is possible.

Pay is based on the TVöD SuE collective bargaining agreement and depends on your professional experience and qualifications. A 13th month’s salary (at 100%, instead of 85%) is paid after one year of service. We have between 32 and 34 days of vacation per year. Christmas Eve and New Year’s Eve are paid holidays. The cost of an HVV/Deutschlandticket is fully covered, and if interested, you can participate in a fitness program.

The Position: Responsibilities and Working Conditions.

We are looking for at least one new early childhood educator with a perfect command of the English language.

Your responsibilities include the attentive care, nurturing, and support of the infants entrusted to us in accordance with our educational philosophy, working closely with the children, parents, and the entire team. Your would spend your daily life spekaing English.

You would be a permanent member of the nursery team. Some experience in this field and a preference for this age group would be advantageous.

Our working conditions are truly worth highlighting: In the elementary section, four colleagues together care for 35 children; in the nursery section, four additional colleagues care for 16 children. In addition, we employ a housekeeping staff member with educational qualifications and, in the future, a substitute.

We hold weekly team meetings to discuss weekly schedules, activities, and specific situations, as well as to plan parent-teacher conferences and developmental meetings. Our sponsoring organization places great emphasis on providing good working conditions.

The Team: One for all, all for one!

Some of us have been working together successfully and happily for over ten years. It goes without saying that we support one another and treat each other with care. Our sense of humor and our willingness to stand up for one another carry us through the sometimes hectic daily routine of the daycare center.

On concept days, we discuss educational topics, engage in professional development, and reflect on our work. Regular weekly team meetings, preparation time, and supervision are just as much a part of our routine as extended get-togethers during company outings and Christmas parties.

Has this piqued your curiosity? Then be sure to read on…

Important: Empathy, joy, and qualifications.

To ensure we comply with legal requirements, it is very important that our new team member holds a completed, state-recognized qualification as an early childhood educator (m/f/d), a degree in early childhood education or early childhood development, or a degree as a social pedagogue (m/f/d). It would be helpful if you have a good understanding of the English language, as we are a bilingual facility.

We are looking for an empathetic person with a Reggio Emilia approach (including a child-centered perspective) and someone who genuinely enjoys working with children, because we want you to look forward to coming to work.

Feel free to get to know us!

The Daycare Center: Location. Concept. Focus Areas.

The daycare center is located in the heart of Planten un Blomen and is surrounded by plenty of greenery. It is easily accessible by public transportation from all parts of Hamburg (Gänsemarkt, Dammtor, Stephansplatz).

There are two groups, a nursery group and an elementary group, in which 46 children are currently cared for by eight early childhood educators. Our facilities allow us to organize various projects and activities in workshops and specialized rooms.

The foundation of our concept is the Reggio approach. Above all, it reflects our attitude toward others and how we wish to approach life’s changes. Our daycare is a place for self-directed, holistic learning, and we foster a respectful approach not only toward the children entrusted to us, but toward all people.

We integrate key areas such as yoga, woodworking, art studio work, language development, music, relaxation and movement, and preschool preparation into our daily routine. Do you have a particular focus? A passion? Let’s find out together if we can integrate this into our daily routine as well…

Start up initiative: Kindertagesstätte an der Bucerius Law School e.V.

Our small operator, “Kindertagesstätte an der Bucerius Law School e.V.”, was founded in 2008 and is a member of the Paritätischer Wohlfahrtsverband Hamburg. Loki Schmidt was the founding patron of our daycare center.

Our organization consists of a single facility. This means that decisions can be made and implemented quickly, easily, and on an individual basis. Here, people are still allowed to be people; they are heard and are not just a personnel number.

As a member of the Bucerius family and an initiative of the ZEIT STIFTUNG BUCERIUS, our work makes an important contribution to promoting an open, democratic society.

The Future: Do you think we’re a good fit for you?

Then please send us your application materials. We would love to get to know you.

If you’re interested, feel free to check out our website (https://www.law-school.de/services/kita (https://www.law-school.de/services/kita) ) or our Instagram account (kita.buceriuslaw).

Thank you for your attention, and we hope to see you soon!

...you're in the middle of it

The Institute of Clinical Pharmacology at Goethe University Frankfurt is seeking a PhD Candidate / Doctoral Researcher to join the research group of Dr. Hahnefeld. The successful candidate will contribute to an interdisciplinary research project in cooperation with the Fraunhofer ITMP Frankfurt at the interface of analytical chemistry, lipid biology and inflammation research.

The project investigates how lipid metabolism and lipid-mediated signaling are regulated in inflammatory settings. The work combines cell-based experiments with mass spectrometry-based lipidomics, fatty acid analysis and targeted lipid mediator measurements. A particular focus will be placed on the development, optimization and application of robust analytical and computational workflows for the analysis of complex biological datasets. The research group uses high-resolution mass spectrometry and reproducible bioinformatic approaches to investigate lipid-mediated mechanisms in inflammatory and metabolic diseases. The position offers the opportunity to work in a collaborative research environment with interdisciplinary partners in lipid biology, immunology, imaging and proteomics.

The position is limited up to three years.

Your Role:

- Plan, conduct and document experiments in cellular models of inflammation and metabolic perturbation.
- Prepare biological samples and perform LC-HRMS-based lipidomics and metabolomics measurements and further develop associated analytical workflows.
- Perform GC-HRMS-based analysis of fatty acids
- Conduct LC-MS/MS measurements of lipid mediators using established methods.
- Perform comprehensive quality control, raw-data validation, data annotation and statistical analysis of complex mass spectrometry datasets.
- Develop and apply reproducible workflows for data processing, visualization and interpretation using R and/or Python.
- Contribute to the integration and interpretation of lipidomics data with complementary datasets generated by collaborating groups, including imaging- and proteomics-based data.
- Validate selected findings in close collaboration with project partners.
- Present research results in scientific publications, project meetings and at national and international conferences.

... your skills are what we're looking for

Die Medizinische Hochschule Hannover (MHH), mit rund 10.000 Beschäftigten größter Landesbetrieb des Landes Niedersachsen, ist eine universitäre Einrichtung für Forschung und Lehre in der Human- und Zahnmedizin und ein Universitätsklinikum der Supramaximalversorgung. Forschung, Lehre, Krankenversorgung und Administration arbeiten im Integrationsmodell auf dem MHH-Campus Hand in Hand.
About Us

The Hannover Medical School (MHH), with about 10,000 employees the biggest company of Lower Saxony, is a university institution for research and teaching in the human and dental medicine and a university hospital of supra-maximum medical care. Research, teaching, medical care and administration work hand in hand in the integration model at the MHH-campus.

The Peter L. Reichertz Institute for Medical Informatics (PLRI) is one of the largest university centres for medical informatics in Germany. It belongs to two leading universities, is situated in one of Europe's most research-intensive regions, and offers excellent opportunities for research. In interdisciplinary projects, the PLRI collaborates with health centres, research institutes, corporations, and public institutions in order to shape the future of the health system and medicine. The activities range from diverse topics on the local level, to regional, national, and global collaborations.

The research group "Clinical Data Science" focuses on the detection of novel routine clinical and -omics biomarkers for disease diagnosis and prognosis to personalize and thus improve patient treatment. To achieve this, we integrate phenotypical information and routine clinical as well as (multi)-omics data by high-dimensional statistics and state-of-the-art artificial intelligence to gain novel insights into underlying disease pathomechanisms. Moreover, we are interested in developing and implementing research data platforms for complex (multi-)omics data. The project "MALDIDive: Enabling AI Research with Public MALDI-TOF Fingerprints across Microbial Diversity", to be carried out within an interdisciplinary research team and funded by the German Research Foundation, will establish a well curated data platform of MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry datasets from the Leibniz Institute German Collection of Mircoorganisms and Cell Cultures GmbH (DSMZ). We are looking for an enthusiastic PostDoc who is interested in omics data platform development and deployment for future AI use.

Your Responsibilities

- data platform architecture, backend, and frontend development as well as deployment for MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry database/platform and associated metadata
- development of interactive data visualization concepts and their implementation into data platform
- development and realization of short explanatory videos for platform users
- co-organization and co-leading of stakeholder workshops to define user requirements and conduct user test cycles
- presentation to the scientific community, i.e., by publishing in high-level journals and via presentations at international conferences
- close collaboration with interdisciplinary project partners from AI / data science, analytical, and micro­biological research communities, particularly the DSMZ
- bachelor / master student co-supervision

Your Profile

- PhD / Dr. rer. nat. / Dr.-Ing. degree in data science / bioinformatics / computational biology / informatics / physics or similar research fields

- proficiency in backend / frontend development and / or database programming, including one or more of the following programming languages: VueJS, TypeScript, SQL, PYTHON, R Shiny, nginx, Docker, etc.
- proficiency in English (written and oral)
- desired: experience with code documentary systems and RestAPI
- desired: knowledge of the German language

jobs.description:
Full-Stack Software Developer (m/f/d): TETTRIX project

Senckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position in the Senckenberg Data and Modelling Center (SDMC) at the Senckenberg Research Institute and Natural History Museum Frankfurt, starting as soon as possible:

Full-Stack Software Developer (m/f/d): TETTRIX project

(Full-Time / Part-Time)

Location: Frankfurt
Employment scope: Full-Time / Part-Time options are available
Type of contract: Temporary, initially limited to 2 years
Remuneration: Collective agreement of the state Hesse (TV-H) / E11- E13

The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.

The city of Frankfurt, where the Senckenberg Society was originally founded, hosts the organization’s central administrative services along with two research institutes housing extensive scientific collections and one of Senckenberg’s most renowned institutions, the Senckenberg Natural History Museum Frankfurt. Senckenberg is as much a part of the city’s identity as its skyline and its traditional apple wine.

The position is within the Geobiodiversity Information and Data Management team of the Senckenberg Data and Modelling Centre and contributes to a project funded by the European Union, TETTRIX – TETTRIs neXt level for the taxonomy of tomorrow. The team works at the interface of biodiversity informatics, ecological modelling, and data management, focusing on integrating, analysing, and making biodiversity data accessible for research and conservation. The TETTRIX project aims to strengthen taxonomic capacity for biodiversity research by developing, validating, and scaling innovative tools, workflows, services, and training pathways, while addressing critical knowledge and capacity gaps across Europe. Within the TETTRIX project, the position will develop a web-based, open-access biodiversity mapping and Species Distribution Modelling (SDM) platform that enables reproducible data and modelling workflows and transforms biodiversity data into actionable knowledge for biodiversity monitoring and conservation. The role combines full-stack software development with biodiversity data integration and close collaboration with researchers and technical partners.

Your tasks

- Develop the platform's web application end-to-end: SPA frontend (interactive map, species/variable selection, model-run monitoring) and REST API backend.
- Integrate the application with the PostgreSQL/PostGIS metadata layer and the AWS-side batch and data-lake services.
- Co-design and implement the data infrastructure of the Open Modular SDM Platform, including a columnar lakehouse (Parquet, DuckDB, Dask on AWS Batch) covering the full GBIF and OBIS datasets.
- Develop and operate the hybrid infrastructure, integrating AWS-based services with the institute's internal serving layer (PostgreSQL/PostGIS, map tiles and APIs), and coordinate the associated technical tasks.
- Implement map-tile serving, caching and optimise frontend performance.
- Set up and maintain CI/CD, automated tests and containerised deployment (Docker) in cooperation with central IT.
- Participate in project and team meetings and coordinate closely with the scientific team on a day-to-day basis.

Your profile

- Degree in Computer Science or comparable practical experience.
- Solid skills in TypeScript/JavaScript and a modern framework (React, Vue or similar).
- Backend experience in Python (e.g. FastAPI/Flask) or Node.js; sound REST API design.
- Experience with SQL/PostgreSQL; PostGIS and web-mapping libraries (MapLibre GL, Leaflet, OpenLayers) are a strong plus.
- Experience with cloud-based data infrastructure, particularly AWS services (S3, Batch).
- Knowledge of columnar data storage and lakehouse technologies (Parquet, DuckDB, Dask).
- Experience with data pipelines, batch processing and the integration of large-scale datasets.
- Knowledge of hybrid infrastructure architectures and the integration of cloud-based and on-premises services.
- Experience with Docker, Git and CI/CD.
- Very good command of English.
- Willingness to work on site in Frankfurt (up to 40% remote work is possible).

Desirable skills

- Familiarity with open-access biodiversity databases such as the Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF) and the Ocean Biodiversity Information System (OBIS), Darwin Core standards, and biodiversity data life cycles
- Familiarity with species distribution modelling and associated statistical/machine-learning approaches (e.g. GLM/GAM, MaxEnt, Random Forest)
- A track record in scientific publications, reproducible scientific computing, or open-source projects

We offer

- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations
- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution
- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension plan

Senckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of ethnic or cultural origin, age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion or belief, age, sexual identity or and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.

How to apply?

Please upload your application (letter of motivation, CV, relevantcertificates and references, if available) electronically as a single PDF by 15. November2026.

Senckenberganlage 25
60325 Frankfurt am Main

jobs.description:
Senckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at its institute Senckenberg am Meer, German Centre for Marine Biodiversity Research in Hamburg, starting as soon as possible

Research Scientist and Project Coordinator (m/f/d) in the field of Zooplankton Biodiversity

(full time / part-time )

Location: Hamburg

Employment scope: full-time / part-time options available

Type of contract: temporary contract limited until 30.09.2029

Remuneration: collective agreement of the state Hesse, TV-H E13

﻿

The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.

As part of the institute “Senckenberg am Meer” located in Wilhelmshaven, with its two departments Marine Research and German Centre for Marine Biodiversity Research (DZMB), the Hamburg research site, which belongs to the DZMB, focuses on researching taxonomy and systematics of marine life forms.

The position is based within the Zooplankton Working Group and is part of the joint project ZooM-In (Innovative Methods for National Zooplankton Monitoring), contributing to the further development and standardization of modern methods for marine biodiversity monitoring. The project is funded by the Federal Ministry for the Environment, Climate Action, Nature Conservation and Nuclear Safety (BMUKN) through the National Biodiversity Monitoring Centre’s initiative Sustainable Biodiversity Monitoring.

The project will be carried out in close cooperation with the Helmholtz Institute for Functional Marine Biodiversity (HIFMB) as well as federal and state authorities.

Your tasks

- Project management of the project ZooM-In

The Max Planck Society is Germany's premier research organization. The 86 Max Planck Institutes conduct research at highest levels, in the service of the general public, in the natural sciences, life sciences, social sciences, and the humanities.

The Max Planck Institute for the Structure and Dynamics of Matter (MPSD) is located at the Science Campus Hamburg-Bahrenfeld and investigates dynamical phenomena within matter down to the elementary timescales of atomic and electronic motions, the femtosecond or attosecond timescale. The focus is on the use of short wavelength ultrafast probes, such as X-rays or electron pulses, which are capable of measuring atomic and electronic structures in matter of all kinds.

The MPSD currently consists of five scientific departments focusing on solid state physics and theoretical methods in these fields. The MPSD is a partner in the Center for Free-Electron Laser Science (CFEL), collaborating with the Deutsches Elektronen Synchrotron (DESY), European XFEL (EuXFEL) and the University of Hamburg in the development of science based on the X-ray Free Electron Lasers (XFELs).

To strengthen our support for experimental research, the MPSD is seeking a highly motivated

Electronics Engineer (m/f/d)

Your position

- Work closely with researchers and engineers to provide practical, user-oriented technical solutions for a broad range of experimental setups.
- Prepare and maintain technical documentation, including circuit diagrams, PCB layouts, assembly instructions and test procedures.
- As the role involves hands-on development, assembly, testing and support of laboratory equipment, regular on-site presence is an essential part of the position.

Your background and skills

- A university degree (Master’s degree or Diplom) in electrical engineering, electronics or a closely related field.
- Sound practical experience in the development of analogue and digital electronic systems, including circuit design, PCB layout and the assembly, commissioning and testing of electronic devices.
- Proficiency in common ECAD tools for schematic capture and PCB design, ideally including KiCad or Autodesk EAGLE, as well as familiarity with circuit-simulation tools.
- Knowledge of firmware development for microcontrollers, ideally using C/C++. Experience in developing user software for the control, operation and monitoring of electronic devices is also desirable.
- Experience with FPGA development and VHDL is an advantage. Familiarity with CAD systems for mechanical design is also desirable.
- A strong understanding of the requirements and working practices of a diverse scientific and technical environment, combined with intercultural competence and effective communication skills.
- Excellent written and spoken German and English skills.
- Experience in laboratory electronics, measurement technology, scientific instrumentation or experimental physics is desirable.

Our offer

- A varied and responsible position in an international and interdisciplinary scientific environment, with the opportunity to contribute directly to innovative experimental research.
- Close collaboration with scientists, engineers and technical staff on challenging and diverse technical projects.
- A family-friendly working environment with flexible working arrangements, in line with the practical requirements of laboratory-based work.

- An initial contract for two years, with the possibility of permanent employment thereafter.
- The opportunity to work in a collaborative, inclusive and forward-looking research environment.
- A subsidy for the Profiticket as a Germany ticket

Your application

The Max-Planck Society is committed to increasing the number of individuals with disabilities in its workforce and therefore encourages applications from such qualified individuals.

To apply please complete the online application form and attach you English CV and motivation letter as well as all relevant certificates latest 15th November, 2026.

Pricing will be one of your most important areas of responsibility. You will establish pricing as a strategic capability across SUSONITY by:

- Developing and implementing a global pricing strategy aligned with business objectives, customer value and market dynamics.
- Establishing pricing governance, principles, processes and approval frameworks across regions and businesses.
- Driving value-based pricing, price differentiation and improved price realization.
- Strengthening transparency and consistency in pricing decisions through robust data, analytics and performance management.
- Partnering closely with Sales, Marketing, Product Management, Finance and regional leadership to embed pricing excellence into day-to-day commercial decisions.
- Identifying opportunities to improve margins, commercial effectiveness and sustainable profitable growth.
- Enhancing the use of pricing software and digital tools to enable fact-based, timely and scalable pricing decisions.

Build and lead commercial excellence

Beyond pricing, you will lead the continued development of SUSONITY’s global commercial excellence platform:

- Define and implement a global commercial excellence strategy that improves sales force effectiveness and delivers measurable business impact.
- Optimize commercial infrastructure, including customer segmentation, lead management, opportunity tracking and campaign performance.
- Establish meaningful KPIs, dashboards and performance routines that turn data into actionable commercial insight.
- Drive the effective use and continuous improvement of Salesforce, pricing software and other commercial technologies.
- Develop standardized frameworks, processes and tools that create alignment while allowing for relevant regional flexibility.
- Strengthen launch excellence for new products and campaigns in close collaboration with Marketing, Product Management and regional teams.
- Support post-merger integration by helping build a unified, scalable and high-performing commercial operating model.

Lead people, influence globally and raise ambition

You will lead a team of tool and process experts while orchestrating a broad global network of stakeholders across Commercial, Sales, Marketing, Product Management, Finance and other functions. 

Your role will be to create clarity, build momentum and turn strategic priorities into practical execution. You will challenge established ways of working, build strong partnerships and ensure that commercial excellence becomes a shared capability across the organization.
 
What you bring

- A university degree in Business Administration, Commercial Management, Sales, Finance or a related discipline.
- Significant experience in commercial excellence, pricing, sales operations, commercial strategy or a comparable leadership function, ideally within a B2B or chemical industry environment.
- Demonstrated success in developing and implementing pricing strategies, pricing governance, value-based pricing or commercial performance initiatives.
- Strong understanding of the connection between pricing, customer value, sales effectiveness and profitable growth.
- Experience leading teams, cross-functional programs and global stakeholder networks.
- Strong command of CRM systems, preferably Salesforce, as well as pricing software and commercial analytics tools.
- Excellent analytical and conceptual capabilities, combined with the ability to translate insights into clear decisions and practical action.
- Proven project and change management skills, with the ability to lead complex initiatives in a fast-moving, international environment.
- Exceptional communication, influencing and negotiation skills, including the confidence to engage with senior stakeholders.
- A pragmatic, entrepreneurial and collaborative leadership style.
- Fluency in English; additional languages are an advantage.
 
Why join SUSONITY?

This is an opportunity to shape a function that is strategically critical to SUSONITY’s future.

You will have the mandate and visibility to build global pricing and commercial excellence capabilities from the ground up, influence how we go to market and help ensure that the value of our innovations is reflected in every commercial decision.

At SUSONITY, you will work in a culture that combines scientific expertise, creative exploration and entrepreneurial drive. We empower our people to take ownership, challenge conventions and create meaningful impact across markets and industries.

If you are ready to make pricing a true source of competitive advantage and to help build the commercial foundation of a fast-evolving global organization, we look forward to hearing from you.

Absen Optoelectronic Co., Ltd., founded in 2001, is a global leader in LED display manufacturing, renowned for its innovation, reliability, and customer-centric approach. With over 3,000 employees worldwide, we provide cutting-edge LED display solutions across diverse industries.

Absen GmbH, founded in 2013, is the German subsidiary of the Absen Group, headquartered in Mörfelden-Walldorf near Frankfurt am Main. It directly manages the European market, coordinating all sales, service, and logistics activities across Europe, working closely with customers and partners, and ensuring that Absen’s high-quality standards are consistently met.

Technical Service Engineer – European Region 

(full-time, m/f/d)

Location: Mörfelden-Walldorf, Germany (near Frankfurt am Main)

Reporting to: European Service Manager

Role Overview

We are looking for a Technical Service Engineer to join our local service team in Germany and work closely with the European service organization.

Reporting to the European Service Manager, you will receive comprehensive onboarding training and ongoing business guidance to help you quickly gain an understanding of our products, customer service processes, and internal systems, enabling you to successfully integrate into the team and take ownership of your responsibilities.

Responsibilities

- Provide technical consultation, troubleshooting and solution support to customers and partners via phone, email, instant messaging and remote diagnostic tools.
- Diagnose and resolve LED display hardware and software issues remotely and on-site. Prepare detailed fault analysis and service reports.
- Act as the technical point of contact for end customers, system integrators and channel partners across Europe, handling technical inquiries, service requests and escalations.
- Travel across Europe to customer sites as required to provide installation guidance, commissioning, maintenance and repair support, ensuring successful project acceptance and delivery.
- Provide technical training to customers and partners on product operation, routine maintenance, system commissioning, troubleshooting and LED module repair.
- Coordinate with internal teams to ensure timely resolution of customer issues and contribute to continuous improvements in service quality and customer satisfaction.

Qualification

- Technical education or vocational training in Electrical Engineering, Electronics, Telecommunications, or a related field; a bachelor’s degree or above is a plus.
- Relevant professional experience in technical service, field service, or a related technical role. Experience in the LED display or AV industry is a strong advantage.
- Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills.
- Fluent English required; German proficiency is a plus, with Chinese proficiency also considered an advantage.
- Strong customer-oriented mindset with excellent interpersonal and communication skills.
- Willingness to travel extensively across Europe, approximately 50%–70%, and ability to work independently on customer-facing on-site assignments.
- Detail-oriented, well-organized, and capable of working with a structured and systematic approach.

What We Offer

- A supportive, collaborative, and international working environment.
- A flat organizational structure with efficient and open communication.
- A competitive compensation package.
- Comprehensive onboarding and continuous professional development opportunities.
- 30 days of paid annual leave per year.
- Flexible working hours.
- Travel allowances and comprehensive support for business trips.
- Birthday and Christmas benefits.
- Free coffee and beverages in the office.
- Free parking.

Description

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.
Be a part of operating the world’s largest cloud computing infrastructure. Amazon Web Services is seeking bright, motivated, hardworking individuals to fill Senior Datacenter Logistics Specialist positions. The ideal candidate possesses a strong work ethic, attention to detail, the ability to meet deadlines, and a commitment to Operational Excellence.

The Senior Logistics Specialist reviews datacenter inventory, in-bound shipments, and ongoing demand to ensure that proper stock levels are maintained in all locations to support build and repair activities. Working with the Logistics Manager, they create plans to optimize the flow of parts through their lifecycle; tracking inventory location, movement, age, and turns. They work closely with Datacenter Operations Technicians and Datacenter Engineers to fulfill parts quickly and accurately. They work with Procurement and Hardware Engineering to purchase new parts and interface directly with vendors to process RMAs and receive replacements. They are responsible for accurate data entry and resolving questions from peer organizations.

The ideal Logistics Specialist will dive deep into data to understand everything about the datacenter asset lifecycle. Working with software development teams, they will contribute to continuous process improvements to deliver on our goals of high availability and low cost. They maintain up-to-date metrics dashboards and will create reports for internal and external suppliers and management as required.

Responsibilities include manual tasks, such as assembling, addressing, stamping and arranging for the shipment of merchandise and materials. They will also assist in daily scheduling of deliveries and pick-ups to and from production locations. In handling incoming shipments, they will have to unpack boxes and verify contents. The Logistic Specialist will be required to keep precise records of all commodities going in and out of company.

Logistics Specialist is expected to understand all aspects of production, adhere to strict safety standards, maintain very high levels of quality and be willing to travel to support other location within and outside the Country.

Key job responsibilities
Your main responsibilities as Senior Logistics Specialist include:
• You will support the Data Center Operations team by maintaining receiving, warehousing, and distribution operations of parts, consumables and other supplies by initiating, coordinating, and enforcing program, operational, and personnel policies and procedures.
• Comply with local warehousing, health and safety and shipping requirements by studying existing and new legislation; enforcing adherence to requirements; advising management on needed actions.
• Safeguard warehouse operations and contents by establishing and monitoring safety and security procedures and protocols.
• Working with Procurement and other Logistics Managers, you will control inventory levels by conducting physical counts and reconciling with inventory management tools.
• Maintain the physical condition of the storage areas by planning and implementing new design layouts; inspecting equipment; issuing work orders for repair and requisitions for replacement.
We work in a high security environment with sensitive equipment and maintaining this security and accountability will be a primary task. They are responsible for the security and tracking of parts within the storage areas and to the end user.
• Contribute to continuous process improvements to deliver on our goals of high availability and low cost. They maintain up-to-date metrics dashboards and will create reports for management as required.

Safety:
• Follow and maintain the highest safety standards and diligently encourage a world-class safety culture. Own the safety initiatives and projects to foster a strong safety culture.

About the team
Diverse Experiences
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship and Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Early Career Talent
When you join Amazon Web Services as a student or recent graduate, you’ll have the chance for your voice to be heard and amplified. That’s because our teams are looking to learn as much from you as you’ll learn from them. Whether you’re graduating with a high school or equivalent diploma, associate degree, bachelor’s degree, MBA, or PhD, we offer a range of early career opportunities across the globe.

Basic qualifications

- Speak, write, and read fluently in English
- Experience in goods receiving, inventory cycle counts and related auditing and stock control functions
- Experience in logistics

Preferred qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in supply chain/logistics or related field
- Experience managing multiple projects, prioritizing, planning, and managing time
- Experience with data center operations: inventory management, hot/cold aisles, security
- Experience recognizing a challenge and working with a variety of teams and data sources to diagnose the problem and recommend solutions

jobs.occupation: Research Scientist and Curator (m/f/d) of the section Vertebrata (Tenure Track) (Biologe/Biologin)
jobs.description:
Senckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at the Senckenberg Museum of Natural History in Görlitz, ideally as of April 1, 2027:

Research Scientist and Curator (m/f/d) of the section Vertebrata (Tenure Track)

(full time / part time options available)

Location: Görlitz

Employment scope: full time / part time options are available

Type of contract: initially limited to three years; 

the type of time limitation depends on individual profile and legal framework (maximum 3+3 years). A permanent employment is planned after a positive evaluation

Remuneration: collective agreement of the German Länder, TV-L E13

The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.

The renowned Senckenberg Museum of Natural History, located in the medieval town of Görlitz, combines research at an international level with extensive collections and an engaging museum program. The surrounding Upper Lusatia region offers a large variety of opportunities for experiencing nature.

Senckenberg is committed to study the causes and effects of biodiversity loss in the Anthropocene. As part of our strategic development, we launched an ambitious long-term research effort in “Anthropocene Biodiversity Loss” encompassing the modules “Collectomics”, “Biodiversity Genomics”, and “Solution Labs”. Objectives include the transformation of natural history collections into the digital era, studying biodiversity from the genome to the ecosystem levels and offering exploratory spaces for science and society to develop common solutions to Anthropocene challenges.

For the Görlitz vertebrate collection, which comprises approximately 70,000 specimens (preserved using dry, cryogenic, and liquid preservation methods, with the focus on mammals; birds make up a smaller proportion, while other vertebrate groups represent only a small fraction), we are seeking an internationally recognized scientist with a solid track record in mammal research, possibly supplemented by work on another vertebrate groups.

Potential research topics may include various aspects such as mammalian diversity, functional morphology, phylogeny, or biological interactions. Curation and collection-based research should play a significant role in the applicant’s research approach. The selected candidate should be open to research collaborations with SGN colleagues

Your tasks

- Scientific curation and development of the vertebrate collection and the associated resources as an important international research infrastructure through international networking, growth, and improved accessibility.
- Develop a visible portfolio of collection-based research with basic and applied aspects in the broad field of mammalogy and possibly other vertebrate groups by using a range of established and innovative methods and approaches.
- Taking responsibility for the relocation of the collection items, including the infrastructure of the Mammalogy/Vertebrate Section, to the new campus at Bahnhofstraße 30 at Görlitz.
- Secure external research funds.
- Publish results of your research in international scientific outlets.
- Establish collaborations with ongoing projects, regional and national region (e.g., long-term projects on wolf, lynx) and international (e.g., Africa, Mongolia), including with other sections and departments in Görlitz and further Senckenberg institutes.
- Communicate with external stakeholders such as scientific associations, conservation agencies, local and regional authorities, as well as citizen scientists.
- Participate in teaching in the MSc level programs of International Institute Zittau/ Dresden University of Technology.

Your profile 

- Doctoral degree in biology/zoology or a related field
- Expert knowledge of mammals, including native species (the biogeographic focus of the mammal collection is currently the Palearctic), additional expertise in other vertebrate groups
- Proactive willingness to implement innovative research approaches, such as in the field of genomics, morphometrics, AI, imaging, 3D methods, pollutant analysis in a collection context
- Ability to identify attractive research questions and make use of synergies through collaborations

The International Max Planck Research School for Ultrafast Imaging and Structural Dynamics in Hamburg, Germany, offers a structured PhD program focusing on ultra-fast phenomena, X-ray physics and dynamical imaging in all areas of science covering physics, chemistry and biology.

23 Interdisciplinary PhD positions in Ultrafast Science and Quantum Materials – IMPRS UFAST – Hamburg

Research

The program offers exciting research opportunities at ultra-intense electron and X-ray sources to directly observe atomic motions during primary events. The use of ultrafast imaging over the relevant length and time scales generates new levels of understanding of the interplay between structure and dynamics. Specific areas include the theoretical and experimental aspects of quantum materials and atomically resolved dynamics, fundamental light-matter interaction, accelerator-based light sources, coherent controlled molecular and solid state dynamics, molecular imaging, extreme timescale spectroscopy, ultrafast optics and X-ray science

jobs.description:

As a Business Controller (f/m/d) within the TI CP Business Controlling team, you serve as a trusted advisor to the Compression Service Region Europe & Africa, supporting a business spanning more than 35 countries. Working closely with regional leadership, finance teams, and operational stakeholders, you provide transparency on financial performance, drive forecasting and budgeting processes, and enable data-driven decision-making across a dynamic and diverse business environment.

Beyond core business controlling, you contribute to key strategic initiatives, including Enterprise Risk Management (ERM), sustainability reporting, central function controlling, and high-impact transformation projects. By combining financial expertise with business acumen and cross-functional collaboration, you help drive sustainable growth, operational excellence, and long-term value creation across the region.

How You’ll Make an Impact 

* Acting as the primary Finance Business Partner for the Compression Service Europe & Africa management team, providing financial transparency and actionable insights to support strategic decision-making
* Leading regional forecasting, budgeting, financial performance reviews, and financial planning & analysis activities across a network of more than 35 countries while identifying risks and opportunities
* Strengthening the Enterprise Risk Management framework and partnering with sustainability teams to support ESG initiatives, including EU Taxonomy reporting and compliance requirements
* Providing financial governance and controlling support for central functions, ensuring cost transparency, effective resource allocation, and sound financial governance
* Leading and supporting strategic projects and transformation initiatives, delivering financial insights, business case analyses, and value-creating recommendations
* Promoting process harmonization, digitalization, and automation to improve reporting quality, operational efficiency, and decision-making capabilities

What You Bring

* Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration, or a related field; an MBA or other advanced degree is considered an advantage
* Proven experience in controlling, financial planning & analysis (FP&A), business partnering, or finance leadership within an international environment
* Strong expertise in forecasting, budgeting, financial reporting, variance analysis, performance management, and financial governance, ideally complemented by knowledge of Enterprise Risk Management, ESG, or sustainability reporting
* Proven analytical and strategic capabilities with the ability to translate complex financial data into actionable business recommendations and influence management decisions
* Hands-on experience with SAP, financial planning systems, business intelligence tools, and Microsoft Office, combined with excellent stakeholder management and collaboration skills in multicultural organizations
* Fluent English skills; additional language skills are considered an advantage 

About the Team

In our Business Functions we enable our organization to reach their targets by providing best-in class services and solutions in the areas of IT, HR, Finance, Real Estate, Strategy & Technology and more. 

Who is Siemens Energy? 

At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. With ~100.000 dedicated employees in more than 90 countries, we develop the energy systems of the future, ensuring that the growing energy demand of the global community is met reliably and sustainably. The technologies created in our research departments and factories drive the energy transition and provide the base for one sixth of the world's electricity generation.

Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation.      

Find out how you can make a difference at Siemens Energy: https://www.siemens-energy.com/employeevideo

Our Commitment to Diversity 

Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity we generate power. We run on inclusion and our combined creative energy is fueled by over 130 nationalities. Siemens Energy celebrates character – no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability. We energize society, all of society, and we do not discriminate based on our differences. 

Rewards/Benefits 

* In addition to an attractive remuneration package in line with the market, you can expect an attractive employer-financed company pension scheme
* We also offer the opportunity to become a Siemens Energy shareholder
* We offer our employees the opportunity to work flexibly and remotely, and our inspiring offices provide space for collaboration and creativity
* The professional and personal development of our employees is very important to us. We provide them with the opportunities to learn and develop in a self-determined way, various attractive programmes and learning materials are available for this purpose
* In relation to the "compatibility of family and work", we have a wide range of offers, e.g. flexible working time models, childcare places at many locations, the possibility of trial part-time work or even a sabbatical

DESY, with more than 2900 employees at its two locations in Hamburg and Zeuthen, is one of the world's leading research centres. - Development, production, test and operation of state-of-the-art RF measurement devices, to be installed at our cavity test stands

- Performing measurement studies using the developed system on SRF cavities with a very high quality-factor

- MSc. degree in Physics, Electrical Engineering or Computer Science or equivalent qualification

Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc. is the world leader in serving science, with annual revenue of approximately $40 billion. We are a research, development, and production site in Bremen currently, with about 500 employees, whose “high-end” measurement and analysis instruments (mass spectrometers) are used in research and science worldwide. Our innovative products in the fields of Life Sciences MS and Inorganic MS, as well as T  Elemental Analysis, are among the leading products globally in their respective markets.

The Scientific Software & Research Platform Engineer combines scientific investigation, data science, software engineering, and deep instrument knowledge to improve instrument performance, calibration, diagnostics, and reliability. This on-site role requires regular hands-on work with spectrometers, including prototypes, and close collaboration with Research, Production/Operations, and Support.

- Manage data versioning, metadata, experiment tracking, and scalable execution from laptops to servers/clusters.

- Package, install, and validate new iterations in lab and production test environments.
- Collaborate with researchers, Production Engineering, IT/Operations, and Support to ensure reliable and traceable deployment.

Education

Experience

- Experience developing research software and translating scientific insights into diagnostic, predictive, or decision-support tools.
- Comfortable working directly with physical instruments and deploying and validating software in controlled lab or production test environments.

Knowledge, Skills, Abilities

- Scientific Software Engineering: Python, clean APIs, modular design, testing, and reproducible research workflows.
- Data & Modeling: Data analysis and visualization, SQL/NoSQL and file-based data systems, diagnostic modeling, experiment tracking, and model/version management.
- Engineering Tools: Strong Linux/Bash; CI, containerization, and server/cluster execution. Familiarity with C++/Rust is a plus.
- Production-aware delivery: Ability to install, configure, troubleshoot, and validate research software and translate manual processes into Documented and increasingly automated workflows.
- English: Full professional proficiency, written and spoken.

Master student (d/f/m) in the field of Investment Management

title of thesis: Generative AI & Process Automation in Industrial & Strategic Investment/CapEx Decisions

You are looking for a master thesis and want to get to know the work of an Investment Manager in Industrial Operations? Then apply now! We look forward to you supporting us in the central Capex Management department as a master student (d/f/m)!

- Location: Hamburg
- Start: Q1 2027
- Duration: 6 months

Your location

You will be working at the largest production site for civil aircraft situated in Hamburg. Its location on the southern banks of the river Elbe includes the option to commute by ferry. Experience the special flair of Hamburg in your spare time where vibrant cosmopolitan culture meets nautic legacy.

Your benefits

- Work-life balance with a 35-hour week (flexitime).
- International environment with the opportunity to network globally.
- Work with modern/diversified technologies.
- At Airbus, we see you as a valuable team member and you are not hired to brew coffee, instead you are in close contact with the interfaces and are part of our weekly team meetings.

Your tasks and responsibilities

As-Is Process Mapping:

- Assess the current state of the end-to-end CapEx dossier creation lifecycle across operational sites. You will have a close exchange with the results of the VS (Value Stream Assessments) results.

Optimisation Analysis:

- Pinpoint bottlenecks, redundant reporting between local presentations and our enterprise CapEx Planning Tool (CPT), and root causes in heavy 27-slide dossiers

Solution Design:

- Outline proposed improvements by architecting an intake and generation pipeline connecting Google Drive, Gemini AI, and Google Slides to condense content into a decision-oriented 7-slide format and and integrate “investment intelligence”, e.g. benchmarking or cost referentials.
- Design, test, and calibrate prompt or similar tools workflows for Gemini to synthesize executive summaries, risk matrices, and multi-year cash phasing projections.

Pilot Case:

- Test your approach by running 1 to 3 live industrial investment dossiers through the automated pipeline.

Performance Comparison & AI Compliance:

- Evaluate KPI improvements (As-Is vs. To-Be), measuring administrative time savings and controller approval speeds and general compliance.

Desired skills and qualifications

- Enrolled fulltime in the final year of a Master’s degree (Bac+5 / MSc) in Industrial Engineering, Information Systems (with strong business/operations interest), Business Analytics, Data Science, or a related dual engineering/business program.
- Technical Mindset: Strong interest in Generative AI prompting, workflow automation, and low-code integration (e.g., Google Workspace ecosystem, Apps Script / Python, API interactions).
- Business & Financial Curiosity: Comfortable understanding operational investment concepts (CapEx vs. OpEx, cash phasing, business cases, ROI/NPV logic).
- Communication & Change Leadership: Strong interpersonal skills to interface smoothly with diverse stakeholders (from shop-floor industrial engineers to financial controllers).
- Language Proficiency: Negotiation-level fluency in English (working language). Knowledge of French, German, or Spanish is an asset.

Integration of quantum-based algorithms into classical computing environments, and system-levelstability/error analysis of the integrated hybrid stack.

Running simulations on HPC systems, including efficiently parallelizing computational tasks

Writing HPC-executable, production-ready code

Ensuring scalability and robustness of algorithms in large-scale environments

Identifying and resolving error sources in the integrated hybrid stack, particularly cascading errors acrossmodules

Developing independent code for simulations, extending beyond the use of standard software libraries

Demonstrated experience running simulations on HPC systems

Excellent teamwork and communication skills

Fluent English (spoken and written)

The applicant must demonstrate the ability to do such a verification withoutAI assistance in the interview.

The Gesellschaft für wissenschaftliche Datenverarbeitung mbH Göttingen (GWDG) is the university computing centerfor the Georg-August-Universität Göttingen and a computing and IT competence center for the Max Planck Society.The provision of high-performance HPC systems has been one of its tasks for over 40 years. In 2020, the Universityof Göttingen / GWDG was accepted as one of eight computing centers (NHR-Nord@Göttingen) in the National High-Performance Computing (NHR) network. The GWDG also operates the national AI service center KISSKI and is apartner in the EU AI Factory HammerHAI. Furthermore, the GWDG operates HPC resources for the GermanAerospace Center (DLR). As a national supercomputing center, the GWDG provides technical support to researchersand students from various scientific domains, including digital humanities, life science, earth system science, andengineering. We also participate in both national and international research projects. In the field of quantumcomputing, the GWDG also runs the QUICS project, providing SMEs with access to quantum computing resources.

We are looking for highly motivated candidates to join the QC team at the GWDG focused on anomaly detection forindustry applications. The goal is to build a platform for such use cases based on existing stacks, giving companies atool for quantum anomaly detection.

The GWDG together with the Faculty of Mathematics and Computer Science and the Campus Institute Data Science(CIDAS) of the University of Göttingen provides a stimulating research environment in Scientific Computing, with anopportunity to conduct research in the intersection of applied computer science, High-Performance Computing,Quantum Computing, and AI.

Focus:

Connecting quantum workloads to GWDG’s existing HPC infrastructure. Requires a deep understanding ofboth classical HPC architectures and the specific characteristics of quantum jobs. The developer will takeresponsibility for scheduler logic, including:

SLURM partition mapping

Optimization of SLURM execution for Quantum Computing Jobs

Implement HPC transpilation pipelines and, more generally, workflows for HPC/AI pre- and post-processing

Performance tuning of hybrid workloads

Implementation of monitoring and benchmarking mechanisms

PhD and/or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Physics, or a related field, combined with demonstrableindustry or research experience

Ability to code in Python

Proven coding experience (without AI assistance): scope, functions, variables, classes, array methods, etc.

Demonstrable expertise in optimizing HPC stacks for proper system implementation and tuning

Experience building and operating software-based services, ensuring long-term maintainability

Knowledge in QC (quantum computing) job characteristics and resource requirements, and familiarity withcompiler/transpiler pipelines

Excellent teamwork and communication skills

Fluent English (spoken and written)

Do you fit

all

the above requirements? Then we welcome your application!

Desirable

Demonstrable experience tuning SLURM (partitioning, QoS, job prioritization policies) in a production HPCenvironment

Experience benchmarking and profiling hybrid classical/quantum or GPU workloads

Experience enabling optimal, resource-efficient operation of hybrid classical/quantum workloads

Familiarity with monitoring and observability tooling for HPC systems (e.g., Prometheus, Grafana)

Background in systems administration or DevOps for research computing infrastructure

German B2 or higher

A modern, diverse work environment at the intersection between academia and industry

Qualification and further development of your skills

Social benefits of the public sector

For our location in Hamburg we are seeking:

Embedded & Systems Software Developer for PETRA IV

Limited: 2 years | Start: 01.01.2027 | ID: FSMA045/2026 | Deadline: 08.11.2026 | Full-time/Part-time | Remote work possible

DESY, with more than 2900 employees at its two locations in Hamburg and Zeuthen, is one of the world's leading research centres. Its research focuses on decoding the structure and function of matter, from the smallest particles of the universe to the building blocks of life. In this way, DESY contributes to solving the major questions and urgent challenges facing science, society and industry. With its ultramodern research infrastructure, its interdisciplinary research platforms and its international networks, DESY offers a highly attractive working environment in the fields of science, technology and administration as well as for the education of highly qualified young scientists.

The DESY Photon-Science Detector Group designs and builds innovative and state-of-the-art X-ray cameras for us in a variety of scientific experiments, in Hamburg and world wide. We are developing new high-speed cameras for an upcoming major upgrade to our X-ray facilities, PETRA IV, and improved software is required for camera control, data handling, and interfacing to users and the facility's systems. We are looking for a software developer to work on these tasks together with our experts in detector engineering and scientific computing.

With the PETRA IV project, DESY is launching one of the most ambitious and innovative large-scale research projects worldwide. PETRA IV, the most brilliant synchrotron radiation source of the next generation, will be the ultimate 4D X-ray microscope, setting new standards in precision and performance. To implement the project, we are looking for motivated employees who want to get involved in a complex project with international appeal. More information about PETRA IV: PETRA IV (https://cockpit.as-mediendesign.de/jump1/133043/2/696)

- Developing software for controlling and configuring a large camera system consisting of multiple units
- Developing a system for receiving detector data at high speed on a set of data acquisition PCs, in collaboration with experts in hardware acceleration
- Developing the interfaces between the X‑ray camera and the facility's control and scientific computing systems

About you:

- Master's degree in software engineering, computer science or equivalent
- Experience with embedded and/or systems programming
- Experience with both Python and a lower-level language (preferably C++)
- Good standard of English
- Good team player, and the ability to work effectively with experts in other fields (firmware developers and detector engineers)
- Experience with high performance computing
- Experience with high-speed networking

Good reasons to join:

Look forward to a unique working environment on our international research campus. Respectful cooperation and the well-being of our DESY employees are particularly important to us. Gender equality is an important aspect for us. To support work‑life balance we offer flexible working hours, variable part-time, job-sharing models and participation in mobile work (up to 50%). You will benefit from our family-friendly and collegial atmosphere, our established health management and occupational pension provision. As a public funded employer, we offer you a secure workplace and facilitate your individual career with our comprehensive training and development opportunities. Remuneration is according to the regulations of the TV‑AVH. DESY offers its employees a financial supplement for a German job ticket (Deutschland-Ticket) at both locations

For further information, please contact David Pennicard at +49 40 8998‑4544 (https://tel:+494089984544) (david.pennicard@desy.de (david.pennicard@desy.de) ).

Apply now! (https://cockpit.as-mediendesign.de/jump1/133043)

DESY promotes equal opportunities, diversity and inclusion (https://cockpit.as-mediendesign.de/jump1/133043/2/2544) . We therefore welcome applications from people of all dimensions of diversity. The professional development of women (https://cockpit.as-mediendesign.de/jump1/133043/2/2820) is very important to us and therefore we strongly encourage women to apply for the vacant position. VetterTec is an innovative company headquartered in Kassel, Germany, with more than 95 years of experience in the development and manufacturing of machinery and systems for industrial drying and dewatering, particularly for the food processing industry. With a team of more than 160 employees across six locations and an international sales share exceeding 80%, we offer an exciting and dynamic working environment.

To support our continued growth, we are looking for a Project Engineer who is passionate about driving technically demanding projects to success.

As a Project Engineer, you take ownership of projects from kick-off through final handover, both technically and organizationally. Acting as the customer's main point of contact, you work closely with Technical Engineering, Process Engineering, Procurement, and site teams to ensure successful project execution. This role is ideal for someone who leads through technical expertise and practical experience, with a strong focus on technical project responsibility rather than pure project coordination.

Your Responsibilities:

- Full project ownership from order handover to technical and commercial handover (TOC) - budget, schedule, risk and scope
- Single point of contact for the customer throughout the project
- Functional leadership of the core project team - holding the team's capacity together and keeping the project moving as one
- Technical judgment: understanding the equipment and the process well enough to challenge assumptions and demand the right decisions at the right time
- On-site presence at the milestones that matter — project kick-off, construction start, mechanical and electrical completion, commissioning start, and the final performance run (Leistungsfahrt) through handover
- Presence at key suppliers for the acceptance (FAT) of critical components
- Running the team's agile rhythm - weekly syncs, a shared task board, rolling short-term planning, and visualizing progress - and adjusting quickly when the project needs it
- Integrating the contributions of Technical Engineering, Process Engineering, Procurement, Manufacturing, Installation and Commissioning into one coherent project, without replacing any of them

What You Bring:

- Professional experience in international plant or equipment engineering (Anlagenbau), ideally with process or industrial equipment
- A hands-on, practical mindset — someone who has stood on a shop floor or a construction site, not only in front of a screen; we weigh practical experience over theoretical credentials
- A mechanical engineering background as a Techniker (completed apprenticeship plus Techniker) or a comparable practical qualification (Bachelor's / FH degree)
- Experience in vessel and plant construction (Anlagen- und Behälterbau) - manufacturing methods and welding processes
- Project management capability - comfortable owning budget, schedule and risk - with a technical center of gravity
- Business-fluent English (must-have); German is a plus, not a requirement
- Willingness to travel internationally, including assignments of around two weeks at a time
- Comfortable leading a team with lightweight agile practices - task boards, short review cycles, rolling planning - rather than heavyweight process
- Professional or Senior level - we are hiring at both

How We Work:

- Projects follow a clear phase structure, but day to day we work in short cycles — weekly team syncs, a shared task board, and rolling four-to-six-week planning alongside the overall schedule
- Remote work is possible for this role, with on-site presence expected for supplier acceptances of key components and for construction and site activities
- You don't need to be based in Germany
- Onboarding starts in the office; afterwards, your working pattern is by arrangement
- A relaxed, direct working atmosphere — we'd rather solve a problem in the team meeting than escalate it

What We Offer:

- Real ownership of international projects from kick-off through commissioning and final handover
- A technically challenging role with a high level of responsibility and the opportunity to shape Project Engineering at VetterTec
- A collaborative, solution-oriented culture with short decision-making processes
- 30 days of annual leave, attractive working conditions, and a competitive compensation package
- Comprehensive employee benefits, including bike leasing, subsidized public transportation, Corporate Benefits, and additional company benefits
- Extensive personal and professional development opportunities in an international environment

﻿Please don't spend time writing a cover letter. Instead, send us a brief project portfolio describing a project you have taken from the initial phase through execution and final handover, highlighting your responsibilities, key challenges, and achieved results.

**Take Your Opportunity - **Join us and actively contribute to the continued growth and development of our company. Together, we strive to inspire our employees and customers through innovative technology, modern structures, and sustainable growth

Together Towards the Future. Are You Ready to Join Us?

Constructor University (formerly Jacobs University) is a private, state-accredited, English-language university in Bremen. We offer Bachelor, Master, and PhD programs in three schools: School of Science, School of Computer Science and Engineering, and School of Business, Social and Decision Sciences. Our principles are first-class teaching and research, international diversity, and multidisciplinary cooperation. Constructor University consistently achieves top results in national and international university rankings. As an international university, we attract highly talented and open-minded students from all over the world. Currently, over 1.800 students from 110 nations live and study on our residential campus.

Constructor University is seeking to fill a tenure-track faculty position in organic chemistry with a focus on synthetic organic chemistry, and we invite applications from interested candidates for the following position, to be filled ideally by January 2027:

Assistant Professor of Organic Chemistry (f/m/d)
(full-time, tenure-track, initially limited to 3 years)

Your Responsibilities:

The School of Science is particularly interested in a candidate who combines experimental and computational or theoretical approaches for the development of synthetic methodology and synthesis of bioactive molecules or functional materials. The implementation of AI, machine learning, or data-driven control / optimization is highly welcome, for example, for synthesis planning, activity prediction, sensing, or structural topology. jobs.description:
Constructor University (formerly Jacobs University) is a private, state-accredited, English-language university in Bremen. We offer Bachelor, Master, and PhD programs in three schools: School of Science, School of Computer Science and Engineering, and School of Business, Social and Decision Sciences. Our principles are first-class teaching and research, international diversity, and transdisciplinary cooperation. According to the 2024 Times Higher Education (THE) World University Rankings, Constructor University is among the top 25 percent out of more than 1900 universities worldwide and is ranked as the second most international university in the world. As an international university, we attract highly talented and open-minded students from all over the world. Currently, over 1,600 students from 110 nations live and study on our residential campus.

The research group led by Prof. Dr. Andrey Ustyuzhanin at Constructor University, in collaboration with Constructor Knowledge Labs (CKL) and Constructor Technology (industry partner), invites applications for Ph.D. student positions in the field of Computer Science, with a focus on Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML).

This PhD position is part of an initiative to advance knowledge representation and adaptive reasoning systems. The research will focus on developing flexible frameworks for actionable knowledge representation that support storage, retrieval, and dynamic adaptation of information across diverse tasks.

Key objectives include:

- Transforming unstructured data into interactive knowledge graphs and personalized cognitive maps.
- Designing models that provide interpretable, persistent, and navigable structures of knowledge.
- Addressing challenges such as hierarchy, composability, and coarse-graining for robust, task-specific reasoning.
- Exploring individual and community-level knowledge modeling, including personalized domain maps, profile extraction from artifacts (e.g., papers, courses), and cross-domain abstraction.

The overarching goal is to create systems that enable transparent, adaptive, and spatially intuitive representations of knowledge, supporting both individual users and collaborative communities.
