Imagine a future where you play a key role in ensuring electrical safety across our offshore substations and wind turbines while helping us push the boundaries of safe, efficient, and reliable offshore operations.

Join us in this role where you’ll take independent ownership of electrical safety within your area of responsibility, overseeing electrical installations on wind turbines in our German wind farms. You’ll combine your deep technical expertise with on-site presence—both at your permanent base in Norddeich and offshore—in order to guide colleagues, strengthen procedures, and ensure safe systems of work.

Welcome to HV and Transmission GER

You’ll be part of HV and Transmission GER, where you and your colleagues will ensure electrical safety governance and operational support across high-voltage infrastructure in our German offshore wind farms. Your team is dedicated to managing safety-critical systems, uplifting operational standards, and sharing expertise across the organisation.

As a team, we collaborate closely, support one another’s development, and bring a proactive, solution-oriented mindset to every challenge.

You’ll play an important role in:

- preparing and reviewing risk assessments for offshore electrical work
- supporting the selection, training, and supervision of Authorised Persons, electricians, and electrically instructed persons offshore
- contributing to the qualification and supervision of contractors in the offshore electrical environment
- developing, implementing, and improving maintenance plans for offshore electrical installations
- coordinating multiple employers involved in offshore electrical activities
- planning, organising, delivering, and documenting electrical safety training
- implementing, strengthening, and regularly reviewing the Wind Turbine Safety Rules (WTSR) and Orsted Electrical Safety Rules (OESR)
- assuming designated roles within the Safe Systems of Work, such as Authorising Engineer, Authorising Officer, or Training Mentor
- auditing work processes before offshore deployment.

To succeed in the role, you:

- have completed a degree within electrical engineering, or equivalent
- bring strong expertise within electrical safety, including standards, laws, and regulations
- demonstrate technical leadership competence
- offer switching experience in high-voltage environments above 20 kV
- communicate confidently in both English and German at B2 level or higher
- are comfortable using IT systems, including Microsoft Office, SAP, and AI tools
- ideally have a qualification for live working, experience with wind turbines, or prior responsibility as an electrician
- meet the minimum competency requirements within your onboarding timeframe, supported by our learning and development processes.

**Country-specific requirements: **fulfil the requirements of a responsible electrician (vEFK) according to VDE 1000-10.

Please note that in this role you will be mainly working in our office in Norddeich from Monday to Friday. An important part of the role will be an inspection of plants and the professional guidance of the electricians. This requires partial work offshore (20-40%) in a 7- or 14-day shift pattern.

Your missionWe are seeking a motivated Junior Fermentation Scientist to join our biotechnology team and support the development and optimization of microbial fermentation processes. This is a hands-on laboratory role with a strong focus on planning and executing fermentation experiments, from shake-flask cultivation to bench-scale fermentations.

You will work independently at the clean bench, prepare andoperate fermentation experiments, and monitor relevant process parameters and performance
indicators. Your responsibilities will also include analyzing key process and product KPIs using bioanalytical methods such as SDS-based analysis, enzymatic assays, and HPLC, as well as evaluating, documenting, and reporting experimental results.

The role offers a high degree of autonomy in organizing your day-to-day laboratory work, with responsibility for ensuring that experiments are thoroughly planned, executed, analyzed, and documented. You will contribute directly to improving our microbial fermentation workflows and advancing robust and scalable bioprocesses.
• Plan, prepare, and perform microbial cultivation and fermentation experiments, ranging from shake-flask cultures to bench-scale fermentations of up to 5 L
• Carry out laboratory work under aseptic conditions, including work at the clean bench and the preparation of culture media, buffers, solutions, and reagents
• Set up, operate, monitor, and maintain bench-top fermentation systems and associated laboratory equipment
• Monitor fermentation performance and evaluate relevant process and product KPIs throughout experimental campaigns
• Perform bioanalytical characterization of fermentation samples using methods such as SDS-based analysis, enzymatic assays, HPLC, and other relevant analytical techniques
• Evaluate experimental data, identify trends and deviations, and summarize results in a clear and structured manner
• Document experiments thoroughly and learn how to prepare concise reports of experimental results and conclusions
• Organize and prioritize your laboratory activities independently, ensuring that experiments are properly planned, executed, analyzed, and documented within agreed timelines
• Contribute to the maintenance and organization of microbial strains, cell banks, laboratory materials, and equipment
• Collaborate closely with colleagues across different disciplines and contribute to the continuous improvement of our fermentation processes and laboratory workflows

• A degree or vocational qualification in biotechnology, microbiology, bioprocess engineering, biological laboratory technology (e.g. BTA), or a related field
• Practical experience working under aseptic conditions and confidence in standard microbiological and biotechnology laboratory techniques
• Hands-on experience with microbial cultivation; experience with shake-flask cultures and/or bench-scale fermenters is highly desirable
• Familiarity with the preparation of culture media, buffers, solutions, and reagents, as well as accurate sample handling and laboratory documentation
• Experience with, or a strong interest in learning, analytical methods for evaluating fermentation samples, such as SDS-based analysis, enzymatic assays, and HPLC
• A structured and reliable approach to experimental work, with the ability to independently organize laboratory activities and follow experiments through from preparation to data analysis and reporting
• A practical, hands-on mindset combined with curiosity, attention to detail, and a willingness to troubleshoot and learn new techniques
• A collaborative and team-oriented approach, while being comfortable taking ownership of assigned experiments and project tasks
• Good communication skills in English, both written and spoken; German is a plus

Join our Griesheim Biobank team as EU Sample Management Coordinator (Logistics Coordinator & Import/Export Analyst).

How You´ll Add Value

As EU Sample Management Coordinator (m/w/d), you will coordinate the shipment of biological samples, laboratory materials, and related goods throughout Europe and internationally. In this role, you will also help ensure compliance with applicable customs, import/export, and trade regulations by supporting the accurate preparation, review, and coordination of shipment documentation and related processes.

The role offers a combination of hands-on logistics coordination, customs administration, customer communication, and process improvement. Success in this position requires strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment while ensuring shipments meet internal standards and external regulatory requirements.

This is an opportunity to join an established international organization and play a key role in supporting scientific and clinical research projects across Europe.

What You´ll Do

- You are part of a four-person logistics team that serves as the central point of contact for logistics matters across our operations, as well as for customers and service providers.

- Your routine tasks include packaging and labeling goods ready for shipment, as well as preparing cover letters, freight documents, and customs documentation.
- You support import and export compliance activities, including reviewing shipment data for customs relevance, helping ensure correct classification, documentation completeness, and adherence to internal procedures and applicable regulations.
- You are responsible for coordinating with customs authorities, brokers, and other relevant parties to ensure smooth border crossings, including in time-critical cases.
- You help monitor and maintain records related to import/export activities and support internal compliance checks, audits, and process documentation updates where required.
- You support the continuous development of our logistics processes and service offerings, including with a focus on compliance, efficiency, and sustainability.
- You also support incoming goods processing when needed, checking for completeness and informing the relevant departments, for example in the case of deliveries of chemicals and reagents.
- Additionally, you are responsible for inventory, as well as managing and ordering logistics-related materials.
- You understand and strictly adhere to standard operating procedures (SOPs) in English and contribute to maintaining high ethical and quality standards in all shipment-related activities.

What You´ll Bring

- Successfully completed vocational training or a degree in business administration, logistics, customs, or a similar qualification.
- Practical work experience in logistics, customs, import/export, or within a freight forwarding company.
- Sound understanding of customs clearance processes, shipping documentation, and import/export compliance requirements; experience with dangerous goods is a plus.

- Strong hands-on mentality.
- Attention to detail and excellent prioritization skills.
- Fluent in German and English (B2 level or higher).

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher (f/m/d) to characterize young star-planet systems and their flaring activity (Astrophysiker/in, Astronom/in)
jobs.description:
The Max Planck Institute for Solar System Research (MPS) in Göttingen is one of the world's leading research institutions in the field of solar physics and planetary research with around 300 employees. The interdisciplinary research focus is the investigation of the development, diversity and dynamics of planets, moons, small bodies, the sun and solar-like stars. The MPS develops and operates scientific instruments for current and future space missions (e.g. ESA, NASA), and carries out cosmochemical laboratory investigations of meteorites as well as numerical modeling on state-of-the-art supercomputers.

The Department Solar & Stellar Interiors at MPS invites applications for the position of a

Postdoctoral Researcher (f/m/d) to characterize young star-planet systems and their flaring activity

In recent years, exoplanetary science has undergone a major shift -- moving from exoplanet detection towards understanding star-planet systems as a whole, including the host star, interplanetary medium and galactic context. Specifically, tidal and magnetic interactions between planets and their host stars have been recognized to be able to modulate the evolution of both, including the atmospheric evolution of the planet and its habitability. The newly established ERC StG project PLANETARE seeks a postdoctoral researcher with a background in stellar magnetism and/or exoplanetary science to develop novel ways of detecting and characterizing the mutual influence of stars and planets with a focus on the influence of planets in short orbits on the magnetism of their host stars. At the core of the project is a new way to find exoplanets: detecting them through their magnetic interaction with the host star. This position builds the observational foundation - the sample, the activity catalog, and the geometry of the systems - and confirms any transiting planets among the interacting systems.

Your Tasks

- Compile the most accurate and complete flaring activity catalog to date using space-borne photometry
- Search the sample of flaring stars for transiting planet candidates using space-borne photometry
- Constrain the orientation of the rotational and magnetic axes of interacting systems
- Measure stellar activity characteristics and their predictive power for interaction

The transit search, flaring catalog and geometry measurements will constrain some of the drivers of interaction and its observability, working towards a true occurrence rate of magnetic interaction in young star-planet systems. You will work closely with a second postdoc (https://karriere.mps.mpg.de/jobposting/ff58b9b82b6efc0b224bf8134f1471929fdc639c0) within a small, newly formed team of two postdocs and a PhD student, led by the PI (Ekaterina Ilin). Group members are supported to lead their own papers and proposals, and to present at international meetings in both the stellar and exoplanet communities.

Your Qualification

- A PhD in physics or astrophysics (PhD must be awarded by the start date)
- Previous experience in observational astronomy, ideally including space-borne optical photometry
- The ability to work in a team
- A good command of the English language

Our Offer

- Comprehensive onboarding, professional development and further training opportunities
- Diverse and varied tasks in an international work environment
- Renumeration according to TVöDBund, based on qualifications and experience, annual bonus and additional pension scheme (VBL)
- 30 days of vacation plus 4 additional days off
- Full-time and part-time employment; flexible working time and possibility of mobile work
- Cooperation with local bilingual Montessori child care center
- Good connection by public transport
- Corporate health management

Additional Information

- Start date between January and October 2027
- Duration: 4 years
- Remuneration is according to EG 13 TVöD-Bund
- Application deadline is October 30, 2026 (interviews in late November / early December 2026)

We look forward to receiving your informative application documents (cover letter, CV, references, certificates). Please submit these via the digital application portal (https://www.mps.mpg.de/career/jobs (https://www.mps.mpg.de/career/jobs) ). If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact Dr. Ekaterina Ilin (ilin@mps.mpg.de (ilin@mps.mpg.de) ).

The Max Planck Society endeavours to achieve gender equality and diversity. Furthermore, the Max Planck Society seeks to increase the number of women in those areas where they are underrepresented and therefore explicitly encourages women to apply. This is your chance to connect with your peers, learn directly from our seasoned leaders, and gain insights from the best in the industry.

Throughout the programme, you will be developed into an established and valuable team member from day 1. Most importantly, you'll have learned more about yourself and what makes you truly great. Above all, you'll have the unparalleled opportunity to do your best work in an industry that is literally reshaping how we live in our world.

jobs.occupation: Research Associate / Postdoc (m/f/d) in the field of Cryogenic Quantum Electronics (Physiker/in)
jobs.description:
With around 15.000 students and 3.800 employees, the Technische Universität Braunschweig is one of Germany’s leading institutes of technology. It stands for strategic and performance-oriented thinking and acting, relevant research, committed teaching, and the successful transfer of knowledge and technologies to the economy and society. We consistently advocate for family friendliness and equal opportunities.

Our research focuses are mobility, engineering for health, metrology, and city of the future. Strong engineering and natural sciences are our core disciplines. These are closely interconnected with economics, social and educational sciences and humanities. Our campus is located in the midst of one of the most research-intensive regions in Europe. We work successfully together with over 20 research institutions in our neighborhood as we do with our international partner universities.

The Division of Cryogenic Quantum Electronics, led by Prof. Dr. Oleksandr Dobrovolskiy, investigates fascinating physical phenomena governing the dynamics of magnetic and superconducting systems and develops quantum electronic devices based on these principles. Its research bridges materials science, experimental physics, electrical measurement science, and metrology. To strengthen the research group and advance its cutting-edge research in cryogenic quantum electronics, we are seeking a

Postdoctoral Researcher (m/f/d)
(EG13 TV-L, full time - fixed term)

with demonstrated expertise in experimental low-temperature physics.
The position is to be filled on a fixed-term basis for an initial period of 2 years. The successful applicant will be given the opportunity to pursue a further scientific qualification (habilitation).

Your tasks

- You will carry out research in the area of cryogenic and quantum electronics, with a focus on experiments at mK temperatures.
- You will apply for and work on research projects.
- You will perform measurements in a dilution refrigerator and other cryogenic setups, develop, build and optimize cryogenic measurement platforms.
- You will publish research findings in leading international journals and participate in national and international conferences.
- You will be involved in teaching at the University (preparation and implementation of courses as well as supervision of students’ work).

Your Qualifications

- You hold a completed university degree at Master’s level or equivalent, as well as a completed PhD in a field relevant to the position (e.g. physics, electrical engineering, materials science, or a related field), and ideally have postdoctoral research experience.
- You have experience with low-temperature experiments, ideally involving dilution refrigerators in the fields of superconductivity and/or magnetism, as well as good programming skills (e.g., Python, LabVIEW).
- You have knowledge of superconducting and/or magnetic devices, high-frequency and microwave engineering, nanotechnology, and/or quantum measurement techniques, or you are willing and able to acquire this expertise quickly.
- You have excellent English language skills; knowledge of German is desirable.
- You are flexible, can perform under pressure and work well in a team.

We offer

- work on exciting future-oriented research topics in an inspiring work environment as part of the university community
- A vibrant campus life in an international atmosphere with lots of intercultural offers and international cooperations
- Pay in accordance with the collective agreement TV-L (a special payment at the end of the year as well as a supplementary benefit in the form of a company pension, comparable to a company pension in the private sector) including 30 days' vacation per year
- flexible working and part-time options and a family-friendly university culture, awarded the "Family-friendly university" audit since 2007
- special continuing education programs for young scientists, a postdoc program, as well as other offerings from the Central Personnel Development Department and sports activities.

Further notes
We welcome applicants of all nationalities. At the same time, we encourage people with severe disabilities to apply. Applications from severely disabled persons will be given preference if they are equally qualified. Please attach a proof of disability to your application. We are also working on the fulfilment of the Central Equality Plan based on the Lower Saxony Equal Rights Act (Niedersächsisches Gleichberechtigungsgesetz—NGG) and strive to reduce under-representation in all areas and positions as defined by the NGG. Therefore, applications from women are particularly welcome in this case.

The personal data will be stored for the purpose of processing the application. By submitting your application, you agree that your data may be stored and processed electronically for application purposes in compliance with the provisions of data protection law. Further information on data protection can be found in our data protection regulations at https://www.tu-braunschweig.de/datenschutzerklaerung-bewerbungen (https://www.tu-braunschweig.de/datenschutzerklaerung-bewerbungen) .

Application costs cannot be reimbursed.

Deadline for applications is 31.10.2026.

Please send your application via email to oleksandr.dobrovolskiy@tu-braunschweig.de (https://mailto:oleksandr.dobrovolskiy@tu-braunschweig.de) with the following documents in the PDF-format:

• Cover letter
• Curriculum vitae (CV)
• List of publications
• Brief summary of previous research / third-party projects (2 pages)
• Doctoral degree certificate
• Names of two references

and Fundamental Electrical Engineering

jobs.occupation: Scientific Programmer (mfd) High-Performance Computing and Software Engineering (Informatiker/in)
jobs.description:
The Max Planck Institute for Marine Microbiology is a research institute of the Max Planck Society. It was founded in 1992 in the State of Bremen and employs around 200 staff members. In close collaboration with numerous university and non-university research institutions, we explore the diversity and function of microorganisms in the ocean and their interactions with their environment. Scientists from all over the world, engineers, technicians and administrative staff together make an important contribution to global marine and environmental research.

In the Department of Ocean Biosphere Dynamics, we are looking to fill up a position as

Scientific Programmer (mfd)

High-Performance Computing and Software Engineering

The department investigates the dynamics of the ocean carbon cycle, its variability and predictability, and its role in the Earth system through climate–carbon cycle feedbacks operating across timescales from days to millennia. A central objective is to improve the representation of marine carbon, nutrient cycling and microbial processes in Earth System Models while increasing spatial model resolution to capture key physical and biogeochemical dynamics in the ocean.

To support this mission, we are seeking different Scientific Programmers (m/f/d) to drive the next generation of ocean biogeochemical modelling in Earth System Models. The successful candidates will contribute to the development, integration, and performance optimization of a state-of-the-art modelling framework, enabling increasingly sophisticated representations of marine biogeochemical processes and unprecedented high-resolution numerical experimentation. Together, they will help ensure that the modelling infrastructure combines scientific excellence with cutting-edge software engineering, delivering robust, efficient, and scalable performance on current and future exascale computing platforms.

The successful candidate will help ensure that the modelling framework of the HAMburg Ocean Carbon Cycle model (HAMOCC) which is part of the ICON Earth system modeling framework remains technologically advanced and capable of efficiently exploiting emerging HPC architectures. Emphasis will be placed on heterogeneous computing and the optimal use of CPU and GPU resources to maximize model performance, scalability, and portability.

A particular focus of the position will be a dedicated project to prepare, optimize, and benchmark the code for deployment on heterogeneous CPU/GPU systems, ensuring efficient performance and supporting the transition to next-generation HPC infrastructure.

The role involves close interactions with researchers, research students and model developers to translate scientific advances into reliable and maintainable model code. The successful candidate will also have the opportunity to contribute to peer-reviewed publications and present research outcomes at scientific conferences.

Key responsibilities:

- Develop and optimize model code of HAMOCC for modern supercomputing architectures
- Enable and improve heterogeneous execution across CPUs and GPUs
- Lead and contribute to software development, maintaining Git repositories, testing and debugging, code review, and Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) to ensure robust, maintainable, and reproducible code
- Implement performance analysis, profiling, and optimization strategies
- Support portability across current and future HPC platforms
- Collaborate with model developers to translate scientific requirements into efficient software solutions

Desired qualifications:

- Degree in computer science, computational science, applied mathematics, or a related field
- Experience with numerical modelling and analysis and handling of large simulation datasets
- Strong knowledge of HPC programming (Fortran and C/C++) and performance optimization
- Knowledge of parallel programming paradigms such as MPI, OpenMP, OpenACC or equivalent technologies
- Experience with large-scale scientific software projects, including software testing and debugging, code review workflows
- Strong knowledge of software engineering best practices, including Git
- Fluent in English, with solid scientific writing skills and a strong interest in working collaboratively within an international and interdisciplinary team

What we offer:

This position is initially offered for three years. Continuation beyond the initial term is intended, subject to satisfactory performance, applicable legal requirements, and the availability of funding.

We offer a position in an international science environment. You can expect a multifaceted job with challenging tasks in an exciting, academic work environment. You will have a high degree of autonomy and creative freedom, and we will promote your further education, e.g. within the framework of external courses and certifications. The compatibility of private life, family and career are important components of our personnel policy. You will be paid according to the collective agreement for the public service (TVöD Bund). Allowances are possible depending on qualifications and areas of responsibility.

Are you interested?

We look forward to receiving your full application via our online application portal. This should include a statement of interest, CV, publication list (when applicable) and a list of references (with contact information). Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled. Applications received by 15 September 2026 will receive full consideration; applications received after that date may be considered until the position is filled.

The Max Planck Society is committed to employing more disabled individuals and especially encourages them to apply. The Max Planck Society strives for gender and diversity equality. We welcome applications from all backgrounds.

We are looking forward to your application!

Working students are students who are enrolled at a University or some other institution of higher education, and who are employed in a reasonably long, fixed-term position parallel to their studies. This position must not be confused with an internship or with the possibility of writing a final thesis.

This employment usually takes place directly on the company's premises. A working student's main focus remains on their studies, which is why, during term-time, working students are not allowed to work more than 20 hours per week.

Working students therefore usually work near their place of study, so as to conveniently combine studying and employment.

jobs.description:
Snapshot of Your Day 

Our Industrial Cybersecurity department is seeking a highly qualified and driven industrial cybersecurity specialist to support vulnerability management efforts within the Product and Solutions domain. As an Industrial Cybersecurity Specialist, you will play a critical role in ensuring the security posture of wind power plants by proactively identifying and supporting the remediation of potential security risks.
You will become part of the Industrial Cybersecurity Technical Competence Center (TCC), a diverse and international team of experienced cybersecurity professionals supporting the business and development teams in securing systems by default across Product and Solutions, Manufacturing IT and Business managed IT.
In this role you will play a key role in supporting and enhancing the vulnerability management process to strengthen the security posture of company’s products and solutions. 

How You’ll Make an Impact 

* Driving and continuously improving the vulnerability management process.
* Staying up to date with emerging security threats, vulnerabilities, and industry best practices to continuously improve our vulnerability management program.
* Assessing identified vulnerabilities by analyzing their severity, exploitability, and relevance to our company’s products and solutions.
* Collaborating with cross-functional teams to define and implement effective remediation strategies and action plans.
* Supporting the development of mitigation plans to address vulnerabilities by applying patches, implementing alternative safeguards, or facilitating risk acceptance decisions.
* Advising stakeholders on security best practices and providing recommendations for effective vulnerability treatment.
* Reporting on vulnerability findings, remediation efforts, and overall security posture to senior management and relevant stakeholders.

What You Bring

* A university degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Computer Science, or a comparable field
* Profound experience in cybersecurity, product security or OT security, preferebly in the energy sectore. Experience with widely recognized OT cybersecurity standards, including ISA/IEC 62443, NIST SP 800-82, and ISO 27001 is preferred. Experience with regulatory compliance requirements specific to OT environments (e.g., NIS2 NERC CIP, EU Cyber Resilience Act) is highly welcome.
* Deep expertise in vulnerability management, including conducting assessments, performing security testing, and developing remediation strategies
* Deep understanding of common security vulnerabilities, attack vectors, and exploitation techniques. Hands-on experience with industry-standard vulnerability scanning techniques and tools (e.g., Nessus, Qualys, Burp Suite, OWASP ZAP)
* Familiarity with industry-standard SCA and SAST techniques and tools (BlackDuck, Snyk, SonarQube). Knowledge and experience with SCADA and Industrial Control Systems is preferred.
* Fluency in English and excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate across functions and convey technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders
* Relevant cybersecurity certifications such as CEH, OSCP, PNPT, GICSP, ISA/IEC 62443 Cybersecurity Expert are highly welcome.

About the Team

Our Global Functions are essential in driving the company's strategic initiatives and ensuring operational excellence across various departments, business areas, and regions. These roles support our vision to become the most valued energy technology company in the world. As part of our team, you contribute to our vision by shaping the global energy transition, partnering with our internal and external stakeholders, and conducting business responsibly and in compliance with legal requirements and regulations.

Who is Siemens Energy? 

At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. With ~100.000 dedicated employees in more than 90 countries, we develop the energy systems of the future, ensuring that the growing energy demand of the global community is met reliably and sustainably. The technologies created in our research departments and factories drive the energy transition and provide the base for one sixth of the world's electricity generation.

Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation.      

Find out how you can make a difference at Siemens Energy: https://www.siemens-energy.com/employeevideo

Our Commitment to Diversity 

Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity we generate power. We run on inclusion and our combined creative energy is fueled by over 130 nationalities. Siemens Energy celebrates character – no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability. We energize society, all of society, and we do not discriminate based on our differences. 

Rewards/Benefits 

* In addition to an attractive and competitive compensation package, you can expect a generous employer-funded retirement plan.
* We also offer the opportunity to become a shareholder in Siemens Energy at very favorable employee rates.
* Under our motto #BetterTogether, we provide our employees with the flexibility to work remotely or in the office. Our workspaces are designed to inspire collaboration and creativity, ensuring a fulfilling work environment.
* We are deeply committed to the professional and personal development of our employees.
* You will have the opportunity to learn and grow at your own pace, with access to a variety of appealing programs and initiatives.
* To support work-life balance, we offer a diverse range of options, including flexible working hours, childcare facilities at many locations, opportunities for part-time work, and even sabbaticals.

We value equal opportunities and welcome applications from people with disabilities.

This employment usually takes place directly on the company's premises. A working student's main focus remains on their studies, which is why, during term-time, working students are not allowed to work more than 20 hours per week.

jobs.description:
About us

Airbus pioneers sustainable aerospace for a safe and united world. The Company constantly innovates to provide efficient and technologically-advanced solutions in aerospace, defence, and connected services. In commercial aircraft, Airbus offers modern and fuel-efficient airliners and associated services. Airbus is also a European leader in defence and security and one of the world's leading space businesses. In helicopters, Airbus provides the most efficient civil and military rotorcraft solutions and services worldwide.
Job description

In order to support the Gust Loads & Aeroelastics department, Airbus Operations is looking for a

Master student (d/f/m) in the field of Aerodynamics in the Gust Loads & Aeroelastics department

You are looking for a master thesis and want to get to know the work of a job title? Then apply now! We look forward to you supporting us in the Gust Loads & Aeroelastics department as a master student (d/f/m)!

- Location: Hamburg
- Start: 01.06.2025
- Duration: 6 months

Your opportunity

- Are you passionate about aircraft physics?
- Are you keen to master the way we compute external loads acting on the vehicle due to maneuvers, flight in turbulence, landing impact, ground-handling?
- Do you like to work in an empowered manner?
- Do you enjoy connecting people and collaborating with many different interfaces?
- This job will give you the opportunity to work internationally with several internal flight physics departments and with teams located in Europe and India.

About us

We are a team of 16 multicultural and passionate engineers who perform the gust calculations for overall aircraft design for all aircraft types. Our team is involved from a very early design stage until certification and also in-service support. We are responsible for running build model activities such as finite element modeling, creating mass and aerodynamics models. We perform gust loads calculation, including failure cases, and deliver to internal interfaces. On top, we are deeply involved in research and technology aspects with new aircraft configuration assessments, model based system engineering, automation and machine learning.

Introduction

The current industry approaches of modeling unsteady aerodynamic flow for the prediction of gust loads typically assume linear flow conditions. Linearity greatly reduces the computational time required to evaluate all the flight points and gust conditions required by the certification specifications (CS-25). At the same time, disregarding non-linearities such as boundary layer separation arising from the high angles of attack induced by strong gusts can lead to an over-estimation of loads and thus to an increased structural weight of the aircraft.

Your location

You will be working at the largest production site for civil aircraft situated in Hamburg. Its location on the southern banks of the river Elbe includes the option to commute by ferry. Experience the special flair of Hamburg in your spare time where vibrant cosmopolitan culture meets nautic legacy.

Your benefits

- Work-life balance with a 35-hour week (flexitime).
- International environment with the opportunity to network globally.
- Work with modern/diversified technologies.
- At Airbus, we see you as a valuable team member and you are not hired to brew coffee, instead you are in close contact with the interfaces and are part of our weekly team meetings.
- Opportunity to participate in the Generation Airbus Community to expand your own network.

Your tasks and responsibilities

During this six months Master thesis you will develop and evaluate an unsteady aerodynamic model that includes the effect of flow separation in a piecewise linear approach. The model will be built using linearized computational fluid dynamics (CFD) of a complete flexible aircraft and adapted using aerodynamic data obtained in the non-linear flow region at high angles of attack. You will evaluate the model by comparison against higher-fidelity models, such as obtained from non-linear time domain simulation, with respect to gust loads.

You will contribute to:

- Optimize the design of Airbus commercial aircraft in the frame of new wing technologies
- the development of new approaches to model unsteady aerodynamics considering non-linearities for gust loads and flutter computation
- Actively support us as a new member of our team on our journey

Desired skills and qualifications

- You are a fulltime enrolled master student (d/f/m) within Engineering, Mechanical Engineering or equivalent
- You have good knowledge in aerodynamics, CFD and potential flows
- Ideally you already have first experience in CFD using TAU or CODA
- You have knowledge in coding using Python and/or Matlab
- You bring basic knowledge in overall aircraft design and basic competencies in flight loads calculation and flight mechanics
- You are passionate to understand physical aspects and to use your engineering judgement
- If you are familiar with tools like MSC.NASTRAN or ALTAIR HyperWorks, this is beneficial
- You are a highly motivated, proactive and open-minded person with a great sense of initiative
- You are keen to deepen your technical knowledge while enjoying to work in a multicultural team
- Your English is at negotiating level

Please upload the following documents: cover letter, CV, relevant transcripts, enrollment certificate.

With a tradition spanning more than 600 years, the Faculty of Medicine at Leipzig University is one of the largest research institutions in the Leipzig region. With more than 1.300 employees, it is the largest of the university's 14 faculties and provides training for approximately 3,500 students in human medicine and dentistry as well as pharmacy and midwifery. The Faculty of Medicine was founded in 1415, making it one of the oldest medical faculties in Germany with an unbroken tradition of teaching.
PhD Position - Craniofacial Biology and PTEN-Dependent Tissue Homeostasis
The research group "Cranio- and Orofacial Development" (https://research.uni-leipzig.de/petersen_lab/) at Leipzig University Medical Center (UKL) offers a PhD position within a DFG-funded collaborative project investigating PTEN-dependent craniofacial tissue homeostasis. The project is particularly suited to candidates interested in craniofacial and skeletal biology, molecular signaling, spatial omics, and metabolism.
Project Background
PTEN is a central regulator of PI3K-AKT signaling and coordinates cell growth, metabolism, and tissue homeostasis. The project investigates how loss of PTEN in the osteoblast lineage alters the postnatal craniofacial complex. The PhD project will focus on teeth and their supporting periodontal tissues, alveolar and craniofacial bone, and the temporomandibular joint (TMJ). Using an inducible postnatal genetic mouse model, we aim to determine how PTEN-dependent signaling changes tissue architecture, bone remodeling, cellular states, and molecular programs. A complementary part of the project will investigate the associated adipose/metabolic phenotype in close collaboration with Dr. Antje Garten and her group from the Molecular Endocrinology at the Center for Pediatric Research (https://research.uni-leipzig.de/garten_lab/).
The PhD candidate will investigate

- PTEN-dependent changes in teeth and periodontal tissues, craniofacial and alveolar bone, and the TMJ
- Cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying altered bone remodeling and craniofacial tissue homeostasis after postnatal PTEN deletion
- Spatially resolved tissue responses and their relationship to PTEN-associated adipose/metabolic changes

Methods and Approaches
The project combines state-of-the-art experimental and computational techniques, including:

- Inducible transgenic mouse models and genetic reporter systems
- Histology, immunofluorescence, advanced microscopy, and micro-computed tomography
- Spatial transcriptomics of dental, periodontal, bone, and TMJ tissues
- Molecular biology, quantitative image analysis, proteomic integration, and bioinformatic analyses

Candidate Profile
We are looking for a highly motivated candidate with:

- Master of Science degree or a Diploma in Biology, Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Biotechnology, Bioinformatics or Chemistry
- Interest in craniofacial biology, mechanobiology, or regenerative medicine
- Experience in molecular biology, cell biology, animal models, and/or bioinformatics
- Strong motivation to work in an international and interdisciplinary research environment
- Good communication skills and proficiency in English

Research Environment
The project is embedded in the Department of Orthodontics at Leipzig University Medical Center. Our research focuses on craniofacial biology, tooth and periodontal tissue homeostasis, skeletal remodeling, genetic mouse models, advanced imaging, and spatial omics. The collaboration with Dr. Antje Garten provides complementary expertise in PTEN biology, metabolism, and adipose tissue, enabling the PhD candidate to connect local craniofacial phenotypes with systemic metabolic alterations.

The WIRTGEN GROUP, a Deere & Company business, is a global leader in road construction and materials processing equipment, serving customers through five established product brands and an international network of manufacturing, sales, service, and dealer operations. As part of Deere & Company, WIRTGEN GROUP combines its deep industry expertise, strong customer relationships, and distinct business heritage with Deere’s global capabilities, values, and commitment to integrity. WIRTGEN GROUP and Deere operate within a shared Ethics and Compliance function, supported by common program expectations, systems, policies, and standards of ethical business conduct.

Deere and Company’s Global Ethics and Compliance department is looking for a

Compliance Manager (m/f/d) 

The Compliance Manager serves as the primary Ethics and Compliance partner for WIRTGEN GROUP globally, helping foster a culture of integrity, collaboration, and responsible business conduct across a complex international organization. The role operates as a broad-based compliance generalist, providing practical guidance and support across the full spectrum of ethics and compliance matters. Working closely with WIRTGEN GROUP stakeholders and businesses and the broader Deere and Company Ethics and Compliance team, this role supports compliance program implementation, risk management, stakeholder engagement, and the continued alignment of WIRTGEN GROUP into Deere and Company’s enterprise compliance framework.  The position is located in WIRTGEN GROUP’s headquarters, based in Windhagen, Germany.

Your Responsibilities: 

- Serve as the primary Compliance Manager supporting WIRTGEN GROUP globally, acting as the strategic interface on compliance risks, program expectations, regulatory matters, and alignment with Deere and Company’s Ethics and Compliance strategy
- Provide practical, business-oriented compliance guidance across a broad range of matters, including but not limited to: anti-bribery and anti-corruption, fraud risk, third-party relationships, trade compliance, conflicts of interest, gifts and entertainment, training, policy and regulatory interpretation, and employee questions or concerns.
- Implement, maintain, monitor, and manage compliance program elements for WIRTGEN GROUP, including policies, controls, third-party risk management activities, training, communications, monitoring, and reporting processes.

- Partner with business leaders and functional stakeholders to identify, assess, prioritize, and mitigate compliance risks, translating those risks into practical recommendations and actions.

- Develop and support risk-based compliance training, communications, monitoring activities, management reporting, and continuous improvement initiatives.
- Build and maintain strong relationships with WIRTGEN GROUP and Deere stakeholders, providing guidance, coaching, and support while promoting a culture of integrity, ethical behavior, transparency, and accountability.

What Skills You Need: 

- At least 5 years of practical experience working as a compliance specialist, compliance manager, or similar professional supporting a company’s broader ethics and compliance needs.
- Experience supporting or managing multiple elements of a corporate ethics and compliance program, such as risk assessment, training and communications, policy guidance, conflicts of interest, gifts and entertainment, anti-bribery and anti-corruption, third-party risk management, fraud risk, trade compliance, monitoring, or reporting.
- Ability to operate as a compliance generalist, recognize issues across different compliance disciplines, provide sound initial guidance, and engage subject-matter specialists when appropriate.

- Ability to build relationships, establish credibility, and influence stakeholders across multiple cultures, business functions, organizational levels, and regions.

What Makes You Stand Out:

- Experience conducting compliance risk assessments, developing risk mitigation plans, and monitoring remediation activities.
- Experience developing or delivering compliance training, communications, monitoring activities, dashboards, and management reporting.
- Ability to influence senior leaders and drive change through collaboration, credibility, and trust.
- Experience in process optimization and continuous improvement initiatives.

Education: 

Ideally you will have a degree or equivalent related work experience in the following:

- Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent level in Business Administration, Law, Compliance, Risk Management, Finance, Accounting, Public Policy, or a related field

jobs.occupation: 100% Remote Customer Success Manager – Hotel SaaS Platform (Hospitality Industry, DE & EN) (Account-Manager/in)
jobs.description:
Company Overview

Hotel Res Bot is a fast-growing company helping hotels and travel agencies automate their inbound communications using self-trained AI.

Our platform is designed specifically for reservation and group sales teams, helping them manage and respond to high volumes of inbound email communication more efficiently and consistently.

We integrate with hotel systems such as PMS and booking engines, but our core focus is improving how hotel teams handle guest and group requests via email in their daily operations.

We are a small, international team working in a trust-based, remote-first environment where ownership, clarity, and direct communication matter more than hierarchy.

Job Summary

This is a client success role focused on helping hotel reservation and group sales teams adopt new ways of working, integrate our system into their daily operations, and build long-term, trusted relationships.

You will act as the main point of contact for your clients and ensure the system becomes part of their day-to-day workflow, particularly in how they manage and respond to inbound emails, enquiries, and group requests.

The role is about driving real usage and long-term value in operational environments — not sales and not technical implementation.

You should understand how hotels operate, especially reservation or sales departments, and be comfortable working with hotel systems and communication workflows.

Attitude & Culture

Since this is a fully remote position within a small but close-knit international team, we place strong importance on finding someone who is comfortable working independently, communicating clearly, and taking ownership of their responsibilities.

We work in a trust-based, non-micromanaged environment. You have flexibility in how and when you work, and in return we expect reliability, accountability, and good judgement in managing your clients and responsibilities.

Support and collaboration are always available when needed, but this role is best suited to someone who is proactive, organised, and comfortable operating with a high level of autonomy.

We also place strong value on a healthy team and error culture. We focus on learning and improving together rather than assigning blame. Open, respectful communication is essential to us — disagreement is welcome, but personal attacks are not. Maintaining a constructive and collaborative environment is especially important in a fully remote company.

Your Impact

Client Success & Adoption

- Own relationships with hotel reservation and group sales teams
- Support teams in integrating the system into daily email-based workflows
- Ensure clients are actively using the platform in real operational settings
- Conduct regular online check-ins and occasional onsite visits (day trips)
- Identify gaps in adoption and proactively improve usage and engagement

The Voice of the Customer

- Act as the main bridge between hotel operations and our internal team
- Translate real operational challenges into structured, actionable feedback
- Ensure the system reflects how hotels actually manage guest and group communication in practice
- Help improve workflows, messaging, and configurations based on real-world usage

Relationship Ownership

- Build and maintain long-term, trusted relationships with hotel teams
- Monitor usage, engagement, and operational success over time
- Ensure clients consistently gain value from improved communication workflows
- Maintain accurate and structured records of client interactions and activity

Internal Collaboration

- Work closely with support, product, and technical teams
- Support smooth handovers from onboarding and implementation
- Contribute to improving internal processes based on real client feedback

Who You Are

The Hotel Operator

- 2–3 years experience in: - hotel reservations department, OR
- group sales department, OR
- front office with strong email handling responsibility
- Strong understanding of how hotel reservation and group email workflows operate in practice

The Communicator

- Fluent in German (C1 / business level – required)
- Fluent in English (required)
- Spanish is a plus, but not required
- Able to communicate clearly with both operational teams (e.g. reservations, group sales) and senior hotel or HQ management, adapting the message to the audience while keeping clarity and structure
- Comfortable proactively engaging with clients via email, phone, or online calls when needed to support adoption and ensure effective daily use of the system
- Able to help align day-to-day usage with longer-term operational goals and ensure the system is delivering value across both operational and management levels

Tech-Aware (but not technical)

- Understanding of hotel systems such as: - PMS
- Booking engines
- Channel managers (basic understanding)
- Comfortable learning and working with digital tools used for client management and reporting
- No coding required, but confident working with structured systems and workflows

Project Management (Nice to Have)

- Previous experience in project coordination or project management, or relevant training/certification, is a plus
- Comfortable coordinating tasks, tracking progress, and following up with different stakeholders to keep activities on schedule
- Able to manage multiple client priorities while maintaining clear communication and structured documentation

Ownership Mindset

- Works independently and takes responsibility for outcomes
- Structured, reliable, and proactive
- Identifies issues early and acts before escalation is needed

Growth & Development

This role offers clear long-term development opportunities into:

- Senior Customer Success roles
- Implementation / Operations Lead roles
- Product-facing or solution-focused positions
- Closer collaboration with product and operational strategy

We actively support learning, ownership, and internal progression.

Benefits

- 100% remote work environment
- Flexible working hours
- Flat hierarchy and direct access to decision-makers
- Supportive international team culture
- Opportunity to grow with a fast-growing company
- Company-provided equipment (Laptop + screen + keyboard + mouse)

How to Apply

Please send your CV and a short cover letter explaining:

- Your experience in hotel reservations or group sales
- Your experience handling high volumes of guest or group emails
- Why you are interested in hotel communication automation and operational improvement
- Your language skills and eligibility to work in Spain or Portugal

Please send applications to:
career@hotelresbot.com

Equal Opportunity Statement

Hotel Res Bot is an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and are committed to creating a respectful, inclusive, and collaborative environment for all employees.

jobs.occupation: Research Scientist and Curator (m/f/d)  of the section Vertebrata (Tenure Track) (Biologe/Biologin)
jobs.description:
Senckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at the Senckenberg Museum of Natural History in Görlitz, ideally as of April 1, 2027:

Research Scientist and Curator (m/f/d) of the section Vertebrata (Tenure Track)

(full time / part time options available)

Location: Görlitz

Employment scope: full time / part time options are available

Type of contract: initially limited to three years;

the type of time limitation depends on individual profile and legal framework (maximum 3+3 years). A permanent employment is planned after a positive evaluation

Remuneration: collective agreement of the German Länder, TV-L E13

The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.

The renowned Senckenberg Museum of Natural History, located in the medieval town of Görlitz, combines research at an international level with extensive collections and an engaging museum programme. The surrounding Upper Lusatia region offers a large variety of opportunities for experiencing nature.

Senckenberg is committed to study the causes and effects of biodiversity loss in the Anthropocene. As part of our strategic development, we launched an ambitious long-term research effort in “Anthropocene Biodiversity Loss” encompassing the modules “Collectomics”, “Biodiversity Genomics”, and “Solution Labs”. Objectives include the transformation of natural history collections into the digital era, studying biodiversity from the genome to the ecosystem levels and offering exploratory spaces for science and society to develop common solutions to Anthropocene challenges.

For the Görlitz vertebrate collection, which comprises approximately 70,000 specimens (preserved using dry, cryogenic, and liquid preservation methods, with the focus on mammals; birds make up a smaller proportion, while other vertebrate groups represent only a small fraction), we are seeking an internationally recognized scientist with a solid track record in mammal research, possibly supplemented by work on another vertebrate groups.

Potential research topics may include various aspects such as mammalian diversity, functional morphology, phylogeny, or biological interactions. Curation and collection-based research should play a significant role in the applicant’s research approach. The selected candidate should be open to research collaborations with SGN colleagues

Your tasks

- Scientific curation and development of the vertebrate collection and the associated resources as an important international research infrastructure through international networking, growth, and improved accessibility.
- Develop a visible portfolio of collection-based research with basic and applied aspects in the broad field of mammalogy and possibly other vertebrate groups by using a range of established and innovative methods and approaches.
- Taking responsibility for the relocation of the collection items, including the infrastructure of the Mammalogy/Vertebrate Section, to the new campus at Bahnhofstraße 30 at Görlitz.
- Secure external research funds.
- Publish results of your research in international scientific outlets.
- Establish collaborations with ongoing projects, regional and national (region (e.g., long-term projects on wolf, lynx) and international (e.g., Africa, Mongolia), including with other sections and departments in Görlitz and further Senckenberg institutes.
- Communicate with external stakeholders such as scientific associations, conservation agencies, local and regional authorities, as well as citizen scientists.
- Participate in teaching in the MSc level programmes of International Institute Zittau/ Dresden University of Technology.

Your profile

- Doctoral degree in biology/zoology or a related field
- Expert knowledge of mammals, including native species (the biogeographic focus of the mammal collection is currently the Palearctic), additional expertise in other vertebrate groups
- Proactive willingness to implement innovative research approaches, such as in the field of genomics, morphometrics, AI, imaging, 3D methods, pollutant analysis in a collection context
- Ability to identify attractive research questions and make use of synergies through collaborations
- Excellent academic track record adequate to your career stage
- Experience in the acquisition of third-party funding and project management
- Experience in supervising staff (doctoral candidates, BSc., MSc., students, technical staff), ability to work in a team
- Very good command of German (B2)
- Fluency in English, both spoken and written
- Class B driving licence (international driving licence)
- Willingness to travel on occasion to the extent possible considering your personal circumstances

Desirable skills

- Knowledge in molecular, biochemical or biophysical techniques in taxonomy and ecology
- Knowledge in research data management and databases
- Experience in curation and management of zoological collections, and in museum work

We offer

- Access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations
- An attractive job within the inspiring and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution with excellent infrastructures and collaborations opportunities, e. g. in morphology, genomics, evolutionary biology, (paleo-)ecology
- A working place in completely new building with dissection and other laboratories, collection rooms, in the historic town of Görlitz with rapidly developing local research community (DZA, CASUS, IHI/TUD, HiLusatia), yet situated very close to nature with high mammal diversity and opportunities for field work
- Opportunities to participate in teaching and outreach activities, e.g., in our museum and with collaborating universities
- Opportunities for establishing an independent academic working group and acquiring further academic qualifications
- Flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension plan

Senckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Women are particularly encouraged to apply as they are underrepresented in the field of this position; in the case of equal qualifications and suitability, they will be given preference. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.

How to apply?

Please upload your application (letter of motivation with a short description of your previous and current research foci, a CV, certificates of academic achievements, list of publications as well as letter(s) of recommendation, if available) as a single PDF file by November 10, 2026.https://www.senckenberg.de/de/stellenanzeigen/

For data protection information on the processing of personal data as part of the application and selection process, please refer to the privacy policy on our homepage at https://www.senckenberg.de/en/imprint/

For further information about the Senckenberg Gesellschaft für Naturforschung please visit www.senckenberg.de

Contact

Senckenberg Gesellschaft für Naturforschung

Senckenberganlage 25

60325 Frankfurt a.M.

For specific questions about this role please contact Prof. Dr. Hjalmar S. Kühl.

E-Mail hjalmar.kuehl@senckenberg.de

The Institute of Radiochemistry and Experimental Molecular Imaging (IREMB) is seeking a postdoctoral researcher for a translational research project in the field of radiopharmaceutical tracer development and molecular imaging. The postdoc position will initially be embedded for one year in the internationally funded IMAGESTRO project. There is an option of extension for another year. The focus of the work will be on the biological validation of newly developed PET or SPECT radiotracers.
The IMAGESTRO project aims to develop novel 18F-labeled PET tracers for the non-invasive imaging of estrogen receptors in the brain, to characterize them preclinically, and to translate them into human applications. jobs.description:
The University Medical Center Schleswig-Holstein (UKSH) combines world-class international research with interdisciplinary patient care. We are the state's only comprehensive care provider and its largest employer. Our approximately 17,500 employees ensure highly personalized care—which is indispensable for the people of Schleswig-Holstein.
The University Hospital Schleswig-Holstein (UKSH) with its locations in Kiel and Lübeck is one of the largest medical care centers in Europe. It serves to warrant maximum medical care in the northernmost federal state and guarantees medical-technical care at the highest level, especially for patients who require highly differentiated diagnosis and therapy. The unique feature of university medicine is the interaction of health care, research and teaching with the result that scientific findings flow directly into the health system.

Our research aims to develop novel diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for chronic inflammatory diseases, including inflammatory bowel, liver, lung and skin diseases. To achieve this, we investigate the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying immune regulation in different disease contexts and employ state-of-the-art technologies to comprehensively characterize human immune cells, with a particular focus on antigen-specific CD4+ T cells. A major focus of our research is the integration of high-dimensional single-cell and immune repertoire data. Our group combines enrichment of rare antigen-specific CD4+ T cells with multidimensional flow cytometry, single-cell RNA sequencing, T cell receptor sequencing and ATAC sequencing to investigate cellular states, immune cell differentiation, clonality and regulatory mechanisms in health and disease.

As a PhD student / postdoctoral researcher in bioinformatics, you will be an integral part of the research activities within our group. You will develop and pursue independent research projects and also contribute to a broad range of collaborative projects involving different members of the group. Your work will focus on the computational analysis, integration and interpretation of high-dimensional sequencing data, with particular emphasis on:

- Analysis of single-cell RNA sequencing, T cell receptor sequencing, and ATAC sequencing data
- Integration of transcriptomic, TCR, epigenetic and flow cytometry data to characterize immune cell states and regulatory mechanisms
- Development and application of reproducible bioinformatics workflows and analysis pipelines, including data visualization and interpretation
- Active contribution to diverse collaborative projects within the group, including the planning and design of computational analyses in close interaction with experimental scientists

Start in our team:
Join our research team starting from February 1st 2027. The position is initially limited to two years, with the possibility of extension. We are looking forward to welcoming you as part of our team with all your skills and commitment.

What we offer:

- Salary will be according to the German salary scale TV-L (German TV-L E13, PhD student 65%, Postdoc 100%)
- A full-time position, currently 38,5 hours/week; part-time employment may be compatible within the framework of certain working time models
- Exceptional technical infrastructure especially for multi-dimensional flow-cytometry and for next generation sequencing at the the Institute of Medical Immunology and the Center of Molecular Biosciences (ZMB)
- You can find more exciting benefits offered by the UKSH here:Benefits (uksh.de)

What you can expect:

- A fascinating research environment for the investigation of basic processes of human immune reactions with direct implications for immune-mediated diseases
- A systematic training to work independently in a challenging and diversified research field
- The opportunity to work in a dedicated, supportive and international research team
- An extensive pool of sophisticated methods and complex laboratory instruments

Whatyou bring with you:
University degree (Master's or equivalent) in bioinformatics, computational biology, biology, biostatistics, data science or a related field; completed PhD required for postdoctoral positions

Strong interest in single-cell omics, immunology and computational analysis of biological data

Experience with next-generation sequencing technologies (e.g. scRNA-seq, TCR-seq or ATAC-seq) is desirable

Good programming skills in R and/or Python, including the development, adaptation and documentation of computational workflows

High degree of commitment, independence, organizational skills and responsibility, along with strong communication skills in English and the ability to collaborate effectively with experimental and clinical teams

We look forward to receiving your application (CV, motivation letter stating research and career interests, copies of education certificates, and two letters of recommendation) by 29.10.2026; please include job posting number 29445.
