jobs.description:
Shape compliance. Drive governance. Protect global business.
 

At DHL Group, we connect people and improve lives through our global logistics network. Behind our world-leading operations stands a strong commitment to governance, compliance, and risk management. We are looking for an experienced Manager of Insurance Tax, Regulation & Compliance Germany (m/f/d) to play a pivotal role in ensuring that our insurance activities remain compliant, transparent, and future-ready. This position combines insurance taxation, regulatory compliance, governance, and stakeholder management in a highly international environment.
 

Manager of Insurance Tax, Regulation & Compliance Germany (m/f/d)
   

Why experienced insurance professionals join this role
* Move from advising to owning insurance governance decisions.
* Shape multinational insurance programs across a global organization.
* Influence strategic decisions involving Tax, Legal, Treasury, Procurement, and Risk Management.
* Work at the intersection of insurance, regulation, governance, and business strategy.
* Gain exposure to some of the most complex international insurance arrangements in the market.

 

You'll make an impact by:
* Defining and evolving DHL Group's global insurance governance framework.
* Ensuring regulatory excellence across international insurance programs.
* Leading complex tax, regulatory, and compliance initiatives.
* Managing interactions with authorities, regulators, auditors, brokers, and insurers.
* Providing strategic guidance on multinational insurance structures and cross-border risk solutions.

 

What You Will Do:

Insurance Tax & Compliance
* Serve as the central expert for insurance premium tax matters in Germany.
* Advise business stakeholders on insurance taxation, insurance distribution compliance, and regulatory requirements.
* Assess domestic and international insurance programs, including multinational insurance structures, global master policies, local policies, captive insurance arrangements, and Freedom of Services (FOS) solutions.
* Review and evaluate insurance premium tax treatment for insurance contracts and insurance-related services.
* Support the design, implementation, and launch of new insurance programs while ensuring tax and regulatory compliance. Governance & Risk Management

* Maintain and continuously improve insurance tax governance and compliance frameworks.
* Design and oversee internal control systems for insurance premium tax processes.
* Contribute to the enhancement of DHL Group's Tax Compliance Management System.
* Conduct risk assessments and compliance reviews related to insurance distribution and taxation.
* Promote transparency, documentation standards, and audit readiness across the organization. 

 

Regulatory & Audit Management
* Manage insurance premium tax audits and regulatory reviews independently.
* Act as the primary contact for tax authorities, auditors, legal advisors, insurers, and brokers.
* Develop strategies to address audit findings and mitigate regulatory risks.
* Monitor developments in German and international insurance tax legislation and relevant court decisions.
* Ensure regulatory awareness and compliance regarding insurance distribution activities in Germany.

 

Cross-Functional Collaboration
* Work closely with colleagues from Tax, Legal, Treasury, Procurement, Risk Management, and other business functions.
* Support DHL business units in understanding and meeting insurance compliance requirements.
* Coordinate with external advisors, brokers, insurers, and regulatory stakeholders across multiple jurisdictions.

 

What You Bring
* University degree in Law, Tax, Business Administration, Finance, Insurance, Risk Management, or a related field.
* Several years of professional experience in insurance taxation, insurance regulation, compliance, risk management, legal, or related disciplines.
* Proven expertise in German Insurance Premium Tax (IPT) regulations and insurance compliance requirements.
* Experience managing regulatory inquiries, audits, disputes, and complex multinational insurance programs.
* Strong understanding of commercial insurance products, including Property, Liability, Marine, Cargo, Cyber, D&O, Financial Lines, and Employee Benefits.
* Experience developing governance, control, and compliance frameworks in international organizations.
* Excellent English language skills and good German language proficiency.

 

Who You Are

You are a strategic and analytical professional who enjoys navigating complex regulatory environments. You combine technical expertise with strong stakeholder management skills and are comfortable advising senior decision-makers. You thrive in international settings, communicate effectively, and maintain the highest standards of integrity and quality.
 

What We Offer
* A highly visible role with global impact across one of the world's leading logistics companies.
* Exposure to complex international insurance, tax, and compliance topics.
* Opportunities to collaborate with senior stakeholders across multiple functions and regions.
* A diverse, inclusive, and collaborative working environment.
* Continuous professional development and career growth opportunities within DHL Group.(Employer value proposition formulated based on the role's global scope and responsibilities.)

 

Why DHL Group?

At DHL Group, we are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone can contribute and grow. We value diverse perspectives and believe that our people are the key to our success. Employment decisions are based on qualifications, skills, experience, and performance.
 

Your benefits
 
* Well-Being: Fun, team spirit, and health are crucial factors. Therefore, within the company, we offer a wide range of health and preventive care services, an occupational physician
* Family-friendly: The compatibility of family and work has many facets, such as childcare, care for family members, etc. We support this, for example, through kindergarten places as well as the Betreuungs- und Erholungswerk (support and recreation program).
* Employee Share Program: As an employee, you have the opportunity to participate in DHL Group's employee share program and share directly in the company's long-term success.
* Mobility: We move not only letters or parcels but also our employees through offerings such as company bicycles, job tickets and possibly company cars.
* Location: The Post Campus brings together people from more than 60 countries. The Post Tower is easily accessible by car, public transportation and bicycle. To facilitate the workday, the campus offers amenities such as parking spaces, post office, café, canteen and more.
* Onboarding: Individual onboarding, training on the job, networking, a dedicated certified program, etc., lay the foundation for a successful start at DHL Group.
* Development opportunities: We offer numerous development opportunities through a comprehensive training landscape, junior talent programs, coaching etc.
* Social commitment: Through global corporate programs, we improve the educational and career opportunities for young people and engage in disaster management at airports. We also contribute to local environmental protection and aid projects initiated by employees on a voluntary basis.
* What else? Company pension plan, social counseling, inclusion consulting, cleaning service, insurance cooperation, corporate discounts, events, sabbaticals and much more!

 

About DHL Group

DHL Group is the world’s leading logistics company, connecting people and businesses in more than 220 countries and territories through a comprehensive portfolio of logistics, e-commerce, parcel, express, freight forwarding, and supply chain management services.

With approximately 580,000 employees worldwide, DHL Group operates one of the largest global logistics networks.

Our purpose is simple: Connecting People. Improving Lives.
 

Apply now with your complete documents, stating your salary expectations, using the application button.
 

For further information, please visit careers.dhl.com. For initial personal contact and any questions, please contact Sven Rötzel at sven.roetzel@dhl.com or 0228-189-52128.
 

We look forward to receiving your application*.

CONNECTING PEOPLE. IMPROVING LIVES.
 

*At DHL Group, applications from all individuals are welcome, regardless of age, gender, origin, religion or physical attributes.

Who We Are 🌍

Limatica measures what batteries whisper. We turn the tiny voltage noise of battery cells into a quality verdict, far faster than conventional tests, and help cell manufacturers cut scrap.

We are a team of twelve in Chemnitz, spanning data, ML, HPC, hardware and industrialization. Early adopters across Europe and Asia already use our technology. In 2026 we move from pilots to production lines, and our data grows faster than our team.

What You'll Do 🔧

Our measurement stations produce several hundred GB of high-resolution voltage data per hour. You own the step from raw signal to reliable answer.

- Work with novel cell noise data: Derive features from raw time series that make physical sense that hold up in production
- Build for streaming: Design feature computations that work in streaming mode, at a throughput of up to 10,000 measurements per hour.
- **Make throughput a design decision:**Build modular, parameterizable nodes for our distributed processing pipeline and help bring them into our Rust-based production environment.
- **Ship modules, not scripts:**Automate evaluations end to end, from raw data to reports for our engineering team and our customers.
- Own customer projects technically: Assess requirements, communicate interim results and findings, and turn feedback into improvements.

What You Bring 🕵️

- Measurement experience: A degree in electrical engineering (or comparable) and 3+ years with real-world measurement data. Sampling, noise, filtering and artifacts you know from practice, not just lectures.
- Physical intuition: You can explain why a feature makes sense, and you prefer a simple, well-understood method over a model nobody can explain.
- Data at scale: You think in throughput: data formats, intermediate results, distributed and cached processing.
- Clean engineering: Python, Git, tests and CI/CD as a matter of course. No Rust expertise needed, but the will to learn it.
- Customer confidence: Fluent German and English, written and spoken. You explain results clearly to engineers and managers alike.

Why Limatica 🚀

- Real ownership: Your own part of the pipeline and your first customer project within months. As we grow, this role can grow into technical lead.
- Learn what few get to learn: Electrochemistry, Rust in production and data engineering at scale, with real cells and international manufacturers.
- Share the upside: Salary package including virtual stock options.
- Invest in yourself: Additional holiday for personal learning
- Flexibility & wellbeing: Flexible hours, hybrid work, further benefits via Guud Card

What it's like here: You get a lot of trust and a lot of room to shape things. We look for people who stay with a problem until it's solved and who enjoy the moments when a customer launch needs the whole team. Those are the moments where people here grow fastest. This role is intentionally a towards-senior position. You will take on increasing responsibility for pipeline modules and customer projects. Those who help shape the architecture and lead projects independently grow into a senior role with us.

CGM Leverages AI: We’re looking for people who feel the power of AI in the e-health environment, who want to help shape change, and who are driven by a curious passion to see how technology can make healthcare smarter, simpler, and better.

Together, we are shaping the healthcare system of the future. Become part of our mission and make a difference - for a world where knowledge saves lives!

You design and develop high-end C++ components for our medical desktop applications, with a strong focus on performance, stability, and scalability.

You architect, implement, and review complex multithreading and parallelization concepts to ensure efficient, safe, and responsive execution in everyday clinical use.

You analyze, refactor, and optimize our large existing codebase (QT, CMake, Conan, MSVC, and embedded CEF), identify bottlenecks, and systematically raise the performance and quality of long-lived products.

Several years of senior-level experience in professional C++ development, ideally in high-performance, highly parallelized desktop systems with significant ownership and end-to-end responsibility.

Excellent academic background with a completed university degree in computer science, mathematics, physics, electrical engineering, or a comparable technical discipline with very good grades.

A structured, analytical way of working, high-quality standards, strong problem-solving skills, innovation drive, proactive ownership and a pronounced sense of entrepreneurship with genuine enthusiasm for shaping the future of healthcare IT.

jobs.occupation: Scientific Project Coordinator (f/m/x) Environmental Data and AI Platform (DataMon) (IT-Projektkoordinator/in)
jobs.description:
© Kletr / Fotolia The Helmholtz Centre for Environmental Research
(UFZ) is a world-leading institution in environmental research and a
member of the Helmholtz Association, Germany’s largest scientific
organisation. With approximately 1,200 employees across Leipzig,
Halle, and Magdeburg, we have been conducting research since 1991
using a transdisciplinary approach to address the most pressing
challenges of our time: biodiversity loss, climate change, and
environmental pollution. Our goal is to translate excellent research
into practical solutions for policymakers, business, and society, and
to serve as a reliable partner in supporting transformation processes
toward a sustainable and just future for current and future
generations. We foster a culture of collaboration, openness, and
diversity within a work environment that actively promotes creativity
and personal development. Scientific Project Coordinator (f/m/x)
Environmental Data and AI Platform (DataMon) The job DataMon is a new
strategic UFZ initiative to build an integrated environmental data and
AI platform that brings together established monitoring products,
scientific data services and cross-domain analytical capabilities. The
platform will make UFZ data products more accessible, interoperable
and AI-ready, while creating new opportunities for integrated
environmental research and knowledge transfer. As Scientific Project
Coordinator, you will play a central role in turning this ambitious
interdisciplinary initiative into a coherent implementation process,
connecting scientific, technical and organisational perspectives
across UFZ and with external partners. Your tasks Establish and
maintain the integrated DataMon roadmap across the shared platform,
monitor and data-product modules, and cross-cutting AI and
spatial-computing services. Work closely with module leads to clarify
requirements, resolve dependencies and conflicts, prepare decisions,
agree on priorities and next steps, and ensure consistent follow-up
across the DataMon portfolio. Coordinate milestones, deliverables,
dependencies, resource requirements, risks and decisions across module
leads, research data management, IT, knowledge transfer, research
infrastructure units, technical working groups and external service
providers. Translate scientific and user needs into clear technical
and organisational requirements, identify reusable solutions and
synergies across modules, and align priorities, interfaces and
implementation pathways. Prepare and facilitate Steering Group
meetings, readiness reviews and cross-project workshops; draft
decision papers and ensure that agreed actions are followed up and,
where necessary, escalated. Establish and maintain project controls
for schedules, risks, changes, decisions, reporting and documentation,
and prepare concise status and management reports. Support the
procurement and commissioning of external development services,
coordinate service providers, and monitor deliverables, acceptance
criteria and knowledge transfer in close cooperation with the
responsible UFZ units. Coordinate the transition from project
implementation to sustainable operation, including responsibilities,
update cycles, quality assurance, maintenance requirements and user
support. We offer The freedom to master even the most demanding
challenges between basic research and practical application The chance
to work in interdisciplinary, international teams and benefit from a
variety of perspectives First class integration into national and
international research networks to work together on global challenges
Excellent research infrastructure and research data management to
optimally support your work Flexible working hours and a wide range of
options for balancing work and care responsibilities through our
family office Competent support and advice for international
colleagues arriving at the UFZ from the 'International Office' Special
annual payment, capital-forming benefits and subsidised Germany Job
Ticket A workplace in a vibrant region with a high life quality and
social and cultural diversity Your profile An academic degree at
master’s level or equivalent in environmental or natural sciences,
computer or data science, geoinformatics, engineering, science and
technology management, or a related field Several years of experience
managing complex, interdisciplinary digital, research-infrastructure,
software or data-platform projects, including multi-team roadmaps,
deliverables, dependencies, risks and reporting Proven ability to lead
through influence, create commitment across organisational boundaries,
address conflicts constructively, prepare and facilitate decisions,
and ensure consistent follow-up A strong technical understanding of
data platforms and software development, interfaces and APIs, data and
metadata workflows, FAIR principles, cloud or compute environments,
and AI-enabled services. Hands-on coding experience is welcome, but
not essential Excellent facilitation, presentation, negotiation and
writing skills, with the ability to communicate confidently with
researchers, IT specialists, management, stakeholders and external
service providers A structured, independent and outcome-oriented
working style, sound judgement in evolving and complex project
settings, and experience with agile or hybrid project management
approaches Very good written and spoken English and German Experience
with public procurement, contract deliverables or external service
provider management is an advantage The UFZ values diversity and is
actively committed to ensuring equal opportunities for all employees,
regardless of their origin, religion, beliefs, disability, age or
sexual identity. We welcome people who represent diverse backgrounds,
identities and perspectives. We therefore particularly encourage
people who are affected by structural discrimination to apply to us.

About us Welcome to TOI TOI & DIXI! We are the world’s leading
provider of mobile sanitary solutions, with operations across Europe,
the USA and Asia. Our TOI TOI® and DIXI® brands are represented in
31 countries, supported by more than 5,400 employees worldwide. At TOI
TOI & DIXI, everyone has the opportunity to make an impact. Flat
hierarchies, short decision-making paths and an appreciative working
culture create space for new ideas, personal responsibility and
professional development. In this hybrid position, you will combine
two complementary roles: As IT Business Partner, you will be the
trusted advisor and primary IT contact for our business units in the
Czech Republic, Slovakia and Poland. As IT Project Manager, you will
lead and deliver international IT projects across the Group. Your Role
Act as the single point of contact between IT and business
stakeholders in the Czech Republic, Slovakia and Poland for all new
demands, projects and digital initiatives. Build strong relationships
with stakeholders at all levels, understand their requirements and
translate business needs into scalable, value-adding IT solutions
Identify opportunities for digitalisation and guide new demands from
initial concept through prioritisation and approval to successful
implementation Coordinate internal teams, external service providers
and vendors to deliver IT projects on time, within scope and within
budget Define project objectives, scope, resources and schedules in
close collaboration with all relevant business and IT stakeholders
Develop and maintain project plans and documentation, monitor progress
and performance, and provide transparent status reporting Manage
project risks, dependencies and changes to scope, schedule and costs,
escalating issues where necessary Align IT services and investments
with business priorities while continuously improving service quality
and measurable business value Keep stakeholders informed about project
delivery, service performance, innovations and emerging technologies
Contribute ideas on digital trends and responsible AI use that improve
processes and the way we work Maintain regular on-site contact with
our locations in the region and support international projects beyond
your assigned Business Partner scope Facilitate demand management,
prioritisation and alignment of business requirements within the Group
IT portfolio. Ensure that technology initiatives and IT investments
deliver measurable business value and support strategic objectives.
Your Profile A degree in Information Technology, Computer Science,
Business Administration or a comparable qualification Three to five
years of professional experience in a comparable position, ideally as
an IT Business Partner, IT Project Manager or Business Analyst Fluent
written and spoken English and at least one of Czech, Polish, or
Slovak are mandatory; German language skills are an advantage. Proven
experience in successfully managing IT projects and sound knowledge of
both project life cycle and systems development life cycle
methodologies A strong understanding of core business processes,
particularly in areas such as Finance, HR, Operations and Sales Broad
knowledge of current technologies and digitalisation trends, with the
ability to identify their potential business value Practical
experience with common AI tools, such as Microsoft 365 Copilot or
comparable generative AI assistants, and the ability to use them
responsibly in daily work Excellent analytical, organisational and
stakeholder-management skills, combined with a structured and
solution-oriented approach Strong client-facing and communication
skills, with the confidence to engage effectively with stakeholders
from the shop floor to C-suite level A client-focused, proactive and
self-driven mindset with the ability to build trust and long-term
relationships Willingness to travel regularly within the region and,
where required, internationally Experience with project management
tools such as Microsoft Project or Smartsheet is an advantage; PRINCE2
certification is a plus Your Benefits Hybrid modern working model:
Work from home or from our office in Ratingen (Germany) with flexible
working hours. Permanent employment contract: Enjoy job security with
a long-term commitment. Supplementary company health insurance:
Additional health benefits provided by the company. Comprehensive
onboarding and training: Benefit from an individual onboarding plan
and extensive induction training to ensure a smooth start. Continuous
development opportunities: Take advantage of advanced and additional
training courses. Employee well-being: Access our company health
management program and enjoy 30 days of annual vacation. Collaborative
culture: Thrive in an environment of open communication and
cooperation. Contact us TOI TOI & DIXI Group GmbH Magdalena Gutland
(Recruiting & HR-Marketing) Halskestr. 38 40880 Ratingen

jobs.employer_name: Boehringer Ingelheim Pharma GmbH & Co. KG
jobs.description:
Boehringer Ingelheim is a biopharmaceutical company active in both human and animal health. As one of the industry's top investors in research and development, the company focuses on developing innovative therapies that can improve and extend lives in areas of high unmet medical need. Independent since its foundation in 1885, Boehringer takes a long-term perspective, embedding sustainability along the entire value chain. Our approximately 54,500 employees serve over 130 markets to build a healthier and more sustainable tomorrow. Learn more at www.boehringer-ingelheim.com
The Position
Are you passionate about bringing innovation to our equine customers to improve the lives of horses and the people who love them? We're seeking for a customer focused, results driven business leader to join our global equine business to continue building and leading a customer centric innovation roadmap in line with the business segment strategy.
This is an important leadership position within the global equine team. You will foster cross-functional collaboration together with R&D, Supply, Regions and Countries and move Innovation/Business Development projects forward. You will lead the commercial perspective of projects, support long-term pipeline forecasting, and manage strategic business model innovation initiatives.
If you believe that this is the next career move for you, we look forward to receiving your dedicated application and getting to know you further!
This position has a hybrid setup with at least three days per week on site.
Tasks & responsibilities

- In this role, you will work closely with Global Head Equine GSM, Equine Franchise Managers and Technical Service Managers to ensure that a consistent overall innovation roadmap is put together and implemented in line with Business Segment strategy.
- As part of this you will be responsible for driving the GSM input on BD&L and R&D potential pipeline opportunities in alignment with the Business Segment Strategy.
- Your lateral leadership skills will help you to foster cross-functional collaboration together with R&D, Supply, Regions and Countries teams for internal innovation and BD&L projects.
- You will champion the Global Strategic Marketing (GSM) needs during project development management within project teams, leading commercial perspective in projects and drive the GSM input into appropriate prioritization for research projects within sub-franchise portfolio including project status tracking and stakeholder communications.
- You will lead commercial input into product profiles from strategic and business perspectives.
- Finally, in close collaboration with Global Head Equine GSM and franchise managers, you will derive global forecasting assumptions and review / align them with key countries as needed.

Requirements

- Master degree in the field of Veterinary science or similar required.
- Highly specialized knowledge and experience in the field of equine health with a deep understanding of the therapeutic and veterinary science areas and customer needs in this field
- Strong lateral leadership skills to foster cross-functional work
- Ability to communicate decisions to senior stakeholders in an international/cross-cultural matrix environment
- Strong financial and business acumen
- Strong strategic and analytical capabilities
- Excellent knowledge of English, further languages of advantage

With us, you can develop your own path in a company with a culture that knows our differences are our strengths - and break new ground in the drive to make millions of lives better.

Here, your development is our priority. Supporting you to build a career as part of a workplace that is independent, authentic and bold, while tackling challenging work in a respectful and friendly environment where everyone is valued and welcomed.

Alongside, you have access to programs and groups that ensure your health and wellbeing are looked after - as we make major investments to drive global accessibility to healthcare. By being part of a team that is constantly innovating, you'll be helping to transform lives for generations.

Want to learn more? Visit https://www.boehringer-ingelheim.com

Ready to contact us?
If you have any questions about the job posting or process - please contact our HR Direct Team, Tel: +49 (0) 6132 77-3330 or via mail: hr.de@boehringer-ingelheim.com

About us European Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (ESMC) GmbH is
the joint venture between TSMC, Bosch, Infineon and NXP. For the first
time, global technology leader TSMC is building a semiconductor fab in
the heart of Europe, offering cutting-edge manufacturing technologies
for next-generation semiconductor products. ESMC represents a shared
commitment to strengthening the European semiconductor ecosystem. For
our future fab in Dresden, we are looking for a highly motivated and
committed: AMHS Hardware Engineer (m/w/d) Become the heart of our fab
automation. The Automated Material Handling System (AMHS) will be the
nervous system of our fab. As an AMHS Hardware Engineer, you’ll be a
technical expert, designer, problem-solver, and team leader. You’ll
ensure that our wafer transport systems (transfer tools, sorters, N2
systems) operate at maximum efficiency. Tasks Your Mission: Take the
lead on hardware performance and drive technological development:
System Optimization & Setup: You will be responsible for the
installation, commissioning, and continuous improvement of our AMHS
hardware. In-Depth Troubleshooting: For complex issues, you will
conduct root cause analyses (8D, FMEA, SPC) and implement sustainable
solutions. Project Management: You will lead cross-functional projects
aimed at improving productivity, quality, and cost efficiency—from
planning through to performance review. Technology Scouting: You will
evaluate new equipment and materials, work closely with suppliers, and
develop in-house hardware solutions to meet operational needs.
Leadership & Mentoring: You will lead and mentor a team of technicians
and junior engineers, share your knowledge, and foster team spirit
through clear communication. Fab Setup: You will actively assist with
installation and coordinate upgrades in close collaboration with other
departments. Profile You are a proactive team player who thrives in a
dynamic, fast-paced environment and is willing to take on
responsibility. Qualifications: A Master’s degree in Engineering,
such as Mechanical or Electrical Engineering, Automation, or a related
field. Experience: Professional experience in the semiconductor
industry is required. Technical expertise: In-depth knowledge of
optimization algorithms, control systems, and mechanical automation.
Methodological skills: Proficiency in quality tools such as SPC, FMEA,
and 8D problem-solving. Personality: Hands-on mentality, resilience,
and the ability to motivate and lead teams professionally. Language:
Fluent in English (company language). Basic communication skills in
Mandarin or German is a plus. Training: Available for on-the-job
training in Taiwan, 9 to 12 months. Location: Dresden, Germany We
offer Each journey starts with a first step. Joining ESMC at this
early stage will provide you with the unique opportunity to actively
shape the future of the fab in Dresden, boost your career and put your
true potential to the test. You will be working in a fast paced,
international startup environment whilst at the same time having
access to the experience, talent, and resources of the largest and
most advanced semiconductor manufacturer in the world, TSMC. You have
ample opportunities to learn about TSMC Operations, Digital
Transformation, and various advanced Facilities related topics, both
in Taiwan and other sites around the world. Behind the world’s most
advanced technology are real people with real passion. Our success is
fueled by our core values: Integrity, Commitment, Innovation and
Customer Trust (ICIC). At ESMC we believe in the power of inclusive
leadership and passion. We demonstrate this in our commitment to our

apprentice journey for Europe's newest, most advanced semiconductor
facility? As a Senior HR Specialist - Apprenticeship & Vocational
Training (m/f/d) at ESMC in Dresden, you will move beyond standard
administration to drive collaborative success across all core phases
of our technical vocational education. You will be the architect of
our future talent pipeline— managing employer branding at schools,
coordinating dual-training plans, mentoring Gen-Z apprentices, and
ensuring legal compliance. Fitting into our fast-paced greenfield
environment, this role offers a unique opportunity to shape the next
generation of microtechnology and industrial specialists from the

adults through their personal and professional development.

fab safety regulations, and the technical demands of Microtechnology
(Mikrotechnologe/In). Experience setting up apprenticeship structures
in a fast-growing, ramp-up corporate environment. We offer Security &
Perspective: A permanent employment contract and career advancement
opportunities in one of Europe's leading semiconductors fabs. Company
Pension Plan & Financial Benefits: We support your financial

exclusive Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP). Relocation Support for

Postdoctoral Researcher (m/f/d) – Institute for Pharmacology and Toxicology
Ref.-Nr.  601-2026
Third-party funding

The Faculty of Medicine is an integral part of the Otto-von-Guericke-University Magdeburg and cooperates with the Magdeburg University Hospital A.ö.R. in research, teaching and patient care.

Your Responsibilities:

We are seeking two highly motivated Postdoctoral Research Fellows to join our team investigating the molecular and cellular organization of the nervous system using cutting-edge spatial transcriptomics approaches. The successful candidates will work at the interface of neuroscience, genomics, and computational biology to map gene expression patterns across brain tissue with spatial resolution, contributing to our understanding of neural circuit organization, development, and disease.

This is an exciting opportunity to join a collaborative, well-resourced research environment with access to state-of-the-art spatial profiling platforms (e.g., MERFISH, 10x Visium), advanced microscopy, and high-performance computing infrastructure.

Two positions are available with complementary focus:

- Position 1 — Experimental/Wet-lab focus: Designing and executing spatial transcriptomics experiments on neural tissue, including tissue preparation, probe design, imaging, and data generation
- Position 2 — Computational/Analytical focus: Developing and applying computational pipelines for spatial transcriptomic data analysis, including cell-type mapping, spatial statistics, and integration with single-cell/single-nucleus datasets

(Candidates with strong interest and skills spanning both areas are also encouraged to apply and may be considered for either position.)

Key Responsibilities:

- Design, plan, and conduct spatial transcriptomics experiments on neural tissue samples
- Analyze and interpret complex spatial and single-cell genomic datasets
- Collaborate with neuroscientists, computational biologists, and clinicians within and outside the group
- Present findings at lab meetings, seminars, and international conferences
- Prepare manuscripts for peer-reviewed publication
- Contribute to grant writing and mentoring of graduate/undergraduate students
- Maintain rigorous documentation and adhere to good research and data management practices

Your Profile:

Essential Qualifications:

- A PhD (completed or close to completion) in Neuroscience, Molecular/Cell Biology, Genomics, Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, or a related field
- Demonstrated research productivity (peer-reviewed publications and/or preprints)
- Strong written and verbal communication skills in English

For the experimental-focus position, in addition:

- Hands-on experience with molecular biology techniques (e.g., histology, immunohistochemistry, in situ hybridization, RNA-seq library prep)
- Experience with spatial transcriptomics platforms (e.g., Visium, MERFISH, Xenium, seqFISH) is highly desirable
- Experience with rodent or human brain tissue handling is a plus

For the computational-focus position, in addition:

- Strong programming skills (Python and/or R)
- Experience analyzing single-cell/single-nucleus RNA-seq or spatial transcriptomics data
- Familiarity with relevant packages/tools (e.g., Scanpy, Seurat, Squidpy, STUtility) and statistical/machine learning methods
- Experience with high-performance/cluster computing is a plus

We offer:

- Access to cutting-edge spatial transcriptomics and imaging technology
- A collaborative, interdisciplinary, and supportive research environment
- Funding and support to attend international conferences
- Opportunities for career development, mentoring, and grant-writing training
- Work and family in harmony: Through Klinikzwerge (https://kita.med.ovgu.de/) , childcare may be available, subject to availability
- Help protect the environment and enjoy discounted public transportation through a job ticket
- In addition, we offer a diverse range of sports and relaxation activities as part of our workplace health promotion program
- Onboarding: At the start of your employment, you will participate in our orientation program, where you will receive important information and training sessions

- **Salary: **The salary group E 13 according to “Tarifvertrag für den öffentlichen Dienst der Länder” awaits you
- **Appointment: **The position is to be filled as a full-time position, with a workload of 2,5 years, starting on 2027/01/01

In order to fill a fixed-term position in part-time (25,8895 hrs/wk = 65%) starting in March 2027, we are looking for 1

Research Associate / PhD Candidate in Cellular and Circuit Neuroscience (m/f/x)

The newly established research group of Prof. Dr. Timothy Zolnik at the Faculty of Biology and Biotechnology, Ruhr University Bochum, investigates how deep cortical neurons influence cortical and thalamic circuits. Our work combines cellular electrophysiology with optogenetics, pharmacology and circuit approaches to study mechanisms relevant to attention and arousal.

The PhD candidate will investigate cellular and synaptic mechanisms in defined cortical circuits, with a focus on layer 6b and its interactions with other cortical and thalamic neurons. The project centers on whole-cell recordings in acute mouse brain slices, combined with optogenetic circuit mapping and quantitative analysis.

Scope: part-time
Duration: fixed-term, 3 years
Start: starting in March 2027
Apply by:  2026-10-26

Your tasks:

• Design and perform whole-cell patch-clamp experiments in acute mouse brain slices.

• Measure intrinsic neuronal properties and synaptic responses in identified cell types.

• Combine electrophysiology with optogenetic circuit mapping and pharmacological manipulations.

• Perform or assist with stereotaxic viral injections and prepare tissue for recordings and histology.

• Analyze, visualize and interpret electrophysiological data using quantitative methods.

• Document experiments and present results in lab meetings and at scientific conferences.

• Contribute to scientific manuscripts and the collaborative development of the research group.

Your profile:

• A completed Master’s degree (or equivalent) in neuroscience, biology, physiology, biomedical sciences or a related field (required).

• Hands-on experience with whole-cell patch-clamp recordings in acute ex vivo brain slices (required).

• Experience analyzing and interpreting electrophysiological data (required).

• A strong interest in cellular, synaptic and circuit neuroscience, with careful experimental practice (required).

• Very good written and spoken English and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively (required).

• Experience with stereotaxic viral injections and/or optogenetics (desirable).

• Experience with neuropharmacology, histology, microscopy and/or programming for data analysis (advantageous).

jobs.description:
The University Hospital Bonn (UKB) is one of Germany’s leading university hospitals, combining top-level performance in medicine and research with excellence in teaching. Each year, more than half a million patients receive inpatient and outpatient care at the UKB. Around 3,500 students study medicine and dentistry here, and over 600 people are trained annually in healthcare professions. With approximately 9,900 employees, the UKB is the third-largest employer in the Bonn/Rhein-Sieg region. In the Focus hospital ranking, the UKB ranks first among university hospitals in North Rhine-Westphalia and second nationwide in terms of case mix index (case severity). In 2024, the UKB raised nearly €100 million in third-party funding for research, development, and teaching. The F.A.Z. Institute has named the UKB “Germany’s Training Champion” and “Germany’s Most Attractive Employer” for the fourth consecutive year.

The following full-time (38.5 hours/week) position is to be filled as soon as possible at the Center of Neurology of the University Hospital Bonn:

Postdoctoral Researcher in Computer Vision and Multimodal AI for the Early Detection of Parkinson’s Disease (m/w/d)

The position is fixed-term until 30 September 2028 due to the duration of the research project.

Parkinson’s disease is usually diagnosed only after substantial neurodegeneration has already occurred. Subtle changes in movement, facial expression and speech may emerge years earlier, but current clinical assessments are not designed to detect and quantify them at scale. We believe that computer vision and multimodal AI can help close this gap - and that meaningful progress requires researchers who want to apply cutting-edge methods to a major clinical challenge.

Our goal is to develop objective and scalable digital tools for the early detection and monitoring of Parkinson’s disease. We combine video-based analysis of gait, balance, facial expression and limb movements with speech, touchscreen and wearable sensor data. A particular focus is on individuals with isolated REM sleep behavior disorder, who are at high risk of developing Parkinson’s disease or related neurodegenerative disorders.

The group of Prof. Dr. Michael Sommerauer at the Center of Neurology at the University Hospital Bonn and the German Center for Neurodegenerative Diseases (DZNE) is seeking a highly motivated postdoctoral researcher to join our interdisciplinary team.

The successful candidate will take a leading role in the development of the computer vision components of bradyMX, our multimodal digital motor assessment platform. The position is embedded in the ERC-funded Re-START PD research program and offers the opportunity to work with unique, deeply phenotyped clinical cohorts and longitudinal datasets. Rather than developing methods in isolation, you will work closely with clinicians and neuroscientists to translate methodological advances into tools that may improve patient stratification, clinical trials and, ultimately, the way Parkinson’s disease is detected.

Please submit your application as a single PDF, including: 

• a cover letter describing your scientific interests and motivation for joining the group 

• a curriculum vitae including a publication list 

• contact details for at least two referees

Your responsibilities:

- Lead the development of computer vision methods for quantifying subtle motor abnormalities from clinical video recordings
- Develop robust pipelines for human pose estimation, facial and body landmark detection, movement segmentation, tracking, feature extraction and automated quality control
- Design and evaluate machine-learning and deep-learning models for the analysis of gait, balance, facial expression and upper- and lower-limb movements
- Investigate temporal modelling, representation learning and interpretable movement features for the detection and monitoring of early motor dysfunction
- Integrate video-derived features with complementary digital modalities such as speech, touchscreen tasks, inertial sensors and clinical assessments
- Evaluate model robustness and generalizability across participants, recording conditions, devices and international study sites
- Work closely with the clinical research team on study design, data collection, annotation strategies and the interpretation of model outputs
- Prepare scientific manuscripts, present results at international conferences and contribute to grant applications
- Support the supervision of doctoral, Master’s and medical students

Your profile:

- - A doctoral degree in computer vision, machine learning, computer science, biomedical engineering, medical informatics or a closely related discipline
- Strong experience in machine learning and deep learning for image, video or human movement analysis
- Excellent programming skills in Python and practical experience with frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow or JAX
- Experience in one or more of the following areas: human pose estimation, motion tracking, action recognition, temporal modelling, self-supervised learning, multimodal learning or domain adaptation
- A sound understanding of experimental design, quantitative model evaluation and reproducible research practices
- Experience with version control and collaborative software development; knowledge of containerized workflows and high-performance computing is an advantage
- Interest in translating methodological advances into clinically meaningful applications; previous experience in Parkinson’s disease or medical research is welcome but not required
- A high degree of scientific curiosity, independence and commitment to rigorous research
- Strong communication skills and enthusiasm for working in an interdisciplinary and international environment
- Very good command of written and spoken English; German language skills are not required

What we offer:

- Rich video, sensor and clinical datasets collected using standardized multimodal assessment protocols
- A direct path from methodological development to external validation and clinically relevant application
- Close collaboration with neurologists, neuroscientists, and international experts in Parkinson’s disease and digital biomarkers
- An excellent research environment at the University Hospital Bonn, the University of Bonn and the German Center for Neurodegenerative Diseases
- Access to modern computational infrastructure and support for reproducible data analysis and software development
- Strong support for scientific publications, conference participation, grant applications and the development of an independent academic profile

Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (JGU) is one of the largest universities in Germany. Thanks to its location in the Rhine-Main science region, the university can unfold to its full potential and showcase its innovative power and dynamism. Its status as a comprehensive university allows for multidisciplinary learning and teaching and has great potential for internationally renowned, interdisciplinary research. Almost all of its institutes are located on a single campus close to the Mainz city center - creating a lively academic culture for researchers, teaching staff, and students from every continent.

Academic staff member (Postdoc): Plant RNA Biology

The Wachter group investigates the molecular mechanisms and biological functions of alternative RNA splicing in plants (https://mps-imp.biologie.uni-mainz.de/). Our recent work has identified novel components of the plant splicing-regulatory code, including structured mRNA elements (e.g., https://doi.org/10.1111/tpj.71060 ) and position-dependent functions of pyrimidine motifs (https://doi.org/10.1111/tpj.16739). By combining these functional studies with global profiling approaches, we are building a framework to understand and engineer alternative splicing in the context of plant development and stress responses.

As a member of our international research team, you will examine the regulation and functional impact of splicing decisions controlled by polypyrimidine tract-binding proteins (PTBs), a family of key splicing regulators in plants and animals. Your work will build on our previous findings on PTB functions in alternative splicing and on recent results from ongoing transcriptome-wide approaches, including splicing pattern profiling, iCLIP, and TRIBE. You will further develop these analysis pipelines and integrate the resulting datasets to define the role of this central component of splicing control in the model plant Arabidopsis thaliana. The new insights from these mechanistic studies will be linked to physiological PTB functions we previously observed, including ABA-dependent seed germination and drought tolerance. The overarching goal of this project is to establish the molecular connections between PTB functions and key traits of stress physiology, thereby laying the groundwork for novel strategies to enhance plant resilience. This work is supported by extensive expertise, various core facilities, and a completely new research infrastructure.

Tackling critical questions on PTB functions in A. thaliana using a multidisciplinary approach, which integrates molecular biology, RNA biochemistry, and plant stress physiology
Applying state-of-the-art techniques for gene-specific and genome-wide analyses of RNA biology
Developing an integrated framework to decipher PTB’s role in splicing and its downstream physiological outcomes, with a particular focus on drought stress
Assisting with lab organisation and other general tasks
Contributing to teaching activities for Bachelor's and Master's students within our group
Supervising PhD students and other group members
Presenting your research findings in oral and written form, including conference contributions, reports, and manuscripts

A successfully completed scientific university degree in Biology or in a related field
A successfully completed doctorate (PhD) in molecular plant biology or RNA biology
Experience with a spectrum of molecular methods
Experience in plant (stress) physiology is a plus, but not mandatory
Teaching experience is a plus, but not mandatory
Very good English language skills (at least level B2); German language skills are a plus, but not mandatory
A successful academic track record documented by publications, conference contributions, etc.
A fascination for science, very good communication and teamwork skills

In order to fill a fixed-term position in part-time, full-time (39.83 hours/week = 100%) at the earliest possible date, we are looking for 1

Postdoctoral Researcher (m/f/x) – First-Principles Core-Level Spectroscopy of Functional Interfaces

The successful applicant (m/f/x) will join the research group of Prof. Silvana Botti at the Research Center Future Energy Materials and Systems (RC FEMS) and the Ruhr University Bochum (RUB). The group develops first-principles methods to describe electronic excitations, spectroscopic signatures, and structure–property relations in materials and at functional interfaces.

Core-level spectroscopies — X-ray absorption (XAS/XANES), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and core-loss electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS/ELNES) — are among the few experimental probes that are element-specific and, at the same time, sensitive to the local chemical environment of the excited atom. Because the core hole is strictly localised, the resulting spectral fine structure encodes coordination, charge transfer, oxidation state, and local magnetic order at the single-atom level. Turning this sensitivity into quantitative structural information, however, requires theory: the interpretation of measured spectra rests on the accurate ab initio description of core-hole effects, core-exciton binding, multiplet structure, and electronic correlation. Existing approaches have been developed and validated largely for bulk compounds, whereas the systems of interest for energy conversion and catalysis are surfaces, interfaces, and defects, where symmetry breaking, hybridisation, and local charge redistribution reshape the spectra. The aim of this position is to close that gap. The successful candidate will develop and extend first-principles methods for core-level spectroscopy and establish their predictive accuracy for functional interfaces, including systems containing correlated and magnetic transition-metal elements. The developments will be implemented in existing electronic-structure and spectroscopy codes, released as documented open-source software, and validated against experimental spectra measured by partners at RUB and within RC FEMS. In perspective, these methods will provide the basis for using computed core-level spectra as fingerprints of local atomic arrangements at chemically complex alloy surfaces — an application currently being prepared with experimental groups on campus — so that the candidate will help shape the scientific direction of a planned collaborative research programme from the start. The newly founded Research Center focuses on developing innovative materials and systems for sustainable energy applications. The center’s research areas include photovoltaics, thermoelectricity, energy storage, fuel cells, and sustainable chemical processes, among others. Its interdisciplinary approach involves collaborations between physicists, chemists, engineers, and material scientists to address the challenges of transitioning to a low-carbon economy. The center also offers opportunities for graduate students and postdoctoral researchers to participate in cutting-edge research projects and receive advanced training in the field of energy materials and systems. The chair of Prof. Botti is affiliated with the Faculty of Physics and Astronomy of the Ruhr University Bochum. This faculty is a leading research and teaching institution in the fields of experimental and theoretical physics and astronomy, with a focus on condensed matter physics, astrophysics, and particle physics.

Scope: part-time, full-time
Duration: fixed-term, 2 Years
Start: at the earliest possible date
Apply by:  2026-10-20

Your tasks:

The successful candidate (f/m/x) will

- develop and extend ab initio methods for core-level spectroscopy — X-ray absorption and core-loss EELS near-edge structure, as well as core-level binding-energy shifts in photoemission — with particular attention to core-hole effects, core-exciton binding, and multiplet structure
- extend the description of core-level excitations from bulk compounds to surfaces, interfaces, adsorbates, and defects, and quantify how symmetry breaking, hybridisation, and local charge transfer modify the near-edge spectral features
- treat correlated and magnetic transition-metal elements with methods beyond standard density functional theory, such as dynamical mean-field theory or multiplet ligand-field approaches, and establish for which systems and spectral features this level of theory is actually required
- implement the developments in established electronic-structure and spectroscopy codes, and release them as documented, maintainable open-source software usable by others in the community
- benchmark computed spectra against experimental data in close collaboration with spectroscopy and electron-microscopy partners at RUB and within RC FEMS
- help prepare the extension of these developments to chemically complex surfaces and to forthcoming collaborative research proposals, including preliminary calculations and proof-of-concept studies
- publish results in peer-reviewed journals, present them at international conferences, and contribute to the training of doctoral and master’s students in the group

Your profile:

Required qualifications:

- A master and PhD in Physics
- A strong background in condensed matter physics and in the first-principles electronic-structure theory of solids
- Strong knowledge of quantum mechanics and of the theory of electronic excitations in materials, including core-level excitations and the interaction between the core hole and the excited electron
- Demonstrated expertise in the theory and simulation of at least one core-level spectroscopy, such as X-ray absorption, X-ray photoemission, or core-loss electron energy-loss spectroscopy
- Working experience with methods for correlated or open-shell systems beyond standard density functional theory, for example dynamical mean-field theory, Hubbard-corrected functionals, or multiplet and ligand-field approaches
- High-level programming skills in Fortran and/or Python, and practical experience with established electronic-structure or spectroscopy codes (e.g., VASP, Quantum ESPRESSO, ABINIT, SIESTA, RSPt, TRIQS)
- Demonstrated experience in the development of computational methods and scientific software, documented for example by contributions to a community code or by a released open-source package. We are looking for researchers who develop methods and codes — not users. Experience limited to running standard codes will not be considered.
- Demonstrated ability to carry out independent research, evidenced by publications in peer-reviewed journals
- Good command of English, both written and spoken

At the Faculty of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Institute of Circuits and Systems, the Chair of Highly-Parallel VLSI Systems and Neuro-Microelectronics offers a position as

Research Associate / PhD Student / PostDoc (m/f/x)

(subject to personal qualification, employees are remunerated according to salary group E 13 TV-L)

starting as soon as possible. The position is limited until May 31, 2029. The period of employment is governed by the Fixed Term Research Contracts Act (Wissenschaftszeitvertragsgesetz - WissZeitVG). The position offers the chance to obtain further academic qualification (usually PhD / habilitation thesis). Balancing family and career is an important issue. The position is generally suitable for candidates seeking part-time employment. Please indicate the request in your application.

State-of-the-art AI systems depend heavily on models, providers and hardware from the U.S. and China, which represents a big challenge of Europe’s sovereignty for AI model development and deployment (e.g., trustworthiness, dependability, performance, modularity). The Horizon Europe project OptimAIse (Optimising Performance and Trust for Integrity-driven Modular genAI Software Engineering) addresses these challenges by delivering a scalable, modular, and interoperable reference architecture that leverages European hardware to enable efficient and simplified large language model deployments. The SpiNNaker2 hardware, developed by TU Dresden and commercialized by SpiNNcloud, is one of Europe’s most promising alternatives for the energy-efficient serving of LLMs. SpiNNaker2 is a massively parallel architecture with locally dense compute and globally sparse and low-latency communication, ideal to realize efficient AI models by leveraging sparse and event-based computing.

The candidate will develop and adopt LLMs for the SpiNNaker2 hardware. The models shall be implemented on the hardware using an existing software stack and optimized with ML compilers such as MLIR. Besides applying known approaches such as Mixture-of-Experts, the candidate shall follow the state of the art of efficient language models and try novel approaches on SpiNNaker2. In addition, the work will derive requirements and recommendation for next-generation AI hardware such as Spinnaker3, thus guiding the future of efficient AI systems.

Tasks: 

- scientific research in efficient language models and their hardware deployment
- development and training of sparse and communication avoiding GenAI models optimized for SpiNNaker2 hardware
- implementation of GenAI models (resp. their layers) on SpiNNaker2 using ML compilers (e.g., MLIR)
- presentation and publication of research results in top-tier conferences/journals
- collaboration in European project OptimAIse, integrating GenAI models on SpiNNaker2 for use-case demonstrators

Requirements: 

- university degree (Master’s or equivalent) in computer science, electrical engineering, machine learning or related fields of expertise
- good understanding of LLMs and how they are processed on AI hardware for inference
- very good programming skills (e.g., C++, Python)
- good written and spoken English skills
- high motivation and ability to work independently and in teams
- excellent skills and practical experience in one or more of the following research areas is beneficial:
- compiler frameworks (LLVM, MLIR)
- embedded software development
- computer and accelerator architectures
- parallel and distributed computing

We offer: 

- the opportunity to collaborate within a diverse team of multi-domain experts at HPSN chair
- access to the world’s-largest brain-inspired supercomputer SpiNNcloud
- access to TUD’s HPC environment for ML training
- flexible arrangements for work hours to support a good work-life balance
- 30 days of vacation per year (based on a 5-day workweek)
- extensive opportunities for professional development and continuing education
- health care and sports programs offered by TUD
- a discounted job ticket (also available as a Deutschlandticket)
- participation in the supplementary pension scheme for employees in the public sector via VBL (Federal and State Government Employees Retirement Fund)

TUD strives to employ more women in academia and research. We therefore expressly encourage women to apply. The university is a family-friendly university. We welcome applications from candidates with disabilities. If multiple candidates prove to be equally qualified, those with disabilities or with equivalent status pursuant to the German Social Code IX (SGB IX) will receive priority for employment.

Application:

Please submit your detailed application with the usual documents (Cover letter, CV, degree certificate) quoting the reference code HPSN_OptimAIse_2026 by October 20, 2026 (stamped arrival date of the university central mail service or the time stamp on the email server of TUD applies), preferably via the TUD SecureMail Portal https://securemail.tu-dresden.de by sending it as a single pdf file to christian.mayr@tu-dresden.de (https://mailto:christian.mayr@tu-dresden.de) or to:

TU Dresden, Chair of Highly-Parallel VLSI Systems and Neuro-Microelectronics, Prof. Christian Mayr, Helmholtzstr. 10, 01069 Dresden, Germany.

Please submit copies only, as your application will not be returned to you. Expenses incurred in attending interviews cannot be reimbursed.

TUD is a founding partner in the DRESDEN-concept alliance.

About the role

Münster, Germany · Part-time

The Executive Assistant & Project Coordinator will provide executive, administrative and project coordination support to the CFO. Based in Germany and working closely with the CFO in France, you will help keep financial administration, corporate governance and cross-border operational matters moving to completion.

This is a practical coordination role for someone who is organised, persistent and comfortable following up with banks, lawyers, tax advisers, notaries, corporate service providers and internal teams. You will coordinate documents, signatures, banking administration, KYC and AML requests, legal entity changes and board formalities across the Atari Group.

You do not need to be an accountant or a technical finance specialist. You do need to be reliable with sensitive information, comfortable with formal processes and willing to chase the right people until an item is complete.

What you’ll do

- Provide day-to-day executive and administrative support to the CFO, coordinating priorities across Germany, France and the US.
- Coordinate the preparation, circulation, approval and execution of corporate documents, board resolutions, powers of attorney and other legal or finance documentation.
- Manage signature workflows, monitor outstanding actions and ensure documents are signed, returned and stored on time.
- Coordinate banking administration, including account openings and closures, bank mandates, signatory updates and KYC/AML requests.
- Maintain accurate corporate records and legal entity documentation, ensuring information is complete, current and easy to retrieve.
- Support legal entity shutdowns, entity administration and related projects by coordinating actions across Finance, Legal, tax advisers, banks and external service providers.
- Liaise with banks, external legal counsel, tax lawyers, corporate service providers, notaries and local finance teams on administrative and corporate matters.
- Coordinate board minutes, governance records, approvals, formalities and other recurring corporate requirements.
- Support finance-related administrative work, including gathering information, tracking deadlines, maintaining records and coordinating deliverables.
- Act as a project coordinator for cross-functional finance and governance workstreams, keeping owners aligned and following through on open items.
- Provide administrative support for certain Luxembourg-related matters and coordinate with the relevant internal and external contacts.
- Escalate delays, missing information, unclear ownership or material issues to the CFO or relevant functional lead.

Requirements & Qualifications

- Professional fluency in English, with the ability to communicate clearly in writing and verbally with internal and external stakeholders.
- Experience in an administrative, executive support, banking, legal operations, paralegal, corporate services or similar coordination role.
- Strong organisation and follow-through, with the confidence to chase people, manage deadlines and keep multiple workstreams moving.
- Experience handling confidential information and formal documentation with accuracy and discretion.
- Comfort working with banks, lawyers, advisers, notaries, corporate service providers or other external stakeholders.
- Ability to work independently, prioritise changing requests and operate with flexibility when the CFO and key stakeholders are based in another country.
- Good judgement and attention to detail when coordinating governance, KYC/AML, banking and legal entity administration.

Nice to have

- Professional proficiency in French.
- Experience supporting a CFO, finance leader, executive team or European corporate function.
- Experience in a bank, financial institution, law office, corporate services provider or multinational business.
- Familiarity with KYC/AML processes, bank mandates, signatory administration, powers of attorney, board documentation or legal entity management.
- Experience coordinating entity closures, corporate reorganisations, acquisitions or other cross-border projects.
- Familiarity with Luxembourg corporate or finance administration.

How you’ll work

This role is about making sure important administrative and governance work does not sit unresolved. You will often be coordinating several parties at once, clarifying what is needed, tracking who owns the next step and following up until the document, approval, bank request or entity action is complete.

You will work closely with Finance and Legal, but you are not expected to provide accounting or legal advice. Your value will come from being dependable, organised and persistent, and from creating enough structure that the CFO and specialist advisers can make decisions and complete formalities efficiently.

The role requires flexibility in working hours to accommodate cross-border coordination with the CFO in France, banks, advisers and teams in other time zones.

Why join Atari

This role sits at the centre of an international finance and governance environment. You will work across Germany, France, Luxembourg and other Atari Group locations, helping coordinate the formalities and projects that support the Group’s entities and operations.

You will have visibility across Finance, Legal and senior leadership, with the opportunity to build a reliable operating rhythm for corporate administration and cross-border coordination as Atari continues to integrate and develop its international business.

With a broad range of disciplines, it shapes the future through excellent research and teaching. Its scientific excellence is reflected in the profile areas Light - Life - Liberty, which provide pioneering insights and sustainable solutions for the society of tomorrow. The Chair of Glass Chemistry seeks to fill the position of a
Doctoral research position
in the field of mechanoluminescent materials

commencing on January 1st, 2027, offered as fixed-term position for an initial period of 36 months according to TV-L E13 (75%).

Mechanoluminescence (ML) is the fascinating phenomenon where a material emits light in response to mechanical stimuli, such as scratching, compression, or impact. By translating mechanical stress directly into a visible, infrared, or ultraviolet optical response, ML opens up a plethora of groundbreaking applications. These range from real-time damage monitoring in advanced structural materials to biophysical stress analysis and the visualization of acoustic waves.

Despite its immense potential, the field of mechanoluminescence is still in its infancy. There is a critical gap both in the versatility of practical material solutions and in our fundamental understanding of the underlying physical and chemical mechanisms. This Ph.D. project aims to tackle these challenges, investigating how next-generation inorganic mechanoluminescent materials must be designed and synthesized to meet the stringent demands of future applications.
Design and synthesis of novel inorganic mechanoluminescent materials (e.g., solid-state synthesis, sol-gel processes, or melt-based routes).
Structural and optical characterization using advanced techniques (e.g., XRD, SEM, photoluminescence, and decay spectroscopy).
Mechanoluminescent testing utilizing custom-built setups to evaluate material responses under various mechanical loads (compression, friction, impact).
Fundamental investigation of the charge-trapping and detrapping mechanisms that govern stress-induced light emission.
Collaboration with internal and external partners to explore application-oriented device integration.
Publication of research results in high-impact scientific journals and presentation at international conferences.

Master’s degree (or equivalent) in Chemistry, Materials Science, Physics, or a closely related discipline.
Strong background or keen interest in solid-state chemistry, luminescence, or smart materials.
Hands-on experience with material synthesis and standard characterization techniques is highly desirable.
High level of motivation, curiosity, and the ability to work both independently and as part of an international team.
Excellent communication skills in English (written and spoken); knowledge of German is an asset but not mandatory.

A cutting-edge research project at the forefront of materials science.

In order to fill a fixed-term position in full-time (39.83 hours/week = 100%) at the earliest possible date, we are looking for a

Postdoctoral Researcher (m,f,x) in Computational Neuroscience

The Collaborative Research Center 1280 “Extinction Learning” (SFB 1280) is an interdisciplinary research consortium investigating the neural, cognitive, and behavioral mechanisms underlying extinction learning. Its 19 subprojects bring together researchers from neuroscience, psychology, medicine, and computational modeling across six research locations. The consortium is coordinated at Ruhr University Bochum (RUB). The Computational Neuroscience group at the Institute for Neural Computation at RUB investigates the neural and computational mechanisms underlying learning, episodic memory, and spatial navigation. Within SFB 1280, we use computational modeling to develop mechanistic accounts of learning and memory and work closely with experimental research groups to relate model dynamics to neural and behavioral data. Further information can be found at https://www.rub.de/cns

We are seeking a highly motivated postdoctoral researcher to investigate the neural mechanisms underlying episodic memory and spatial navigation. The successful candidate will develop quantitative spiking neural network models of the hippocampus in an interdisciplinary and collaborative research environment. The project aims to understand how hippocampal sequences during sharp-wave ripples (SWRs) are generated and how they are shaped by previous experience and neuromodulatory influences to support memory consolidation. Computational models will be developed in close interaction with experimental collaborators and validated against in vivo electrophysiological and behavioral data from rodents.

Scope: full-time
Duration: fixed-term, until 30.06.2029 (end of project)
Start: at the earliest possible date
Apply by:  2026-10-19

Your tasks:

- Develop and investigate quantitative spiking neural network models of hippocampal circuits involved in episodic memory and spatial navigation.
- Model how learning and previous experience shape hippocampal representations and sequence generation.
- Derive quantitative predictions from computational models that can be tested using experimental data.
- Analyze and integrate in vivo electrophysiological and behavioral data from rodents to constrain, test, and validate computational models.
- Work closely with experimental collaborators to establish an iterative exchange between computational modeling and empirical research.
- Present research findings at national and international conferences and workshops.
- Publish research results in international peer-reviewed journals.
- Contribute to the supervision and scientific mentoring of doctoral, master’s, and bachelor’s students where appropriate. (At the request of the applicant, participation in teaching is possible.)

Your profile:

- A strong quantitative background and demonstrated experience in computational or mathematical modeling, preferably including biologically plausible or spiking neural network models
- Strong programming skills, preferably in Python, and experience with scientific computing and numerical simulations
- Ability to conduct research independently, develop new research questions, and take responsibility for the implementation and analysis of computational studies
- Excellent communication and teamwork skills and enthusiasm for close collaboration with experimental neuroscientists
- Excellent written and spoken English
- Experience with modern software development practices, version control, high-performance computing, and reproducible research workflows is an advantag

PhD position (f/m/d) in TMS-EEG of episodic memory

The Collaborative Research Center “Episodic Memory” (CRC 1844) is an interdisciplinary consortium consisting of researchers from psychology, computational neuroscience, philosophy and neuroscience. The basis for our research is the Scenario Construction Framework which conceptualizes scenarios as mental simulations of past episodes, constructed from episodic memory traces and semantic information. As a part of this team, you will be trained in interdisciplinary research and have access to a broad spectrum of initiatives to support you in your academic journey. The CRC will be housed at the new research building THINK in Bochum, which is not only equipped with cutting edge technology, but also houses a child care area (which includes, e.g., an outside play area, bedroom), parent child offices, common rooms to foster networking, etc. Within the CRC1844, the Computational Neurology group led by Prof. Dr. Xenia Kobeleva, investigates clinically relevant questions in neuropsychiatry and neurodegenerative diseases using advanced computational approaches, neuroimaging, and neurostimulation. The group is situated in the Institute for Neural Computation and is part of the Bernstein Node Bochum of the Science Hub Neuroscience. Our group works at the interface of clinical neuroscience (neurostimulation and neurodegenerative diseases) and computational neuroscience, with a strong focus on translational research that connects computational methods to real-world clinical data and patient-oriented questions. Our team is young, motivated, international, and genuinely interdisciplinary, bringing together expertise from medicine, neuroscience, psychology, and quantitative sciences. Besides a direct connection to clinical neurology, we are intensively collaborating with world-leading experts for mathematics, psychology, and computer science. The proposed PhD position will focus on the following project: Regions within the cortico-hippocampal network display interactions with the prefrontal cortex during episodic memory. To understand network effects, we will conduct an EEG memory task modulated by transcranial magnetic stimulation, studied by Bayesian modeling and EEG oscillatory analysis.

State-of-the-art AI systems depend heavily on models, providers and hardware from the U.S. and China, which represents a big challenge of Europe’s sovereignty for AI model development and deployment (e.g., trustworthiness, dependability, performance, modularity). The Horizon Europe project OptimAIse (Optimising Performance and Trust for Integrity-driven Modular genAI Software Engineering) addresses these challenges by delivering a scalable, modular, and interoperable reference architecture that leverages European hardware to enable efficient and simplified large language model deployments. The SpiNNaker2 hardware, developed by TU Dresden and commercialized by SpiNNcloud, is one of Europe’s most promising alternatives for the energy-efficient serving of LLMs. SpiNNaker2 is a massively parallel architecture with locally dense compute and globally sparse and low-latency communication, ideal to realize efficient AI models by leveraging sparse and event-based computing.

The candidate will develop and adopt LLMs for the SpiNNaker2 hardware. The models shall be implemented on the hardware using an existing software stack and optimized with ML compilers such as MLIR. Besides applying known approaches such as Mixture-of-Experts, the candidate shall follow the state of the art of efficient language models and try novel approaches on SpiNNaker2. In addition, the work will derive requirements and recommendation for next-generation AI hardware such as Spinnaker3, thus guiding the future of efficient AI systems.
