Doctoral Position (m,f,x) in Computational Neuroscience (Project Z02)

Are you curious about how the human brain stores and retrieves memories? You want bridge the gap between academia and the wider public? The Collaborative Research Center “Episodic Memory” (CRC 1844) is an interdisciplinary consortium consisting of researchers from psychology, computational neuroscience, philosophy and neuroscience. The basis for our research is the Scenario Construction Framework which conceptualizes scenarios as mental simulations of past episodes, constructed from episodic memory traces and semantic information.

We are actively seeking a talented PhD student to join our science communication project within the CRC 1844, which develops a digital serious game for citizen science, establishing a bidirectional bridge between episodic memory (EM) research and the general public. On the one hand, the game facilitates dissemination and intervention studies, with the public being involved in game design and extensions. On the other hand, the game allows for large-scale EM data collection from a diverse population. It also enables longitudinal research on EM, as well as prospective studies of EM changes preceding psychopathology.

Start: from 01.01.2027, pending funding approval

- Help validate the collected EM data in collaboration with experimental projects in the CRC 1844
- Assist the outreach coordinator associated with this project with player recruitment and outreach activities
- Correlate memory performance data from the game with demographic and psychological data in collaboration with the DZPG (German Center for Mental Health)
- Engage in interdisciplinary collaborations with experimental and computational neuroscientists, psychologists, and philosophers

jobs.description:
As a university of applied sciences, we are particularly committed to
sustainable development. Based on our sustainability strategy, we integrate
sustainability into all degree programs, applied research, and our daily
operations. With our campuses in Bochum and Heiligenhaus, we provide important
impulses for the regional development of society and the economy. Numerous
collaborations underline our international focus. We aim to enhance the quality
of our teaching and research by appointing further dedicated and innovative
researchers.

In the Physiotherapy Division of the Department of Nursing, Midwifery and
Therapy Sciences at Hochschule Bochum (Bochum University of Applied Sciences),
a four-year position is available at the earliest possible date, and no later
than March 2027, as

RESEARCH ASSOCIATE / DOCTORAL STUDENT (f/m/d) for the research Project
"multidimensional analytical approaches to improve LBP diagnosis and prognosis"
as part of the DFG Research Unit "DYN3M" (EG 13 TV-L)

The Project is funded by the German Research Foundation (DFG). The position
is fixed-term for a period of 4 years for academic qualification, with a focus
on multimodal data analysis in low back pain. Remuneration is paid in grade E13
TV-L, subject to the fulfillment of personal requirements. The working hours
comprise 23 hours and 54 minutes per week (60% of a full-time position). As
part of this project, a cooperative doctorate at the Doctoral School NRW (PK
NRW) is envisaged.

The DFG-funded research project "DYN3M" (2026–2030) investigates the dynamic
mechanisms of musculoskeletal health and the chronification of low back pain in
order to drive the transition from generic treatment approaches to precise,
personalized pain therapy. As part of your doctorate, you will work at the
intersection of neuroscience, biomechanics, and data science to examine the
interplay between the musculoskeletal system, neural movement control, and
psychological factors. In doing so, you will apply machine learning and
artificial intelligence methods to analyze multimodal data, identify
high-dimensional signatures, and develop predictive models to evaluate whether
individual healing trajectories exist and examing whether specific subgroups
exist for targeted treatments to optimize overall therapeutic success.

Responsibilities:

- Project coordination and operational implementation of the project.
- In addition to project coordination with national and international
partners, the project includes conducting subprojects as part of your doctorate.
- Learning and implementing quantitative data collection and analysis
methods, including machine learning, as well as coordinating and drafting
peer-reviewed publications.
- Participating in the development and application of state-of-the-art data
science models in close collaboration with consortium partners from
biomechanics, medicine, and psychology/psychosomatics.

Postdoc (m/f/d) in Endosymbiosis Research
Job-ID: J000000668
Working hours: Full time
Location: Düsseldorf
Start date: 01.01.2027
Limited until: 31.12.2028
Apply till: 21.10.2026
Payment group: EGr. 13 TV-L
Organization: MathematischNaturwissenschaftliche Fakultät
Job Category: science / research / teach To support our ongoing research, we are seeking a highly motivated Postdoctoral Researcher to join our team. Our group is an enthusiastic and collaborative team of cell and evolutionary biologists investigating the evolutionary transition from bacterial endosymbionts to eukaryotic organelles. We seek to understand, at the mechanistic level, how protists interact with permanent bacterial endosymbionts and how these associations evolve toward organellogenesis. To address these questions, we combine state-of-the-art omics approaches with detailed molecular biological and protein biochemical experimentation. As model systems, we have established the photosynthetic amoeba Paulinella chromatophora and the symbiont-harboring trypanosomatid Angomonas deanei and related species in the laboratory. Neuronal exocytosis is a highly regulated process that enables the rapid release of neurotransmitters from synaptic vesicles. Central to this process is the controlled assembly of SNARE protein complexes, which drive membrane fusion and are regulated by a network of associated proteins. The PhD project will investigate the structural and molecular mechanisms underlying SNARE complex assembly and function in membrane-like environments. A particular focus will be placed on the development and characterization of membrane-mimetic systems, including lipid nanodiscs and synthetic copolymers, to study SNARE complexes and their regulatory proteins under increasingly native-like conditions. Cryo-electron microscopy will be combined with complementary biochemical and biophysical approaches to characterize these systems at the molecular level.
The project offers the opportunity to work in an interdisciplinary structural biology environment at Forschungszentrum Jülich, with access to expertise in cryo-EM, NMR spectroscopy and X-ray crystallography. Cryo-EM studies will be conducted at the state-of-the-art facilities of the Ernst Ruska-Centre (ER-C) at Forschungszentrum Jülich. The expertise in NMR spectroscopy and macromolecular crystallography at IBI-7 offers further opportunities for complementary structural and biophysical characterization. This combination of methods will enable the candidate to address biological questions from different structural perspectives and to develop a broad expertise in modern structural biology. We are looking for a highly motivated candidate with:

A Master’s degree in biochemistry, molecular biology, structural biology, or a related field

Strong practical experience in protein biochemistry, including recombinant protein expression and purification
Previous hands-on experience with cryo-electron microscopy and/or cryo-EM sample preparation
Interest in membrane proteins, protein-protein interactions and structural biology
Ability to work independently as well as in an interdisciplinary research team
Good communication skills in English

jobs.occupation: IMPACT PORTFOLIO MANAGER (Fairer Futures Programmes) (Projektleiter/in / Projektmanager/in)
jobs.description:
Overview:

Fairtrade is the most recognized and trusted sustainability label, working to make trade fairer for people and planet.

For more than three decades, Fairtrade has been making an impact on the way trade works. We believe that every farmer and worker should have access to a better way of doing business, and a better way of living. 

Fairtrade International is an independent non-profit organisation representing more than two million small-scale farmers and workers worldwide. It owns the FAIRTRADE Mark, a registered trademark that appears on more than 37,000 products. Beyond certification, Fairtrade International and its member organisations (three producer networks and 19 national Fairtrade organisations) partner with producers and businesses, engage consumers, and advocate for a fair and sustainable future.

Unit’s description and purpose: 

The Global Impact unit strengthens the Fairtrade system by driving institutional learning and effectiveness through robust monitoring and evaluation systems. We are the hub for the analysis and communication of high-quality data and information about Fairtrade and its impact, as well as supporting strategy delivery. The unit includes the Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) team, which is the Fairtrade system’s hub for MEL which directly connects evidence to strategic decision for the Global Strategy, individual Fairtrade projects and global programmes, Standards, producer support, and more.

PRINCIPAL ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Role purpose: 

The Impact Portfolio Manager (Fairer Futures Programmes) is responsible for stewarding the MEL frameworks for several of Fairtrade’s global product programmes, the flagship programmatic vehicles through which Fairtrade delivers measurable impact for farmers and workers under its 2026–2028 Global Strategy. 

The manager will share responsibilities for a total of three programmes (cocoa, banana, coffee) with another manager, with product- and thematic-specific focus to be determined upon hire.

Working in close collaboration with Fairtrade Producer Networks, Global Product Teams, and the Digital Service Unit, the role ensures that both programmes are underpinned by robust, coherent, and actionable MEL, from framework design through data collection, reporting, evaluation, and learning. The position serves as one of Fairtrade International's primary MEL contact across programme discussions, representing the Global Impact unit in a system that spans FI, National Fairtrade Organizations, and Producer Networks. This role also contributes to the Global Impact unit's impact services offer, drawing on programme MEL expertise to identify and develop customized services for the Fairtrade system and external partners.

Main Responsibilities:            

- MEL Framework, Indicators, and Data Management. Steward and drive the development, maintenance, and continuous improvement of the Theory of Change and MEL framework for several of the Fairer Futures Programmes, working in close collaboration with Producer Networks and Global Product Teams. Steward the KPI and activity/output indicator set for both programmes, including maintaining metadata and monitoring data quality. Work with PN MEL staff, Global Product Teams, and where needed external consultants to ensure systematic consolidation of existing programme data and the design and implementation of regular data collection processes. Coordinate with the Information & Knowledge team on data cleaning, analysis, and visualisation.
- Stakeholder Engagement and Project MEL Alignment. Serve as Fairtrade International's primary MEL contact for the product-expert colleagues in Producer Networks and Global Product Teams, providing technical MEL guidance, supporting capacity on data collection and reporting, and ensuring programme MEL requirements are understood and operationalised across the system. Work with PNs to ensure that MEL frameworks for individual projects within both programme portfolios are aligned to the overarching programme frameworks, providing where capacity is available guidance and quality assurance at project inception and during implementation
- Reporting, Synthesis, and Learning. Lead the preparation of programme-level MEL reporting for programmes, synthesising data and evidence from across the programme portfolio into outputs that feed into the overall strategy reporting cycle. Facilitate learning processes within programmes, identifying evidence-based insights and working with Global Product Teams and PNs to support programme adaptation where warranted. Ensure programme MEL evidence and KPI data are appropriately integrated into the overall strategy MEL cycle in close coordination with the designated strategy MEL lead within the Impact Management team.
- Programme Evaluation. Lead the design, commissioning, and management of the programme evaluations. This includes developing evaluation questions in collaboration with PNs and Global Product Teams, overseeing evaluation partners, and ensuring findings are translated into actionable learning.
- Impact Services and External Engagement. Identify opportunities to offer MEL technical services to Fairtrade system organisations and external partners, drawing on expertise developed through the programmes. Contribute to the scoping, design, and pitching of impact services in collaboration with the Head, with a particular focus on programme MEL, data collection design, and evaluation. Participate actively in relevant system-wide working groups, representing the Impact Management team's MEL perspective on cross-organisational initiatives.

Other tasks that are consistent with the level and responsibilities of this post.

SKILLS REQUIRED:

Level of education: The position holder will have a Master’s degree or higher in development economics, econometrics, applied sociology, social sciences or another relevant field in management or natural sciences. 

Years of professional experience: A minimum of five years' experience in monitoring, evaluation, and learning, with demonstrable experience designing and managing MEL frameworks for multi-stakeholder projects or programmes. At least two years' experience working in or with stakeholders from the Global South, preferably in agricultural or commodity supply chain contexts. Experience in coffee and bananas is an advantage.

Language requirements: Fluency in English required. Professional proficiency in Spanish is a advantage. 

Job Specific Competencies/knowledge: 

- Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning
- Project and Programme Management
- International Development Expertise
- Stakeholder Management
- Planning and execution
- Data Collection Design and Management
- Evaluation Design and Commissioning
- Enhancing data-driven decision making
- Data Analysis (quantitative and qualitative)
- Data Reporting and Synthesis
- Capacity Building

Personal Qualities: 

- Cross-cultural communication
- Facilitation
- Rapid Learning
- Collaboration/Teamwork
- Customer Service
- Presentation Skills
- Relationship Management
- Evidence Collecting
- Flexibility
- Feedback sourcing

Software/Tools: 

- Microsoft 365 (Excel, Word, Outlook, Powerpoint, Teams, Planner)
- Kobo Toolbox (or similar survey design and implementation tools)
- Miro (or similar online whiteboarding tools)
- Canva (or similar graphic design tools)
- Claude.ai (or similar AI  tools)
- Toladata (or similar project monitoring MEL platform)
- Power BI (or similar business intelligence software)

TERMS AND CONDITIONS:

- This is a two-year full-time position within Fairtrade International.
- Location is at Fairtrade International offices in Bonn, Germany with the opportunity for hybrid work arrangements
- The office language is English.
- Salary as per the Collective Bargaining Agreement for the Wholesale and Foreign Trade Industries for North Rhine Westphalia Group 6a and over tariff payments starting from €5455 Gross per month
- Holiday Bonus and 13th salary  
- 30 days of holidays per year (for fulltime employees)
- Subsidised public transportation ticket
- Subsidised meal services
- Childcare cost subsidy 

Please note that Fairtrade International is strict on compliance with the required qualification criteria mentioned above, and only those candidates selected for interviews will be contacted.

OVERVIEW:

Fairtrade is the most recognized and trusted sustainability label, working to make trade fairer for people and planet.

For more than three decades, Fairtrade has been making an impact on the way trade works. We believe that every farmer and worker should have access to a better way of doing business, and a better way of living. 

Fairtrade International is an independent non-profit organisation representing more than two million small-scale farmers and workers worldwide. It owns the FAIRTRADE Mark, a registered trademark that appears on more than 37,000 products. Beyond certification, Fairtrade International and its member organisations (three producer networks and 19 national Fairtrade organisations) partner with producers and businesses, engage consumers, and advocate for a fair and sustainable future.

 Unit’s description and purpose: 

Global Products, Programs and Policy (GPPP) provides leadership to the Fairtrade system with selected product, program and policy intelligence. To this end GPPP provides information, tools and strategic direction as the main outputs. 

GPPP facilitates and contributes to coherent implementation of strategic plans within the Fairtrade system. GPPP develops new ways of delivering Fairtrade’s intended impact in a changing business environment and risk context.

PRINCIPAL ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Role purpose: 

The Cocoa Manager is responsible for implementation of GPPP cocoa works based on work schedule agreed with the Senior Advisor Cocoa. The work will deliver measurable impact for farmers and workers under its 2026–2028 Global Strategy. 

The Cocoa Manager joins a team that works fluidly, sharing responsibilities across multiple workstreams supporting each other where the need is the greatest to achieve their objectives. The environment is dynamic and priorities can shift with external events impacting workplans.  

In addition to other duties the Cocoa Manager, working within GPPP cocoa, will  work in close collaboration with Producer Networks, National Fairtrade Organisations and the Fairtrade International Global Impact team responsible for Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning, to ensure the Fairer Futures Programme – West Africa Cocoa is implemented professionally and on time. The programme is primarily focused on increasing the household income of farmers who are members of Small Producer Organisaitons in the programme. The programme leads to farm level interventions through Small Producer Organisaitons including pruning, cocoa tree planting and shade tree planting among others. The programme includes further interventions on income such as Village Savings and Loans Association, and interventions on social compliance including increasing the effectiveness of child labour monitoring, reporting and remediation. 

Future working responsibilities may extend to other geographies and other commodities.

Main Responsibilities:            

- Supporting National Fairtrade Organisations, in their responsibilities to maintain and grow the market for Fairtrade cocoa.
- Supporting Producer Networks, in their work with Small Producer Organisations, and maintaining and growing the market for Fairtrade cocoa.
- Programme design. Work with stakeholders, and mostly importantly the Producer Network, to ensure programme design is based on evidence with robust monitoring, evaluation and learning contributing to the evolution of the programme.
- Programme implementation. Co-management with the Producer Network based on agreed reporting structures and formats providing oversight and reporting to stakeholders in a timely manner. This will include the running of, and reporting to, a working committee.
- Financial reporting.  Responsible for ensuring timely quarterly financial reporting including an understanding of any variance from plan and agreed actions to remediate that situation.
- Programme monitoring, evaluation and learning. Working with Fairtrade International monitoring, evaluation and learning experts and the Producer Network to ensure implementation and prioritisation of effective monitoring, evaluation and learning in a timely manner.
- External programme reporting. Working with Fairtrade International monitoring, evaluation and learning experts, Producer Network and National Fairtrade Organisations ensuring agreed reporting deadlines are met with quality reporting to be used with commercial stakeholders, government and other interested stakeholders.
- External stakeholder engagement, traders. Working closely with the Producer Network manage relationships with exporter, importer and processers of cocoa who purchase Fairtrade cocoa from Small Producer Organisaitons. Traders are a critical part of the supply chain and their incorporation into the programme is desired and necessary.
- External stakeholder engagement, events. Working with National Fairtrade Organisations you will be speaking at public and trade events on the strategic objectives of our work, the progress and impact with the aim of influencing the sector.
- External stakeholder engagement, media. Where required you will interact with media.
- Fairtrade Standards and Pricing. Liaising with the lead department in Fairtrade on standards and pricing, Fairtrade’s Standards Unit and Pricing Unit, you will be working on standards and pricing matters relating to Fairtrade’s cocoa work and the programme. 

This will include and not limited to consultations, queries and evolution of standards and pricing. 

Other tasks that are consistent with the level and responsibilities of this post.

SKILLS REQUIRED:

Level of education: The position holder will have an undergraduate degree in science or the arts. 

Years of professional experience: A minimum of three years' experience in complex project management which includes implementation in the global South and preferably West Africa.

Language requirements: Fluency in English and French required. Professional proficiency in Spanish is an advantage. 

Job Specific Competencies/knowledge: 

- Project and Programme Management
- People management, particularly where they are not under your direct management
- Stakeholder Management
- International Development Expertise
- Planning and execution
- Financial reporting
- Negotiation
- Public speaking
- Capacity Building

Personal Qualities: 

- Cross-cultural communication
- Facilitation
- Rapid Learning
- Collaboration/Teamwork
- Customer Service
- Presentation Skills
- Relationship Management
- Evidence Collecting
- Flexibility
- Seeking and action on feedback 

Software/Tools:

- Microsoft 365 (Excel, Word, Outlook, Powerpoint, Teams, Planner)
- Miro (or similar online whiteboarding tools)

TERMS AND CONDITIONS:

- This is a two-year full-time position within Fairtrade International.
- Location is at Fairtrade International offices in Bonn, Germany with the opportunity for hybrid work arrangements
- The office language is English
- Salary as per the Collective Bargaining Agreement for the Wholesale and Foreign Trade Industries for North Rhine Westphalia Group 6a and over tariff payments starting from €5455 Gross per month

- Subsidised public transportation ticket
- Subsidised meal services
- Childcare cost subsidy

General informationThe new Chair of Behavioral Accounting ( Prof. Dr. Victor van Pel t) at WHU – Otto Beisheim School of Management in Vallendar is dedicated to the empirical and experimental analysis of decision-making behavior in accounting settings. The focus is on behavioral accounting, controlled, online, and field experiments, and contemporary trends like the use of artificial intelligence. Our research examines how controls, performance feedback, and reporting choices shape the judgments and decisions of managers, employees, investors, and other firm stakeholders. WHU has an international orientation, offers an excellent research environment, and has a vibrant doctoral programme. Moreover, our chair is part of the Finance and Accounting Group, which organizes frequent reading groups and research seminars that further strengthen your doctoral training. This position is particularly suited for people (f/m/d) interested in behavioral research, with a focus on accounting questions, and a career in academia.
Your mission Research
• Conducting independent research in the field of behavioral accounting, in particular on experimental issues in reporting, controls, performance feedback, and the use of artificial intelligence in accounting.
• The aim is to present research results at international conferences and publish them in leading journals.

Teaching
• Collaboration in the implementation and further development of courses in the field of financial and management accounting (e.g. preparation of materials, supervision of students, data analysis or support with experiments).
• Opportunity to gradually take on your own teaching responsibilities and further develop your teaching skills as part of your doctoral programme.

Doctoral programme
• Active participation in WHU’s structured doctoral programme, which includes methodological and theoretical courses, research seminars, and presentations in the doctoral colloquium.
• Use of the international research environment for professional and personal development, including access to laboratory and online recruitment resources and support for conference travel.

Your profileAcademic background
• Above-average master’s degree in accounting, economics, finance or a related area.
• Ideally, your master’s thesis was written in a subject area related to behavioral or experimental research.
• We particularly value if you’ve finished a preparation track, like a research master or another specialized graduate research program.

Technical and methodological skills
• Strong mathematical programming, analytical, and critical thinking skills.
• Experience with experimental design, statistical inference, and academic research and writing practices.
• Proficiency in at least one of the following statistical programming languages: R, Stata, or Python.
• Experience with oTree for conducting experiments is a big plus.

Research interests
• Strong interest in experimental behavioral research, particularly in the areas of accounting.
• Interest in topics such as misreporting, performance measurement and feedback, controls, incentives, and contemporary issues like sustainability and the use of AI is particularly welcome.

Personal requirements
• A passion for learning and scientific research in an international environment.
• Excellent written and spoken English proficiency (German proficiency is not required).

What we offer Academic Environment

WHU has more than 60 faculty members in the fields of management, finance and accounting, economics, entrepreneurship and innovation, marketing and sales, and supply chain management. Research at WHU aims to adhere to three principles: quality, internationality, and practical relevance.

WHU is an equal opportunity employer and thus welcomes applications from individuals with diverse backgrounds. We believe in the benefits of diversity and therefore foster an international, inclusive, and inspiring working environment.

Professor Victor van Pelt
email: Victor.vanPelt@whu.edu

At both the Vallendar and Düsseldorf campuses, we empower leaders to become responsible changemakers, guided by integrity, diversity, and strengthened by a deep sense of togetherness.

jobs.description:
Creating knowledge. Making a difference. Shaping the future. This is what the University of Münster stands for as one of the strongest research-oriented universities in Germany and one of the largest employers in the region. Every day, over 7,000 employees devote themselves to cutting-edge research and excellent teaching. We share more than a workplace. We share the desire to make a real impact – regionally and internationally. Our day-to-day work is distinguished by diversity, openness and space to pursue one’s ideas. Become a part of our team – in academia, a technical or manual trade, or administration.

The Molecular Evolution and Sociobiology Group (AG Gadau) at the Institute for Evolution and Biodiversity (IEB) at the University of Münster, Germany, is seeking to fill the position of a

Lecturer

Akademische Rätin/Akademischer Rat auf Zeit
(salary level A 13 LBesO)

commencing on 01 January 2027. We are offering a three-year, fixed-term position (100%) with the option to extend by an additional three years. The prospective candidate is required to teach four hours per week during the semester (4 SWS).

Your tasks:

- Developing an independent, internationally visible and competitive research program in Evolutionary Biology, Molecular Evolution or Chemical Ecology of Hymenoptera
- Participating in teaching (4SWS/semester) of Bachelor/Master/PhD Students with the option of developing own teaching modules.
- Participation in academic self-administration

Our expectations:

- Having fun doing research and teaching in Evolutionary Biology.
- A university degree and a PhD in Biology, or a related field is required.
- Extensive experience in chemical ecology and either of the following two fields: molecular evolution or evolutionary ecology demonstrated by publications in peer reviewed articles is required.
- Excellent command of English is required.
- Postdoctoral research in evolutionary biology, evolutionary ecology, or chemical ecology is an advantage but not necessary.
- Ideally you have willingness and motivation to work closely with students (BS, MS, PhD) in teaching and supervision.
- Applications for Third-Party funding to build an own, sustainable and independent research program in Evolutionary Biology would be welcomed.
- A high level of organizational and communication skills and readiness to collaborate on shared projects within the IEB/AG Gadau

Advantages for you:

- The AG Gadau and the Institute for Evolution and Biodiversity (https://www.uni-muenster.de/Evolution/ (https://www.uni-muenster.de/Evolution/) ) offer a wide range of opportunities for basic research and teaching in various areas of evolutionary biology, evolutionary ecology, bioinformatics, and biodiversity research.
- The international and interdisciplinary teams at the IEB and within the AG Gadau foster a collaborative working environment and are actively involved in numerous national and international research. This creates ideal conditions for collaborations within these consortia as well as for independent research projects.
-  Appreciation, commitment, openness and respect – values which are important to us.
- Our broad range of diverse work-time models offers great flexibility – also when working from home.
- If you have family members or young children in your care, our Family Service Office offers concrete support to help you balance your private and professional responsibilities.
- As an educational institution, we are deeply committed to offering occupational training and continuing education opportunities tailored to your individual needs.
- From A – Z, Aikido to Zumba, our sport and health programmes ensure a healthy work-life balance.

The University of Münster strongly supports equal opportunity and diversity (https://www.uni-muenster.de/profil/en/diversity/policy/mission-statement.html) . We welcome all applicants regardless of sex, nationality, ethnic or social background, religion or worldview, disability, age, sexual orientation or gender identity. We are committed to creating family-friendly working conditions.

We actively encourage applications by women. Women with equivalent qualifications and academic achievements will be preferentially considered unless these are outweighed by reasons which necessitate the selection of another candidate.

If you have any questions, please contact Prof. Jürgen Gadau (gadauj@uni-muenster.de (gadauj@uni-muenster.de) ) or Dr. Lukas Schrader (lukas.schrader@uni-muenster.de (lukas.schrader@uni-muenster.de) ).

Are you interested? Then we look forward to receiving your application (CV and 2-3-page description of your research plan) by 28-10-2026 exclusively via our online application portal.

For sustainability reasons, we kindly ask you to refrain from submitting paper/printed documents.

Postdocs (2 years) (m,f,x)

The Cluster of Excellence "CASA: Securing the Digital Society" is funded by DFG for the years 2026-2032 with approximately 53 million euros. CASA aims to strengthen the resilience of our digital society. The emergence of disruptive technologies in recent years, especially artificial intelligence and quantum computers, has caused substantial new challenges for cybersecurity research. In the second funding phase, CASA will specifically address these challenges. Thematic priorities include the security of quantum technologies, protection against Al-based disinformation and societal polarization, and new approaches to defending against ransomware. In addition to technical questions, it also investigates the interaction of human behavior and cybersecurity. Research at CASA, which is based at the Horst Görtz Institute for IT Security, follows a strongly interdisciplinary approach. Researchers from the fields of computerscience, cryptography, electrical engineering, mathematics, and psychology work together in an unique constellation in Europe. This holistic approach is unparalleled and holds the potential for scientific breakthroughs. Ruhr-University Bochum (RUB) and its Faculty of Computer Science offer an excellent environment for aspiring young researchers. 20 years ago, the Horst Görtz Institute for IT Security (HGI) was founded here. lt is now one of Europe's most prestigious institutions for basic computer security research. The HGI maintains extensive networks with leading research institutions worldwide and with media and industry. Moreover, it has produced numerous successful security startups. The pioneering work of the HGI forms the basis for the Cluster of Excellence CASA.

jobs.description:
Founded in 1409, Leipzig University is one of Germany’s largest universities and a leader in research and medical training. With around 30,000 students and more than 5000 members of staff across 14 faculties, it is at the heart of the vibrant and outward-looking city of Leipzig. Leipzig University offers an innovative and international working environment as well as an exciting range of career opportunities in research, teaching, knowledge and technology transfer, infrastructure and administration.

The Division of Systems Biophysics of Microbial Dynamics at the Peter Debye Institute for Soft Matter Physics at the Faculty of Physics and Earth System Sciences, seeks to fill the above position.

About the position

- Salary group 13 TV-L 
- Fixed-term position in accordance with the training plan, initially for 1 year; an extension of the fixed-term contract is planned
- 50 % of a full-time position
- As soon as possible

The newly formed Division of Systems Biophysics of Microbial Dynamics (https://home.uni-leipzig.de/sysbiophys/) , led by Professor Katja Taute, is part of the Peter Debye Institute for Soft Matter Physics (https://www.physes.uni-leipzig.de/en/pdi) , which hosts a broad range of biophysics research. Active matter, including bacterial systems, is a growing key research area at the Institute. Our research group develops and uses biophysical methods, including high-throughput, 3D bacterial tracking and microfluidics, in combination with theory and simulations, to quantitatively analyse the spatio-temporal dynamics of bacteria at the level of individuals and populations. One research focus is the chemotactic navigation of bacteria in mechanically complex environments. In nature, swimming bacteria navigate relative to chemical stimuli in environments ranging from open waters to soil and the gut.

The new doctoral researcher is to investigate how the gut bacterium E. coli navigates mechanically complex environments that mimic properties of its natural habitat. Properties of both the bacteria and the environment will be modulated in a controlled fashion to identify the underlying physical mechanisms and address the following questions:

- What is the relationship between behavioural and material parameters that enable optimal navigation?
- Is optimal intracellular information processing specific to the type of environment?
- How do bacteria navigate mechanical gradients?

The role

- Independent, original, experimental scientific research on the above project
- Additional scientific qualification (preparing a doctoral thesis)
- Thorough documentation of research
- Publication of research results, for example at conferences, workshops, or in scientific articles
- Contributions to the Institute’s teaching responsibilities

About you

- An excellent scientific university degree (master of science or comparable) in (bio-)physics, (bio-)engineering or a related field
- Very good command of at least one programming language (Matlab or Python preferred) and of quantitative scientific data analysis
- A track record of academic excellence (e.g. very good grades in the course of study, research or study scholarships and prizes, scientific publications)
- Written and spoken professional fluency in English (at least equivalent to level B2)
- Excellent written communication skills, demonstrated through coherent, structured and precise writing
- Experience with microscopy and scientific image processing would be an advantage
- Interest in quantitative experimental interdisciplinary science
- Collaborative mindset and teamwork skills

What we offer you

- a varied role with a high degree of responsibility in the dynamic environment of a major university
- a professional English-language work environment at the leading edge of interdisciplinary science
- Collaboration in a friendly, supportive and motivated team
- flexible working hours and mobile working to support work-life balance
- Goal-oriented staff development throughout your working life, with opportunities for continuing professional development
- a wide range of occupational health management services 
- Remuneration in line with the collective bargaining agreement of the federal states (TV-L), including an annual special payment and occupational pension scheme
- excellent transport links and the option to purchase a discounted public transport ticket, such as the Deutschlandticket as a commuter pass
- a wide range of food options in the refectories and cafés operated by Studentenwerk Leipzig.

Leipzig University aims to increase the proportion of women in positions of responsibility and therefore expressly invites qualified women to apply. Severely disabled persons – or persons deemed legally equal to them under Book IX of the German Social Code – are encouraged to apply and will be given preference in the case of equal suitability. If you have any questions about accessibility or need assistance with this application process, please contact Leipzig University’s disability officers at: schwerbehindertenvertretung@uni-leipzig.de (https://mailto:schwerbehindertenvertretung@uni-leipzig.de) .

Have we sparked your interest?

Please submit your application in English addressed to Fakultät für Physik und Erdsystemwissenschaften, Herrn Dekan Professor Dr. Johannes Quaas by 1 November 2026 via our online application portal.

Please include the following documents with your application:

- A short letter of motivation (max. 1 page) in which you clearly explain why you would like to work on this project
- A scientific CV (evidence of creative and independent scientific work is an advantage)
- The names and contact information of two people who have agreed to provide academic references
- Academic transcripts clearly listing the courses taken and grades achieved in your entire scientific higher education (bachelor’s as well as master’s or comparable degrees)

Development of novel switchable ultracapacitors and microsupercapacitors for iontronic applications, synthesis of porous carbon materials and porous membranes, development and adaption of new electrolyte formulations, electrochemical characterization, impedance spectroscopy, cyclic voltammetry, integration into a team of PhD and master students, scientific publishing, data management.

jobs.description:
OVERVIEW

Fairtrade is the most recognized and trusted sustainability label, working to make trade fairer for people and planet.

For more than three decades, Fairtrade has been making an impact on the way trade works. We believe that every farmer and worker should have access to a better way of doing business, and a better way of living. 

Fairtrade International is an independent non-profit organisation representing more than two million small-scale farmers and workers worldwide. It owns the FAIRTRADE Mark, a registered trademark that appears on more than 37,000 products. Beyond certification, Fairtrade International and its member organisations (three producer networks and 19 national Fairtrade organisations) partner with producers and businesses, engage consumers, and advocate for a fair and sustainable future.

Unit’s description and purpose: 

The Global Impact unit strengthens the Fairtrade system by driving institutional learning and effectiveness through robust monitoring and evaluation systems. We are the hub for the analysis and communication of high-quality data and information about Fairtrade and its impact, as well as supporting strategy delivery. The unit includes the Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) team, which is the Fairtrade system’s hub for MEL which directly connects evidence to strategic decision for the Global Strategy, individual Fairtrade projects and global programmes, Standards, producer support, and more.

PRINCIPAL ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Overseeing Fairtrade Research and Evaluation: Manages Global Impact commissioned research and evaluations, and supports research and evaluations commissioned by other Fairtrade International units and Fairtrade organizations, ensuring that there are rigorous research methodologies, effective dissemination of findings, practical recommendations, and actionable learnings for the Fairtrade system. Develops and implements procedures and guidelines for the management of research and evaluations within the Fairtrade system.

Amplifying research findings internally and externally: Organizes learning events based on research to ensure learnings are promoted and used by various stakeholder groups within the Fairtrade system. Helps to build appropriate action-plans based on research where learnings are used to promote adaptation, change, and improvement. Presents Fairtrade research findings at external research workshops and conventions and helps to organize and facilitate presentations of others in the Fairtrade system. 

Encouraging a Fairtrade Learning Culture: Develops a Fairtrade Learning Strategy and adapts/maintains Fairtrade Research for Learning Agenda. Ensures that Fairtrade research contributes to understanding Fairtrade’s impact and tests the assumptions in Fairtrade’s Theory of Change. Coordinates research efforts across the Fairtrade system through the Research Task Force. Hosts and guides occasional research-focused interns, students from partner organisations, or student assistants.

Building External Research Collaborations: Builds on an existing academic engagement strategy to engage with external research institutions more deeply to collaboratively fund and perform research on Fairtrade’s impact. Brainstorms with external research teams, contributes to research funding proposals, builds research methodologies, jointly oversees research implementation, and works together to interpret, amplify, and communicate findings.

Managing Digital Learning Platforms: Acts as the product owner for Fairtrade’s Research Hub, a searchable database and platform of external studies exploring Fairtrade’s impact, and Fairlearn, a platform for live and asynchronous Fairtrade e-learning. Contributes to a Steering Committee for an Impact Platform for understanding and learning from Fairtrade’s projects, programmes, and commissioned studies.

Other tasks that are consistent with the level and responsibilities of this post.

SKILLS REQUIRED

Level of education: The position holder will have a Master’s degree (With a research component) or higher (PhD preferred) in development economics, econometrics, applied sociology, social sciences or another relevant field in management or natural sciences. 

Years of professional experience: A minimum of five years’ experience in research and/or impact evaluations, with at least two years’ experience working on topics relevant to, or with, stakeholders from the Global South.

- Project Management
- Research and Evaluation
- International Development Expertise
- Stakeholder Management
- Enhancing data-driven decision making
- eLearning Content
- Event/conferences organization
- Capacity Building

Personal Qualities: 

- Cross-cultural communication
- Facilitation
- Rapid Learning
- Collaboration/Teamwork
- Problem Solving
- Multitasking
- Teaching
- Presentation Skills
- Relationship Management
- Evidence Collecting
- Flexibility
- Mentoring

Software/Tools:

- Microsoft 365 (Excel, Word, Outlook, Powerpoint, Teams, Planner, Clipchamp)
- Adobe Creative Cloud & Suite
- Miro
- Canva
- Claude.ai, or similar AI assistant tools

TERMS AND CONDITIONS

- This is a full-time, maternity cover (apprx. until March 2028) position within Fairtrade International.
- Location is at Fairtrade International offices in Bonn, Germany with the opportunity for hybrid work arrangements
- The office language is English.

jobs.description:
Your role: Laboratory Assistant in Quality Control (m/f/d)

The position is initially limited to 2 years.

In this technically demanding role, you will be largely responsible for the practical implementation and maintenance of our analytical test procedures. Your focus will be on ensuring robust analysis in accordance with international standards directly in the laboratory.

Your Responsibilities:

- Wide-ranging analysis: You will apply chromatographic (HPLC, GC) and wet chemical methods to ensure precise quality control, maintaining data integrity through GMP-compliant documentation and modern laboratory standards (e.g., 5S).
- Pharmacopoeia compliance: You will independently establish and verify analytical methods according to applicable monographs (e.g. EP, USP) and carry out verifications in regulatory revisions.
- Method optimization & CAPA management: You will experimentally investigate and optimize analytical procedures in the context of deviations and CAPA measures to sustainably increase methodological robustness.
- Conducting validation studies: You will carry out method validations and verifications for new products and feedstocks practically on the device and strictly comply with GMP requirements.
- Securing method transfer (APVs): You will develop "best practices" for analytics and record them in supplementary audit regulations (APVs) to ensure consistent application of the methods across the team.

What You Need to Succeed (minimum qualifications):

- Education: You have completed training as a chemical laboratory assistant (m/f/d), CTA (m/f/d) or a comparable qualification and 2+ years relevant professional experience in pharmaceutical quality control.
- Expertise: You have in-depth, field-tested knowledge in instrumental analysis (HPLC, GC, spectroscopy) as well as in the application of international pharmacopoeia (EP, USP).
- Languages: Fluent German and good English skills for working with international pharmacopoeia.

What Will Give You a Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications)

- Methodological competence: Experience in the practical processing of methodological issues in the context of CAPA processes and in the implementation of method validations.
- Way of working: High level of technical understanding of laboratory processes, work reliably in the implementation of complex monographs and passion for working directly in the laboratory.
- IT affinity: Experience with MS Office and chromatography data systems (e.g. Empower) and SAP.

What we offer you – Why Elanco?

- Attractive salary according to the chemical tariff (MTV), full 13th month salary (Christmas bonus) and 40 € holiday pay per day. Plus: employer-financed pension scheme**.**
- Work-life balance: 37.5-hour week and 30 days of vacation. On top of that, there's the "future amount" (up to 5 extra days off or cash), overtime? Are recorded and compensated for by free time**.**
- Well-being: Hansefit membership, annual events (our employee party is legendary!) and preventive care offers directly on site.
- Convenient commute: Subsidy for the job ticket and free parking.
- Benefits: Employee share purchase program and corporate benefits platform.

Additional Information:

- Location: Kiel, Germany - On-site Work Environment
- Travel: 0%
- Position: Limited contract of 2 years.

The foundation Max-Planck-Institut für Kohlenforschung in Mülheim an der Ruhr is a renowned research institution that is over 100 years old and has already received two Nobel Prizes in its history. The institute is engaged in basic research in the field of catalysis with the aim of maximizing the efficient use of natural resources.

As a part of the Cluster of Excellence RESOLV (Ruhr Explores Solvation), the Early Career research group “Catalysis” of Dr. Hanna Hinrika Cramer develops organometallic catalysts with earth-abundant first-row transition metals. The team combines experiments, quantum chemistry, and spectroscopy to study reaction mechanisms and to discover how solvation and catalyst design affect the rate and selectivity. Current projects focus on developing well-defined chromium precatalysts for applications in olefin upgrading and the activation of strong bonds. 

The Cramer group invites applications for a

PhD Student in Organometallic Catalysis 

(full-time, with 39 hours)

- the synthesis and characterization of organometallic complexes
- the development of catalytic applications
- and quantum chemical calculations on electronic structures and reaction mechanisms

- excellent oral and written communication skills in English

Company

Through its Rothe Erde, Uhde and Polysius businesses as well as the majority investment thyssenkrupp nucera, Decarbon Technologies delivers innovative, cutting-edge technologies for the transition to a climate-neutral industrial economy. Rothe Erde is a leading provider of bearings and solutions that play a key role in wind, solar and tidal power plants, among other things. With its solutions for decarbonization, defossilization and the circular economy, Uhde is a technology and implementation provider of large-scale plants for the chemical industry. Polysius supplies green technologies for the cement and lime industry, digital automation solutions, and on-site and remote maintenance services. thyssenkrupp nucera is a global supplier of electrolysis technology for the industrial-scale production of clean hydrogen. The segment employs around 12,000 people, who generated revenues of approximately 3.8 billion euros in fiscal year 2023/2024.

Your responsibilities

- You will actively contribute to the further development and effective implementation of the Compliance Management System within the Decarbon Technologies segment and take ownership of selected compliance areas, including anti-corruption, data compliance, anti-money laundering, and export control/trade compliance. A key focus of your role will be the provision of antitrust and competition law advice as well as the further development and implementation of competition law compliance measures.

- You will monitor and analyze regulatory developments and compliance risks, derive appropriate measures, and support their implementation.

You have a proven track record of not only advising on compliance matters, but also shaping, implementing, and continuously improving compliance programs and governance frameworks.

- You are an effective communicator with strong stakeholder management skills and the ability to build trust and credibility across all levels of the organization.
- You thrive in an international and cross-cultural environment and distinguish yourself through integrity, discretion, resilience, and a high level of personal accountability.

Your benefits

A Snapshot of Your Day 

As a Control Specification Engineer (f/m/d) for Gas Turbine Auxiliaries, you work on open-loop control and protection specifications throughout the entire lifecycle of auxiliary systems, from concept development to commissioning support. You collaborate with engineers, suppliers, instrumentation specialists, and commissioning teams to align technical requirements and ensure seamless system integration. Some days are dedicated to specification development and documentation, while others involve resolving operational challenges, supporting project teams, or addressing site issues. You work in an international environment with colleagues from diverse technical and cultural backgrounds.

How You’ll Make an Impact 

* Responsibility for reference engineering and control specification development for gas turbine fuel systems
* Technical ownership of auxiliary systems, including control, protection, and functional performance aspects
* Coordination and clarification of interfaces with engineering teams, suppliers, commissioning personnel, and other stakeholders
* Creation and maintenance of automation specifications, parameter lists, interface documentation, and related technical documents
* Support for customer-specific engineering requirements and project adaptations
* Back-office support for site activities, troubleshooting, and resolution of technical issues

What You Bring

* Degree in mechanical engineering, process engineering, or a comparable technical field
* Professional experience in control and protection system design with knowledge of relevant engineering disciplines
* Strong analytical mindset and systematic approach to solving technical challenges
* Ability to develop practical and innovative solutions while considering implementation risks
* Strong communication and coordination skills for interdisciplinary collaboration with internal and external stakeholders
* Highly proficient written and spoken English with the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously

Our Gas Services division offers Low-emission power generation through service and 
decarbonization. Zero or low emission power generation and all gas turbines under one roof, 
steam turbines and generators. Decarbonization opportunities through service offerings, 
modernization, and digitalization of the fleet. 

Who is Siemens Energy? 

At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. With ~100.000 dedicated employees in more than 90 countries, we develop the energy systems of the future, ensuring that the growing energy demand of the global community is met reliably and sustainably. Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation.

Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity we generate power. We run on inclusion and our combined creative energy is fueled by over 130 nationalities. This is Worldline.

Worldline helps businesses of all shapes and sizes to accelerate their growth journey - quickly, simply, and securely. And just as we help our customers accelerate their business, we are committed to helping our people accelerate their careers. Together, we shape the evolution.

The Opportunity

We are looking for an Accountant to join our Group Accounting team in a role at the heart of our operations. You will work closely with operational teams, monitor key topics directly linked to business performance and development, and build strong relationships with PMOs and key partners across the organization.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

Working closely with the Finance department and all financial functions of the Group (Order-to-Cash teams, Business Controllers, Consolidation, Finance Management, Treasury, etc.), you will be responsible for the following tasks:

- Perform daily accounting activities: bank operations, purchases, sales, payroll, VAT, and general accounting, including analytical coding of entries.
- Process financial transactions: verification, classification, calculation, accounting and data entry.
- Prepare supplier payment runs according to deadlines (twice per month).
- Monitor and reconcile customer and supplier accounts regularly.
- Work with the FBO teams to ensure timely customer billing.
- Participate in monthly, quarterly and annual closings under IFRS and local GAAP.
- Produce regulatory reporting in accordance with local standards for tax authorities, and possibly central banks and works councils (monthly, quarterly and/or annually).
- Reconcile and justify open balance sheet items and participate in closing and balance sheet review meetings.
- Prepare and file statutory taxes: VAT, Corporate Income Tax, Environmental Taxes and other local taxes.
- Align monthly with the Consolidation team to validate intercompany positions (balance sheet and P&L) and prepare IFRS management reporting for consolidation purposes.
- Collaborate with Finance teams: Finance Business Operations, controlling, consolidation, treasury and other departments.
- Work with fiduciaries and consultants on local and international reporting.
- Manage relationships with external auditors and support internal and tax audits.
- Contribute to the design, maintenance and management of the internal control framework for existing and new activities.
- Continuously improve reporting processes and accounting controls.
- Ensure adherence to internal accounting policies.

Who Are We Looking For

We are seeking individuals capable of driving positive change—people who are proactive, passionate and ready to take initiative. In practice, this means:

- Minimum 3–4 years of experience in general accounting, either in a company or an audit firm.
- Autonomy in managing daily accounting tasks and standard tax declarations (especially VAT).
- Bachelor’s degree required.
- Strong rigor, analytical skills and the ability to structure complex topics.
- Ability to work independently while meeting strict deadlines.
- Capacity to translate business needs for internal stakeholders.
- Proficiency in English (an additional language is a plus).
- Willingness to learn more about accounting, tax and reporting.
- Solid command of Excel and SAP

What we offer

- Growth: The opportunity to progress in a fast-growing environment.
- Culture: Join a team that values proximity and entrepreneurial spirit.

Shape the evolution.

We are pushing towards the next frontiers of payments technology, and we look for big thinkers to join our journey. People with passion, can-do attitude and a hunger to learn and grow. Here you’ll work with ambitious colleagues from around the world, take on unique challenges as a team, and make a real impact on the society. And with our empowering culture, strong technology and extensive training opportunities, we help you accelerate your career. Wherever you decide to go. Join our global team of over 18,000 innovators across 40+ countries, and shape a tomorrow that is yours to own.

jobs.description:
Saarland University is a campus university with a strong international focus and a distinctive research profile characterized by its four core research hubs ‘Computer Science and Informatics’, ‘BioMed’, ‘Europe’ and ‘Sustainability’. With numerous internationally respected research institutes situated in the vicinity of the university and dedicated support for start-up companies, Saarland University is an ideal environment for research, teaching and innovation. The proportion of international students studying at Saarland University is well above the national average and is testimony to the university’s strong international focus. Saarland University has been officially certified as a family-friendly university since 2004.

The Faculty of Human and Business Sciences at Saarland University is inviting applications for the following position to commence in June 2027:

W3 Professorship Computational Social Science (m/f/x; Reference no.: W2906)

The university is also inviting applications for another W2 Professorship (W3 tenure track position) in Political, Social or communication Science (m/f/x; Reference no.: W2905).

This professorial appointment is open regarding the candidate's specific research focus within the field of computational social science. The successful candidate will define their own research agenda, provided that it demonstrates excellence in computational social science, addresses current societal questions, makes use of novel digital data sources and establishes clear links with computer science.

SOUNDS is a research project at Saarland University funded through the Saarland state government’s Transformation Fund. It investigates societally relevant questions through novel digital data sources, digital behavioural traces, social media data and AI-based

methods. This professorship provides the computational social science core of the SOUNDS project. It will combine social-science theory with network analysis, automated text analysis, the study of large-scale digital behavioural data, mobile sensing and AI-based modelling, addressing questions such as collective opinion formation, social cohesion and polarisation, or the role of digital platforms in public communication, and contributing to joint questions, methods and publications with the social sciences and computer science. The successful candidate will be expected to develop and lead externally funded research, including principal investigator roles in coordinated funding initiatives such as Collaborative Research Centres. Teaching duties will include computational and methodological courses, for example on the analysis of digital behavioural data, automated text analysis and network analysis.

These courses will contribute to degree programmes in the social sciences, computer science, data science and psychology. The role also includes the supervision of student theses and the mentoring of early-career researchers. The appointment will be made in accordance with the general provisions of German public sector employment law (see legal recruitment requirements in § 41 Saarländisches Hochschulgesetz, current version available at https://recht.saarland.de/bssl/document/jlr-HSchulGSLrahmen).

We are looking for a researcher with excellent international standing in computational social science and a strong record of working with novel digital data sources applied to societally relevant questions. Your expertise should include computational methods such as network analysis, automated text analysis, the analysis of large-scale digital behavioural data and AIbased modelling. You should be open to a formal affiliation with the Department of Computer Science. You will have an established international research network, an excellent record of high-impact publication and of third-party funding, including grants secured and applications submitted. You should also be prepared to take on principal investigator roles in coordinated funding initiatives such as Collaborative Research Centres. A willingness to teach in English is expected, as is the willingness to teach in German in the medium term.

Saarland University views internationalization as a process spanning all aspects of university life. We therefore expect members of our professorial staff to promote and foster further internationalization. Special support will be provided for projects that expand collaboration within existing international cooperative networks, e.g. projects with partners in the European University Alliance Transform4Europe (www.transform4europe.eu) or the University of the Greater Region (www.uni-gr.eu).

In accordance with the objectives of its gender equality plan, Saarland University is actively seeking to increase the proportion of women in this field. Qualified women candidates are therefore strongly encouraged to apply. Preferential consideration will be given to

applications from disabled candidates of equal eligibility. Furthermore, we welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of nationality, ethnic heritage or social background, religious beliefs, personal beliefs or values, age, sexual orientation or identity.

Please complete the application form in Saarland University's online application portal at www.uni-saarland.de/berufungen and submit it with your application documents by no later than 15 October 2026. Application documents must be uploaded as a single PDF file (max. size 10 MB) and should include the following documents in the order specified:

- Cover letter (addressed to the Dean of the Faculty of Empirical Human Sciences and Economics),
- your résumé detailing your academic career,
- a list of your publications,
- a summary of your research activities and external funding secured to date,
- a list of courses you have taught, sample course evaluations, other evidence of your teaching qualifications,
- a two-page research plan and
- a two-page teaching plan, as well as
- your five most important publications
- Please also include proof of disability if you declared a disability in your application and,
- if you hold a university degree from a foreign university, please provide proof of equivalence from Germany's Central Office for Foreign Education (ZAB) if available. If you have not yet requested proof of equivalence from ZAB, you must submit proof at a later

date if so requested. When you submit a job application to Saarland University, you will be transmitting personal data. Please refer to our privacy notice for information on how we collect and process personal data in accordance with Art. 13 of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) (www.uni-saarland.de/en/privacy). By submitting your application, you confirm that you have taken note of the information in the Saarland University privacy notice.

Ergänzende Informationen:
Anforderungen an den Bewerber: 
Erweiterte Kenntnisse: Qualitative Forschungsmethode, Quantitative Forschungsmethode, Empirische Forschung, Politikwissenschaft, Politologie, Politische Soziologie, Lehrtätigkeit (Hochschule), Soziologie, Datenanalyse

At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Site Microbiologist (Responsible Scientist) (m/w/d)

What tasks await you?

The Site Microbiologists (Responsible Scientist) applies advanced, hands-on GMP microbiology expertise to a range of microbiology topics related to the QC Microbiology Lab, sterile manufacturing areas, and utility systems. Topics include method validation, water systems, environmental monitoring, sterilization/depyrogenation equipment, cleaning validation, audits, and investigations.

Responsibilities / Deliverables:

- Method Validation: Provides expert oversight of method transfers and validations within the QC Microbiology Laboratory in accordance with GMP, USP/Ph. Eur., and Lilly Global Lab Quality Standards. Applies expertise in compendial methods for sterility, bioburden, and endotoxin testing. Demonstrates the ability to further develop knowledge of rapid microbial methods. Understands the analytical instrument validation lifecycle, from user requirements through qualification to instrument release.
- Water Systems: Acts as the microbiological SME for water systems (e.g., WFI, PW, clean steam, and source water). Provides guidance to engineering and sterile manufacturing on water sampling plans during water system qualification and routine monitoring. Interprets water system results from bioburden, endotoxin, and microbiological identity testing, and takes action based on the results to drive system and process improvement.
- **Environmental Monitoring: **Acts as the microbiological SME for environmental monitoring, including viable and non-viable sampling, in Grade A to Grade D areas across manufacturing and QC areas. Provides guidance on implementing environmental monitoring programs in accordance with regulatory requirements. Demonstrates an understanding of the overall contamination control strategy (CCS) for manufacturing and QC areas.
- **Sterilization / Depyrogenation Equipment and Cleaning Validation: **Understands manufacturing equipment and processes such as autoclaves, isolators, dry heat tunnels, and CIP/SIP processes. Has an in-depth understanding of the associated microbiological samples, such as biological indicators, endotoxin indicators, rinse samples, and swab samples. Demonstrates an understanding of testing and interpreting results.
- Audits: Acts as a front-room SME, discussing topics directly with regulatory bodies. Acts as a microbiology SME during audit tours and audit responses.
- Investigations: Leads GMP investigations, including OOS/OOT, deviations, and atypical results, using recognized root cause analysis methodologies such as 5-Why and Ishikawa/Fishbone. Draws sound technical conclusions and recommends corrective and preventive actions.
- **Projects / Workload Projections: **Acts as the QC Microbiology representative for the above-named topics and forecasts QC Microbiology workload.
- Performs technical review, interpretation, and release of raw material, in-process, and finished product data, and contributes to annual product reviews and process validations.
- Provides technical training and mentors analysts through a formal process. Contributes to the development and implementation of Global Lab Quality Standards.

- Education Level: Master’s degree or Bachelor’s degree in a science or engineering-related discipline, with extensive relevant work experience in topics/areas such as QC Laboratories, manufacturing areas, utility systems, environmental monitoring and method validation.
- Experience: 7–10 years of demonstrated relevant experience in a GMP Microbiology Laboratory, sterile manufacturing areas, and utility systems.
- Prior work across the full analytical method lifecycle (development, verification, transfer, validation, and remediation) for microbiological test methods (Bioburden, Endotoxin, Sterility)
- Fluent in English & good German

Additional Skills/ Preferences:

- Demonstrated strong problem-solving skills, with preferred training and proficiency in Root Cause Analysis methodology.
- Demonstrated strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to interact effectively with business partners and auditors.
- Proven ability to focus on continuous improvement.
- Deep understanding of compliance requirements and regulatory expectations, including GMP, USP, Ph. Eur., and EU GMP Annex 1.

Additional Information:

- Ability to travel (approximately 10-20 %)
- On-site presence required

What can you look forward to with us?

- Pioneering spirit: Become part of a team of specialized professionals that will grow to up to 1,000 colleagues over the next three years.

The opportunity

We are seeking an experienced Legal Counsel – Employment & Labor Law (f/m/x) to lead our Social Affairs function across Germany & CEE (Austria, Romania and Czech Republic). Based in Germany, in this strategic role, you will be the architect of our social dialogue for Germany, Austria, Romania and Czech Republic. You will not only provide expert legal advice but also lead direct relationships with Employee Representatives and Works Councils in all four countries. You are responsible for negotiating agreements, ensuring compliance, and fostering a constructive social climate to support the Group’s transformation and growth in the region.

Day-to-day responsibilities

Regional Social Dialogue (DE, AT, RO, CZ)

- Germany (Betriebsrat): Lead negotiations on complex shop agreements (Betriebsvereinbarungen) regarding IT systems, mobile work, and restructuring. Manage co-determinationrights (Mitbestimmung) effectively.
- Austria (Betriebsrat): Lead the relationship with the Austrian Works Council. Navigate the specificities of the Austrian "Social Partnership" and negotiate local shop agreements in compliance with the Arbeitsverfassungsgesetz (ArbVG).
- Romania (Reprezentanții salariaților) and Czech Republic (Odborová organizace): Lead the relationship with the Works Councils.
- Harmonization: Ensure a consistent social strategy across Germany & CEE cluster while respecting local legislative nuances.

Employment Law Advisory

Legal Business Partner: Serve as the primary legal advisor to the HR Country 

- Individual Labor Law: Manage complex individual cases across the region: drafting termination notices, negotiating mutual separation agreements (Aufhebungsverträge / Mutual Termination Agreements), and handling disciplinary measures.
- Contracts: Maintain and update standard employment contract templates for Germany, Austria, Romania and Czech Republic to ensure they remain compliant with the latest local case law.

Restructuring & Strategic Projects

- Transformation Support: Legally structure and execute organizational changes across the region (e.g.,§613a BGB transfers in Germany, AVRAG transfers in Austria).
- Compliance: Roll out Group compliance policies (GDPR, Whistleblowing, Code of Conduct) ensuring they meet the strict data privacy standards of Germany and the specific requirements of the Austrian market.

Litigation Management

- Dispute Resolution: Represent the company in labor court proceedings (Kündigungsschutzklagen) in Germany.
- External Supervision: Select and manage external legal counsel in Austria, Romania and Czech Republic for specific litigation or high-risk cases, ensuring cost control and alignment with Group strategy.

Who are we looking for

Experience & Qualifications

- 8 to 10+ years of experience in Labor Law/Social Affairs, preferably within an international matrix organization, an IT/Consulting firm, or a specialized law firm.
- Works Council Leadership: Mandatory experience leading negotiations with Works Councils.
- You must have deep expertise in the German Betriebsverfassungsgesetz.
- You must have experience or a strong capability to manage Austrian employee representation bodies.
- Regional Scope: Proven ability to manage legal topics across multiple jurisdictions (Germany, Austria, Romania and Czech Republic).

Competencies

- Negotiation Skills: Ability to lead social dialogue in four different legal environments (example: co-determination of Germany).
- Pragmatism: Solution-oriented mindset; you enable business while managing risk.
- Languages: German (Native level) and English (Fluent) are required. French is a plus.

Perks & Benefits

- Regional Responsibility: A key role covering four distinct countries with strategic importance.
- Autonomy: You will be the lead expert for the region Germany, Austria, Romania and Czech Republic, trusted to handle sensitive negotiations with the collaboration of the HR Country Manager.
- Transformation: The opportunity to accompany a high-growth group in structuring its social foundations in the German & CEE market.
